featured.note: What the site leads with. The site renders Ember research generally; this file selects which work is FEATURED and where its numbers come from. Change the featured block to feature different work -- nothing about the site is specific to one issue.

ember.name: Ember
ember.what: Ember is a from-scratch language model trained on one RTX 4090. Everything it knows was learned on that single card. For the #1945 throughput-and-qualification campaign as documented through 2026-09-27, the accounting contract requires receipts for trained-token counts and reproducible checkpoints. This requirement is not evidence that every run met it; no result counts unless a third party can inspect a supporting artifact.
ember.why: The constraint is the experiment. One consumer card is a hard budget, so every question becomes a measurement question -- where the time actually goes, and what would have to change for it to go somewhere else.

featured.title: Training throughput on a single 4090
featured.goal_plain: Make Ember's training step fast enough to apply 80,000 token positions per second on one RTX 4090 -- and prove it twice over: once across at least 1,024 warmed updates, and again across a continuous hour on the frozen production data mixture, without the model learning any worse than it does today.
featured.goal_why: Throughput is the budget for everything else. At today's rate a training run that would answer a research question takes long enough that the question changes first.

acceptance_source.note: The conditions below are TRANSCRIBED from the newest six-gate verdict (attempt 14), which the full acceptance consumer produced. The build refuses if that file's digest no longer matches, so the transcription cannot drift silently. No score is computed here.

conditions.name: Speed, measured over at least 1,024 warmed updates
conditions.plain: At least 1,024 consecutive warmed updates sustaining more than 80,000 applied positions per second, by the tenth-percentile step.
conditions.why: Unmet. The acceptance consumer measured a complete-update p10 of 58,499 over 74,884 updates on attempt 14; the threshold is 80,000.

conditions.name: Speed, sustained for a continuous governed hour
conditions.plain: The same rate held for a full hour on the frozen production data mixture, not just over a burst of updates.
conditions.why: Unmet. The governed hour on attempt 14 ran at 61,740 positions/s including checkpoint write and restore; the threshold is 80,000.

conditions.name: No worse learning
conditions.plain: An equivalence instrument licenses the fast number: whatever made it fast did not change what the model learns.
conditions.why: Met on the current image-inclusive arm: the licence pair passed and the learned function matches.

conditions.name: Protected evaluation minimum
conditions.plain: A protected benchmark suite runs against the checkpoint the qualifying hour produces, and clears its minimum.
conditions.why: Unmet. The protected evaluation on the hour child is below its minimum, and real-image MMMU has not yet separated from the missing- and wrong-image controls.

conditions.name: Frozen production data mixture
conditions.plain: One admitted data identity -- shard ledger, receipt, tokenizer and cursor -- frozen so the hour binds to it and a later reader can reconstruct exactly what was trained on.
conditions.why: Met. The amended image-inclusive mixture identity binds both trained-input digests.

conditions.name: One card, truthful accounting, receipts intact
conditions.plain: Everything runs on the single 4090, every governed run leaves a receipt, and every correction published stays published.
conditions.why: Met. Owned, captured, restored, executor success, receipts intact.

events.because: The frozen criterion reads REFUTED IF the achieved rate on the causal convention comes back BELOW 0.75 of the published 165.2 TF/s. It comes back at 0.388 on the block-causal convention with a 5-matmul backward -- the most generous defensible count, 136 of 256 tiles issued and the recompute charged as work -- and at 0.313 on the least generous. Even the naive square convention returns 0.730, still under the threshold, and that row is self-refuting because it puts the forward at 1.002 of the card's published peak. Every variant the instrument can defend refutes the hypothesis, so this is not a convention artefact. The explanation under test was that the class was unadjudicated for a measurement-convention reason rather than a performance one: the convention hole was real and is now closed, and the conclusion drawn from it was wrong.

events.hypothesis: The refutation does not close the thread, it relocates it. Two things the measurement itself hands over. (1) The backward is 9,479.3 us against a forward of 2,491.1 us, a 3.8x TIME ratio against a 2.0-2.5x FLOP ratio, so the two directions are not equally far from their references and the backward holds most of the 12.0 ms. (2) The trace records the kernel population as fmha_cutlassF/B_bf16_aligned_64x64_..._sm80 -- PyTorch memory-efficient cutlass at Ampere tiles -- which is an observation about WHICH backend ran on an Ada card and not yet a claim that any other backend is available or faster here. The successor asks why the backward specifically sits at 0.35, and it must be measured rather than argued: whether the backend is a choice or the only one this build offers is a source-and-runtime question, not an inference from a rate. Also still open and NOT closed by this refutation: the convention itself, which is now settled and reusable for any later attention measurement on this campaign.

events.because: cycle complete: observed, explained, pre-registered, measured, ruled REFUTED against the frozen criterion, successor named

events.observation: The attention backward is 9,479.3 us per step against a forward of 2,491.1 us. That is a 3.8x TIME ratio against a FLOP ratio of 2.0 (four grad matmuls over two forward matmuls) to 2.5 (five, if the score matrix is recomputed). So the backward is roughly 1.5 to 1.9 times further from its reference than the forward, and it holds 9.5 of the block 12.0 ms. The trace also records the kernel population by name: fmha_cutlassF_bf16_aligned_64x64_rf_sm80 and fmha_cutlassB_bf16_aligned_64x64_k64_seqaligned_sm80, which is the PyTorch memory-efficient cutlass path at Sm80 tiles, running on an Ada sm89 card.

events.hypothesis: Mechanism: the SDPA dispatcher never had the flash backend to choose from. The call site is F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q,k,v,is_causal=True) with no mask and bf16 head_dim 64 -- the signature flash is built for -- so a dispatcher holding flash would normally take it. If the flash kernels are absent from this build or unsupported on this platform, every such call falls through to the memory-efficient cutlass path, whose backward is the least tuned kernel of the pair and whose tiles are compiled for Sm80 rather than the card in the socket. That would produce exactly what is observed: a whole attention population on one cutlass symbol, and a backward further from its reference than its own forward.

events.refuted_if: torch on this host reports the FLASH backend as BUILT and SELECTABLE for exactly this call signature -- bf16, head_dim 64, is_causal true, no attn_mask, the strides _document_sdpa actually produces -- because then the dispatcher did hold flash and declined it, and absence cannot be the mechanism. A partial result also refutes: flash built but rejected for a reason OTHER than platform support, such as stride or alignment, refutes the availability explanation and names a different one.
events.supported_if: torch reports the flash backend unavailable for this signature on this build or platform, so the memory-efficient cutlass path was the only one the dispatcher could reach
events.instrument: seat record: sdpa_backend_availability.py

events.note: SDPA backend availability probe, three small bf16 tensors + one call, under 2 minutes

events.because: The frozen criterion refutes only if flash is BUILT and SELECTABLE, or built and rejected for a non-platform reason. torch states in its own words: Torch was not compiled with flash attention (sdp_utils.cpp:771, from can_use_flash_attention). is_flash_attention_available() is false and USE_FLASH_ATTENTION does not appear in torch.__config__.show() for 2.10.0+cu126. Both refuting branches require flash to be present and neither obtains, so the dispatcher never had it to choose from and the memory-efficient cutlass path was the only one reachable -- which is what the census sees: one symbol, every call, forward and backward. Tested against tensors built the way _document_sdpa builds them, stride 1048576/64/1024/1 and non-contiguous, because stride eligibility is one of the things flash checks. Note for the successor rather than for this verdict: flash_sdp_enabled() returns TRUE while the kernels are absent, so that flag reports the preference and not the capability.

events.hypothesis: SUPPORTED, and the support hands over a sharper question than the one asked. can_use_cudnn_attention returns TRUE for this exact signature and cudnn_sdp_enabled() is true, yet the dispatcher still took the cutlass memory-efficient path -- one symbol, every call. Priority order, a later runtime check, or the cutlass path genuinely winning selection are all consistent with what was observed and the probe cannot distinguish them. That is measurable and it is cheaper to measure than to argue. What this does NOT license: it does not say a flash-enabled build or the cudnn backend would be faster at this geometry. Nothing was compared and nothing was timed, and asserting a saving would be a claim about what a change collects. It also does not make swapping the torch build a treatment -- the build is part of the declared execution environment every governed receipt binds to, so changing it carries its own equivalence question rather than being a kernel swap.

events.because: cycle complete: observed, explained, pre-registered, measured on the card through the window gate, ruled SUPPORTED, successor named

events.observation: torch reports can_use_cudnn_attention TRUE for the exact signature the decoder issues, and cudnn_sdp_enabled() is also true, yet a one-call profile shows the dispatcher selecting fmha_cutlassF_bf16_aligned_64x64_rf_sm80 -- the memory-efficient cutlass symbol -- and the full census shows that same symbol on every one of the 24 forward and 24 backward calls per step. An eligible backend that is never reached is either lower in the priority order or failing a check that eligibility does not cover.

events.hypothesis: Mechanism: backend PRIORITY, not capability. With flash absent from the build, the dispatcher walks its remaining preference list, and if EFFICIENT_ATTENTION sits ahead of CUDNN_ATTENTION for this device then cudnn is never consulted no matter what its eligibility check would have said. can_use_cudnn_attention answers a question the dispatcher never asks in this configuration, which is why the two disagree.

events.refuted_if: with sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.CUDNN_ATTENTION) forced for the identical call, the dispatch still lands on a cutlass memory-efficient symbol, or raises -- because then cudnn is not actually reachable for this signature, the eligibility report was not actionable, and ORDERING is not the mechanism
events.supported_if: forcing CUDNN_ATTENTION dispatches to a distinct cudnn attention kernel on the identical inputs, showing the backend is reachable and was passed over by ordering alone
events.instrument: seat record: sdpa_backend_forced_dispatch.py

events.note: forced-backend dispatch probe: three small bf16 tensors, four calls, under 2 minutes

events.because: Frozen criterion: REFUTED IF with sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.CUDNN_ATTENTION) forced for the identical call, the dispatch still lands on a cutlass memory-efficient symbol, or raises. Neither obtained: forced CUDNN dispatched cudnn_generated_fort_native_sdpa_sm80_flash_fprop_wmma_f16_knob_6_128x64x64_4x1x1_kernel0_0 plus a device memset, distinct from the unforced cutlass symbol, with no raise and no cutlass fallback. Forced FLASH raised RuntimeError No available kernel. So cudnn IS reachable for this signature and the dispatcher does not go there. The MECHANISM I named is refuted by the same run: sdp_utils.cpp:680 cuDNN attention has been runtime disabled fired during the UNFORCED call, so it was considered and refused by a runtime disable, not skipped by priority ordering.

events.hypothesis: WHAT THE REFUTATION DID NOT CLOSE. The runtime disable is not explained: this says nothing about WHY cudnn attention is disabled in this build (platform guard, version guard, or a defaults choice), nor whether it can be enabled at all outside a forced context manager. Nothing was timed, so cudnn-vs-cutlass speed at this geometry is entirely open. WHAT ARITHMETIC NOW CLOSES, and it closes the whole attention thread as an ARM. The attention block is 11,970.5 us of a 175,190 us governed step = 6.83 percent. Driving attention to ZERO gives 1.073x. The standing bar (1945-multiplicative-movement-only clause 1) refuses any arm whose pre-stated ceiling is below 1.5x, so NO attention treatment -- cudnn dispatch, flash rebuild, tiling -- can be dispatched as an arm on this campaign. That is a route ruling from measurement, not an exit ruling on the target. The attention adjudication was still worth its cost: it removed a 12 ms block from the candidate set by measurement rather than by assumption. SUCCESSOR, chosen by SHARE of the remaining factor rather than by authoring cost. The elementwise class is 27,862.9 us -- 15.9 percent of the step, the largest non-GEMM block measured, and the biggest single lever on the table. The census scored it at 1.151 of published DRAM bandwidth. A rate ABOVE the card's published DRAM rate is impossible for genuinely DRAM-resident traffic, exactly as the square-convention attention row was impossible at 1.002 of peak. So one of two things is true and they have opposite consequences: either the bytes are largely cache-resident, in which case DRAM is the wrong roofline and the block has real unmeasured distance against an L2 roofline; or the byte figure derived from recorded input dims is wrong, in which case every bandwidth number in the census inherits the error. Either answer is load-bearing and the discriminator reads a trace already on disk.

events.because: SUPPORTED against the frozen criterion, mechanism inside the explanation refuted by the same run, receipt landed at seat record: sdpa-forced-dispatch-20260914.md, successor seeded. Attention thread closed as an ARM by arithmetic (6.83 percent of step, 1.073x ceiling, below the 1.5x bar) -- not as a question.

events.observation: The non-GEMM bandwidth census records 5.18 ms per step of pure aten::copy_ inside the elementwise class -- kernels that move bytes and compute nothing. Its own not_closed line (a) says the BYTE-REDUCTION direction is untouched and unsized, and that this is where the ~40.6 ms of bandwidth-bound work lives. events.hypothesis: THE MECHANISM, not a restatement of the observation: fused AdamW is a pure streaming update with essentially no arithmetic. Per trainable parameter it READS the parameter, the gradient, exp_avg and exp_avg_sq, and WRITES the parameter, exp_avg and exp_avg_sq -- seven tensor traversals of the trainable set per optimizer step, and about a dozen scalar operations per element. IF that block is running at or near what this card can actually stream, then its 16.8 ms is SET BY THE BYTE COUNT of the optimizer state, and the only lever on it is fewer bytes: lower-precision moments, a state layout with fewer traversals, or fusing the update into the backward so parameters and gradients are touched once instead of twice. IF it is running far below what the card can stream, then the byte count is NOT what sets the time and the cost is somewhere else entirely -- launch structure over 21.3 calls, tail effects on a multi_tensor chunking, or occupancy -- and every byte-reduction treatment is aimed at the wrong quantity. The two readings prescribe opposite treatments, which is why this is worth measuring before anything is proposed. The bytes cannot come from the trace: the profiler records the TensorList dims of _fused_adamw_ as empty, so the inventory has to come from the parameter and optimizer state on disk at the measured head.

events.refuted_if: The optimizer block achieved bandwidth -- computed as the AdamW read/write byte set over the TRAINABLE parameter inventory at the measured head, divided by the measured 16,817.8 us per step -- comes out BELOW 50 percent of the 1008 GB/s published DRAM rate. That refutes the bandwidth-bound reading: the block would then not be limited by its own byte count, every byte-reduction treatment would be aimed at the wrong quantity, and the cost would have to be attributed to launch structure, chunking or occupancy instead. SUPPORTED IF at or above 50 percent: the block is bandwidth-bound at its own byte count, fewer bytes is the only lever on it, and the inventory names which state tensors carry them. THE 1008 GB/s FIGURE IS A PUBLISHED SPECIFICATION USED TO EXPRESS A FRACTION, never a measured ceiling and never an impossibility premise -- the same census already recorded three classes reporting ABOVE it on L2 residency, so a result above 100 percent is a finding about residency and not a contradiction. The byte count will be a LOWER BOUND (each tensor in the read/write set counted once, no cache reuse modelled), so the computed rate is at or BELOW the true one, which is conservative for the refutation direction and must be stated as such in the ruling.

events.because:
REFUTED against the frozen criterion, which reads: "The optimizer block achieved bandwidth -- computed as the AdamW read/write byte set over the TRAINABLE parameter inventory at the measured head, divided by the measured 16,817.8 us per step -- comes out BELOW 50 percent of the 1008 GB/s published DRAM rate." It comes out at 39.15 percent (394.6 GB/s), and at 29.80 percent at the other end of the bracket below, so it is refuted across every population the traced steps could have stepped.

THE BYTE MODEL IS CHECKED AGAINST THE COMPILED KERNEL RATHER THAN ASSERTED. The measured symbol is multi_tensor_apply_kernel<FusedOptimizerTensorListMetadata<4>, FusedAdamMathFunctor<BFloat16, 4, ADAM_MODE 1, false>>, and the instrument REFUSES if any of ILi4EE (FOUR tensor lists: param, grad, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq and nothing else), BFloat16, ADAM_MODE 1 (decoupled weight decay) or Lb0 (amsgrad false) is absent. So seven traversals at 2 bytes = 14 bytes per stepped element is the compiled fact, not my reasoning about AdamW. The checkpoint corroborates it: master_weights is None, params are bfloat16 across all 26 objects, and exp_avg/exp_avg_sq are bfloat16 across all 351 state entries.

THE VERDICT TURNED ON WHICH POPULATION THE KERNEL WALKS, AND THE CONVENIENT ANSWER WOULD HAVE RULED THE OTHER WAY. Three candidates: 474,030,080 elements that actually carry AdamW state (39.15 percent), 701,964,288 declared trainable by the runner model receipt (57.97 percent, which is SUPPORTED), and 3,082,539,008 in the whole optimizer param_group (254.57 percent). The criterion says "the TRAINABLE parameter inventory", which literally points at the declared figure -- the one from the easiest source that yields the more interesting result. It was not taken.

THE DISCRIMINATOR COMES FROM THE TRACE, NOT FROM A DECLARATION. multi_tensor_apply walks the tensor list accumulating 64 Ki-element chunks and launches whenever it reaches 36 tensors or 320 chunks (MultiTensorApply.cuh, depth 4). Simulating that greedy walk predicts the launch count each population would produce, and the trace MEASURED that count at 21.3 per step: the stepped set predicts 23 (error 1.7), the declared set 34 (error 12.7), the param_group 148. And the 1.7 residual is explained rather than waved at -- routing is data-dependent and the capture is 6 steps against an hour of updates, so core-only predicts 13, core+expert0 predicts 18, core+experts0and1 predicts 23, and the measured 21.3 sits between the last two. That brackets the traced population at 360,783,872 to 474,030,080 elements and the achieved bandwidth at 29.80 to 39.15 percent.

WHAT THE REFUTATION LICENSES: nothing byte-shaped. At 394.6 GB/s roughly 60 percent of the card streaming capacity is unused during the block, so lower-precision moments, a fewer-traversal state layout, and fusing the update into the backward are all aimed at a quantity that is not the constraint. The moments are ALREADY bf16, which is part of the answer: the obvious byte lever had been pulled before the block was ever examined.

WHAT IT DOES NOT LICENSE: the reverse claim. Not-bandwidth-bound is not launch-bound. Three candidates survive and this instrument discriminates none of them.

THE ONE ASSUMED TERM CUTS AGAINST THE RULING AND IS STATED FOR THAT REASON. A gradient is not stored in a checkpoint, so its dtype is taken equal to the parameter dtype. Were gradients fp32 the count would be 18 bytes per element instead of 14 and the stepped population would land at 50.3 percent -- at the boundary. The single BFloat16 functor instantiation in the measured symbol is the evidence against that, since a mixed-precision variant instantiates differently, but no artifact states the gradient dtype outright. Separately, no cache reuse is modelled, so the byte count is a LOWER BOUND and the true rate is at or above the computed one -- which is the direction that would weaken this refutation, and is why the 50 percent bar is cleared by 11 points rather than by one.

events.hypothesis:
WHAT THE REFUTATION DOES NOT CLOSE, named while the reasoning is fresh rather than later under pressure to reopen a route.
(a) IT NAMES NO MECHANISM. Three survive: launch structure across 21.3 launches per step; the chunk tail, since 351 tensors of very unequal size are packed into fixed 36-tensor / 320-chunk batches and the last batch of each launch is partial; and occupancy, for which this trace carries no counter at all. Discriminating them is the next cycle.
(b) A BYTE-REDUCTION TREATMENT IS REFUSED AT THIS GEOMETRY AND THIS POPULATION ONLY. If the stepped population grew by an order of magnitude -- more experts receiving gradients, a wider trainable set -- the same block would move toward the streaming regime and the byte lever would come back. This row does not close the byte route for a different configuration.
(c) IT MEASURES NO BYTES. Every figure is derived from an inventory, not read from a device-memory traffic counter. The governed-run evidence contract requires measured traffic reported separately from estimated traffic, and no measured traffic exists for this trace.
(d) THE GRADIENT DTYPE IS UNSTATED BY ANY ARTIFACT. If it is fp32 the ruling sits at the boundary rather than clear of it. Reading it off a live step would settle it cheaply.
(e) IT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT WHETHER THE OPTIMIZER CAN BE OVERLAPPED. The factor-table row-3 proposal -- per-layer optimizer on a second stream as backward finishes each layer -- is a concurrency treatment, not a byte treatment, and this refutation neither supports nor weakens it. Cycle 8 restated composition already carries that 16.8 ms on the overlappable side under an assumption it explicitly flagged as the strongest in the construction.
(f) 844 OF THE 1,195 PARAMETERS IN THE OPTIMIZER param_group HAVE NEVER TAKEN A STEP at this head -- audio, image, all 14 router tensors, and experts 2 through 24, including two of the four experts the counter receipt lists as ACTIVE. Reported because it is what SIZES the population and therefore decides this verdict. It is NOT a ruling that anything is misconfigured and this artifact did not investigate it; whether the router and the remaining active experts are meant to be receiving gradients at this head is a separate question.
(g) ONE TRACE, ONE GEOMETRY, ONE CHECKPOINT, under profiling instrumentation, with no matched-run variation.

events.observation: The optimizer block spends 16,817.8 us per step moving at most 6.64 GB, which is 39.15 percent of what the card publishes -- so roughly 60 percent of the streaming capacity is idle during a kernel that does nothing but stream. The shape of the work is unusual and the numbers are all measured: 21.3 multi_tensor_apply launches per step, 351 tensors of very unequal size (from 1,024 elements at final_norm to 33,554,432 at the embedding), packed by multi_tensor_apply into batches capped at 36 tensors or 320 chunks of 64 Ki elements. That packing means the final batch of every launch is partial, and it means a 1,024-element tensor consumes a whole tensor slot in the metadata while contributing one chunk. 15,847.4 of the 16,817.8 us is the fused AdamW symbol itself; the remaining 970 us is _foreach_zero_ and _foreach_add_.

events.hypothesis:
THE MECHANISM, and the three candidates it separates. multi_tensor_apply assigns one thread block per 64 Ki-element chunk and launches when either the 36-tensor metadata cap or the 320-block cap is hit. Whichever cap binds decides the shape of the inefficiency, and they predict different things.
(1) TENSOR-CAP BOUND. If launches are ending on the 36-tensor cap rather than the 320-chunk cap, the kernel is issuing far fewer than 320 blocks per launch and the card is underfilled by construction -- a grid too small to saturate, repeated 21 times. The stepped set is 351 tensors and 7,233 chunks, so an even packing would give 23 launches at ~315 blocks each and the tensor cap would bind on 9.75 launches; the two caps are close enough here that which one binds is a per-launch question, not a global one, and it can be read from the trace by joining each launch to its grid dimensions.
(2) CHUNK-TAIL BOUND. Every launch has a partial final chunk per tensor, and a 1,024-element tensor still costs a full block. With tensor sizes spanning four orders of magnitude the wasted fraction of each block could be large, and it would show as a grid that is nominally full while most threads exit immediately.
(3) OCCUPANCY BOUND. FusedAdamMathFunctor holds four tensor-list pointers plus the running moments in registers; if register pressure caps resident warps the SMs cannot cover DRAM latency regardless of grid size, and no amount of repacking helps.
These prescribe different treatments -- (1) and (2) are fixed by repacking or by a single flattened update over a contiguous state buffer, which is a layout change with no byte saving; (3) is fixed by a different kernel or not at all. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE PER-LAUNCH GRID GEOMETRY, which the trace already carries: each kernel event records its grid and block dimensions. Joining the 21.3 launches to their grids says immediately whether the launches are ending on the tensor cap (small grids) or the chunk cap (grids at or near 320 blocks).

events.refuted_if: The per-launch grid geometry of the 21.3 multi_tensor_apply launches, read from the trace kernel events, shows a MEDIAN grid of AT LEAST 288 blocks -- 90 percent of the 320-block cap. That refutes the tensor-cap reading: the launches would then be ending on the chunk cap with nearly full grids, the card would not be underfilled by the packing, and repacking the tensor list could not be the lever. SUPPORTED IF the median grid is BELOW 288 blocks: the launches are ending on the 36-tensor metadata cap before they fill their block budget, the grid is smaller than the kernel could issue, and a repack or a flattened contiguous update is a real lever on a block this measurement has already shown is not byte-limited. THE 288 FIGURE IS 90 PERCENT OF A SOURCE CONSTANT (depth_to_max_blocks[3] = 320 in MultiTensorApply.cuh), not a hardware limit and not a performance target. THE MECHANISM, and the three candidates it separates. multi_tensor_apply assigns one thread block per 64 Ki-element chunk and launches when either the 36-tensor metadata cap or the 320-block cap is hit. Whichever cap binds decides the shape of the inefficiency, and they predict different things.
(1) TENSOR-CAP BOUND. If launches are ending on the 36-tensor cap rather than the 320-chunk cap, the kernel is issuing far fewer than 320 blocks per launch and the card is underfilled by construction -- a grid too small to saturate, repeated 21 times. The stepped set is 351 tensors and 7,233 chunks, so an even packing would give 23 launches at ~315 blocks each and the tensor cap would bind on 9.75 launches; the two caps are close enough here that which one binds is a per-launch question, not a global one, and it can be read from the trace by joining each launch to its grid dimensions.
(2) CHUNK-TAIL BOUND. Every launch has a partial final chunk per tensor, and a 1,024-element tensor still costs a full block. With tensor sizes spanning four orders of magnitude the wasted fraction of each block could be large, and it would show as a grid that is nominally full while most threads exit immediately.
(3) OCCUPANCY BOUND. FusedAdamMathFunctor holds four tensor-list pointers plus the running moments in registers; if register pressure caps resident warps the SMs cannot cover DRAM latency regardless of grid size, and no amount of repacking helps.

events.observation:
Cycle 9 refuted the bandwidth reading of the 16,817.8 us optimizer block; cycle 10 refuted the tensor-cap reading (122 of 122 interior launches at the 320-block cap, zero on the 36-tensor cap) and the chunk-tail reading (1.48 percent of dispatched thread slots idle). One candidate survives: occupancy. Cycle 10 also produced the mechanism behind it -- the launch is REGISTER-LIMITED to 2 resident blocks per SM (64 registers per thread, 512-thread blocks, 32,768 registers per block against the device 65,536 per SM), giving 1,024 of 1,536 resident threads = 66.7 percent theoretical occupancy, which the trace own estimate reports as 67 percent.

THE OBSERVATION THAT MAKES THIS TESTABLE WITHOUT A NEW RUN: the SAME trace contains other multi_tensor_apply launches from the same launcher at the same 320-block grid and the same 512-thread block, at DIFFERENT occupancy. aten::_foreach_zero_ runs 21.3 launches per step of ZeroFunctor<BFloat16> at 26 registers per thread and an 83 percent estimated occupancy, and aten::_foreach_add_ runs 4 launches per step of BinaryOpScalarFunctor<float>. So the trace carries its own occupancy-varying control population for the identical launch structure on the identical tensor list.

events.hypothesis:
IF occupancy explains the fused-AdamW shortfall, then within this trace the achieved bandwidth of these kernel classes should track their occupancy: a class at 83 percent should reach roughly 83/67 = 1.24 times the bandwidth of the class at 67 percent, all else equal. If instead the higher-occupancy class reaches far MORE than that, occupancy cannot be the explanation and the residual belongs to the kernel own instruction mix, memory access pattern, or latency structure -- which would refute candidate (3) as stated and leave the block with no surviving mechanism from the original three, forcing a wider hypothesis.

THE CONFOUND, NAMED BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN AFTER. _foreach_zero_ is a PURE STORE at 2 bytes per element; fused AdamW reads four tensors and writes three at 14 bytes per element. Stores can retire fire-and-forget while loads must be waited on, so a pure-store kernel hides latency better REGARDLESS of occupancy. That confound is the reason _foreach_add_ (read + write, float) is included as a second reference despite its tiny sample, and the reason the criterion below uses a 25 percent tolerance band rather than demanding exact proportionality. If the confound dominates, the ruling must say the comparison did not discriminate rather than claim a verdict.

FULL DISCLOSURE, BECAUSE A CRITERION CHOSEN AFTER THE NUMBERS ARE IN IS CHOSEN TO FIT THEM. A back-of-envelope sketch is already possible from figures published in seat record: captured-optimizer-bandwidth-20260914T183257Z.json: _foreach_zero_ at 963.9 us per step over the same population at 2 bytes per element is on the order of 900 GB/s, roughly 2.5 times the fused-AdamW figure. That sketch points at REFUTED. It is disclosed here, before the criterion, with the bar set at a level chosen for its MEANING (a 25 percent tolerance around the occupancy ratio) rather than to be barely cleared by the sketch. The instrument will compute both classes per-launch from each launch own grid and duration, which the sketch cannot do, and the ruling stands on that.

events.refuted_if:
REFUTED IF the ratio of achieved bandwidth (the higher-occupancy multi_tensor_apply class to the fused-AdamW class), each computed PER LAUNCH from that launch own grid and duration and then aggregated, EXCEEDS 1.55 -- that is, exceeds the 83:67 = 1.24 occupancy ratio by more than 25 percent. Then occupancy cannot account for the gap: the card demonstrably streams far faster than 1.24 times the AdamW rate during this same block, so the shortfall belongs to the kernel own instruction mix, access pattern or latency structure rather than to how many warps are resident, and candidate (3) as stated is refuted along with (1) and (2).

SUPPORTED IF the bandwidth ratio is AT OR BELOW 1.55, within 25 percent of the occupancy ratio: occupancy is a sufficient explanation of the difference between these classes and raising it -- fewer registers per thread, a smaller block, or a different functor -- is a real lever on a block already shown to be neither byte-limited nor cap-limited.

THE 1.55 FIGURE IS 1.25 x (83/67), both inputs read from the trace own est. achieved occupancy field. It is not a hardware limit and not a performance target.

INCONCLUSIVE IS THE CORRECT VERDICT, NOT A FALLBACK, IF the pure-store confound cannot be separated -- specifically if _foreach_add_ (read + write) disagrees in DIRECTION with _foreach_zero_ (pure store), or if its 4 launches per step are too few to distinguish its rate from noise at the sample size available. events.hypothesis:
MECHANISM. Published DRAM bandwidth is a peak figure under ideal access. Real kernels lose to access granularity, read/write turnaround on the memory bus, ECC-free but imperfect row-buffer locality, and -- under CUPTI instrumentation -- whatever serialization the profiler imposes. A host that demonstrates 472 GB/s on its best-observed read+write stream has an EMPIRICAL envelope, and every achieved-rate claim on this campaign should be read against that envelope rather than against the spec.

WHAT MAKES THIS TESTABLE RATHER THAN RHETORICAL. The trace contains 138 distinct kernel symbols inside the measured-step windows. A subset of them have element counts derivable purely from launch geometry and byte models derivable purely from their functor signature -- the vectorized_elementwise family encodes vec_size and operand count in the symbol itself. Computing achieved bandwidth across every qualifying shape whose traffic exceeds twice the 72 MB L2 gives an empirical envelope built from this trace, on this host, under this instrumentation, with no spec figure anywhere in it.

WHY THIS OUTRANKS RE-ATTACKING OCCUPANCY. The operator directive is that the next event worth reporting is a source-bound measurement showing a LARGE MULTIPLICATIVE movement. Occupancy, if confirmed, is worth at most the 1.49x the occupancy ratio allows on a 16.8 ms block -- about 5 ms of a 175 ms step, under 3 percent. The denominator question is worth more than any of that, because it decides whether the optimizer block is a 2.6x opportunity or a 1.22x one, and therefore whether ANY optimizer treatment belongs on the critical path at all. An answer of "the block is near the machine demonstrated envelope" redirects the campaign to the levers that change how many optimizer steps happen rather than how fast one is -- which is the contract lever, the operator decision that ten cycles have now backed.

events.hypothesis:
MECHANISM. A CUDA kernel launched on stream A and one on stream B execute concurrently if the device has SMs for both. Bandwidth-bound kernels do not partition the memory system; they contend for it. Two concurrent 400 GB/s-capable kernels do not each get 400 -- they split what the controller delivers, and each one duration grows accordingly. So a per-launch rate computed from a stretched duration is an UNDERSTATEMENT of that kernel isolated capability, and the error is proportional to how much of its life it spent sharing.

WHY THIS OUTRANKS EXTENDING THE ENVELOPE. Cycle 12 owed a successor that lowers its floor and admits the back-referenced symbols, and that successor is real work. But it is work that produces MORE per-launch rates by the same method. If the method is invalid, a third and fourth data point make the wrong answer more confident. A precondition that would invalidate four cycles of arithmetic is worth more than a fifth application of it -- and it is cheaper, because every input is already on disk and the computation is an interval union.

WHAT MAKES IT TESTABLE RATHER THAN RHETORICAL. For each kernel of the measured classes inside the six step windows, compute how much of its own duration is covered by the wall-time interval of ANY other device event -- kernel or memcpy -- in the same trace. Summed over the class and divided by the class summed duration, that is the fraction of measured device time that was shared. It is a single number per class, derived from ts and dur alone, with no byte model and no element count in it.

events.observation: THE HALF OF THE SELECTED ROUTE THAT SURVIVED THIS HOUR IS BUILT ON A 60.2 ms FIGURE WHOSE MECHANISMS ARE ALREADY INDIVIDUALLY REFUTED IN MY OWN REGISTRY, AND I QUOTED IT ANYWAY. Cycle 17 refuted the 2x premise under the FP8 half, which leaves the non-GEMM half as the whole route: 32.7 ms of device idle plus 27.5 ms of elementwise, composed as one 60.2 ms lever worth 1.58x. Querying the registry in that composition own vocabulary -- idle, graph, capture, eager, elementwise, consolidation, launch, adjacency -- returns three rows that bound its parts, and the first query I ran (device idle removable collectible gap between kernels) returned NOTHING, so the widen clause of a-not-closed-line-is-a-claim-about-the-past is what surfaced them. (1) gap-removal-scheduling-bound [REFUTED]: perfect removal of every outside-union interval with the kernel union held fixed is 190,031.6 / 150,052.5 = 1.266x, below the bar. That is the idle term. (2) nongemm-launch-consolidation-bound-is-3.9ms-not-55ms-20260914 [REFUTED]: the whole non-GEMM launch-overhead REMOVAL bound is 3.88 ms, not the ~55 ms the factor-dominant table row 1 assigned it. (3) elementwise-class-is-bandwidth-bound-not-launch-bound-20260914 [REFUTED]: the elementwise launch ceiling alone is 2.65 ms, because the class is bandwidth-bound rather than launch-bound. So "consolidate the elementwise class" collects single-digit milliseconds, not 27.5, and "remove the idle" is separately bounded at 1.266x -- and gap-removal own not_closed line warns in as many words that the gap and eager terms are VERY LIKELY THE SAME MECHANISM COUNTED TWICE. The 60.2 ms composition adds them as if they were independent, which is precisely what clause 4 of treatment-selection-states-its-ceiling forbids. WHAT THE SAME THREE ROWS LEAVE OPEN, IN THEIR OWN WORDS, IS ONE MECHANISM: BYTE REDUCTION. "The BYTE-REDUCTION direction is entirely open and is where the 25.2 ms lives: fusion that keeps intermediates in registers, and elimination of the 5.18 ms of pure aten::copy_. Nothing here refutes it and nothing here sizes it." The sibling row puts the same opening at ~40.6 ms across the whole non-GEMM path. Beside it, two narrower openings: consolidation as an ENABLER of concurrency by reducing dependency edges (named not_closed in both rows, never measured), and L2 residency, unmeasured, with three classes reporting above the published DRAM rate on a ~25 MB working set in a 72 MB L2. THE QUESTION THIS CYCLE MUST ANSWER IS THEREFORE NOT "IS THE NON-GEMM HALF WORTH 1.58x" -- it is "how much of the 25.2 ms of elementwise time is actually BYTES THAT A FUSION WOULD NOT MOVE", which is the only term in the composition that no row has bounded. Nothing is claimed here: this is the observation, and the mechanism and the criterion are the next two stages.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM, STATED BEFORE ANY ARITHMETIC. Device idle and device kernel time are disjoint intervals, so adding 32.7 ms of idle to 27.5 ms of elementwise is not double-counting in the TIMELINE sense, and that is exactly why the composition looked safe. The double count, if it exists, is in the MECHANISMS. A treatment that consolidates or fuses elementwise kernels does not only delete their device time: it deletes the per-launch dispatch holes those kernels created. So a hole sitting between two elementwise kernels is a hole the elementwise treatment plausibly collects BY ITSELF, and crediting it a second time to a separate "remove the idle" treatment counts one act twice. A hole sitting between two GEMM kernels is out of that treatment reach and is genuinely the idle term own. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THEREFORE THE CLASS ON EACH SIDE OF EACH HOLE, and it is computable from a capture already on disk: walk the device-time union per measured step window, and for every interior hole record the class of the kernel that ends on its left and the class of the kernel that starts on its right, using the same class table the millisecond figures come from. WHY THIS DECIDES SOMETHING. Perfect collection of the whole 60.2 ms is 1.58x, which clears the 1.5x arm bar by 0.08. Every part of that composition is separately refuted already -- idle removal alone at 1.266x, non-GEMM launch removal at 3.88 ms, the elementwise launch ceiling at 2.65 ms -- so the composition is the ONLY thing holding the route above the bar, and it holds only if the two terms are independent. If they are not, no non-GEMM composition with a defensible ceiling above the bar currently exists, and the honest consequence is that the route set is empty pending a measured byte-reduction bound rather than that some smaller arm is next. THE ASYMMETRY IS DELIBERATE AND IS NOT A LOOPHOLE: adjacency is NECESSARY for the same-mechanism reading and not SUFFICIENT, because a hole between two elementwise kernels may be a dependency stall or a memory-system wait that survives any consolidation. So a large treatable-adjacent share WITHDRAWS SUPPORT from the independence premise rather than proving the terms identical, and a small share would positively support it. The composition needs the premise supported; it is not enough for it to be merely unrefuted.

events.refuted_if: MORE THAN 50% of interior device idle, measured per step window across the capture, touches a kernel of the non-GEMM TREATABLE set on at least one side. Treatable set, fixed here and not after the numbers: elementwise, triton_fused, cat_copy, index_scatter_gather, softmax, reduce, memcpy, optimizer, loss, sort. It is deliberately WIDE because the route own framing is "the whole non-GEMM side", and a wide set makes the share LARGER -- so the choice works against the composition I am testing, and a narrower reading would make my own refutation weaker rather than stronger. (b) WEIGHT: the time-weighted expected contraction speedup over the measured subset is more than 5 percent relative BELOW the arm s best measured figure -- meaning the better of the two measurements came from a geometry carrying too little time to represent the rest, and quoting it would overstate the route. WHAT REFUTED MEANS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It refutes the REPRESENTATIVENESS of the arm s geometry set, nothing else. It does not refute FP8, it does not refute precision as a route, and it makes no claim about what FP8 achieves at any geometry the arm did not run -- the instrument refuses to produce such a claim by construction. It bounds the ROUTE and not the exit; impossibility is the operator s to rule from receipts.
hypotheses.criterion_supported_if: The measured geometries carry at least 80 percent of the mm device time AND the time-weighted expectation sits within 5 percent of the best measured figure -- in which case the arm s sample does stand for the population and cycle 17 s figures may be carried into a route price directly. --- INCONCLUSIVE BRANCHES: (a) the instrument returns any refusal token, which is reported rather than worked around; (b) the re-run efficiency census disagrees with the class table s gemm classes for the same trace by more than 1 percent, which would mean the two consumers partition the same trace differently and the join is not sound. --- DISCLOSED BEFORE THE RULING, AS CYCLES 17 AND 19 DID: the instrument s deliberate-red battery includes a GREEN case over the real population and the real measured ratios, so I have already seen the answer -- coverage 0.5750 and a time-weighted 1.0672x against a best measured 1.2196x -- and I expect REFUTED on BOTH legs. This is therefore an APPLICATION of a discriminator, not a discovery, and what keeps it evidence is that the criterion is frozen here before the verdict is written, that both thresholds were chosen as the plainly conventional ones rather than to fit the numbers, and that the instrument has six refusal paths and three outcomes.
hypotheses.instrument: seat record: fp8_population_weight.py over (i) seat record: captured-gemm-efficiency-20260914T2340Z.json, produced this turn by re-running captured_gemm_efficiency.py on cia-captured-trace-20260914T183257Z so the population and the class tables of cycles 18 and 19 come from ONE capture, and (ii) the two per-geometry contraction speedups of the cycle-17 receipt seat record: fp8-route-premise-check-20260914T2325Z.json, run ac58938b. Analysis-only: no card, no lease, no GPU window, no new bytes measured.
hypotheses.ruling: REFUTED on the frozen criterion s COVERAGE leg, unconditionally: "the geometries the arm measured carry less than 80 percent of the aten::mm population s device time per step". They carry 0.5750 -- 23,420.6 us of a 40,731.0 us/step mm population. 17,310.4 us/step sits at a leading dimension nobody has run FP8 at (m1024 10,052.7 over five distinct sites, m2048 5,479.7, m32768 1,625.9, m16 152.1), and a further 11,970.4 us/step of fmha attention contraction has no comparable rate in this census at all. The WEIGHT leg also fires as measured -- "the time-weighted expected contraction speedup over the measured subset is more than 5 percent relative below the arm s best measured figure": weighted 1.0672x against best 1.2196x, a 14.28 percent shortfall. The mechanism is exactly the one the cycle predicted: the arm s BETTER figure, 1.2196x, came from m256, which carries 3.07 percent of the population s mm time, while its WORSE figure, 1.0597x, came from m4096, which carries 54.43 percent. But this leg is CONDITIONAL on charging the dW outlier: on the source receipt s own outlier-excluded figures the weighted value is 1.2544x against a best 1.2564x, a 0.16 percent shortfall that does not refute. Stated here rather than in a footnote because a criterion with two legs must say which one carries the verdict. WHAT IS REFUTED IS REPRESENTATIVENESS AND NOTHING ELSE. Not FP8, not precision as a route, and nothing about what FP8 achieves at any geometry the arm did not run -- the instrument refuses to produce such a claim (EXTRAPOLATION_ATTEMPTED) and none is made. The consequence for selection is narrow and real: a route price built by applying 1.2196x, or the 1.1397x unweighted mean, to the linear class is not supported by these measurements, and the population-weighted saving over the subset the arm actually measured is 1,474.2 us/step against a 163,760 us governed step. This bounds the ROUTE and not the exit.
hypotheses.not_closed: CYCLE 20 UPDATE -- what this refutation does NOT close. (1) COVERAGE IS NOT A CEILING ON FP8. 42.5 percent of the mm population, 17,310.4 us/step, sits at an m the arm never ran, and the instrument refuses to impute a ratio there. m1024 alone is 10,052.7 us/step over five distinct sites and is the single largest unmeasured block. Measuring one FP8 site at m1024 would do more to price this route than anything else named on this campaign. (2) WITHIN ONE m THE SHAPES STILL DIFFER. The arm measured one projection site per m with K=1024 and N=3072; the population s four m4096 sites carry N/K of 2048, 1024 and 32768. A within-geometry shape dependence is entirely outside this instrument, which keys on m alone and says so in its claim boundary. (3) THE 11,970.4 us/step fmha POPULATION HAS NO COMPARABLE RATE. Attention contraction through the cutlass memory-efficient path was never run in FP8 and its FLOPs are not shape-comparable in this census. It is excluded from the mm population by construction, not judged. (4) THE WEIGHT LEG IS OUTLIER-CONDITIONAL, and the 2.72x dW event at m4096 (463.97 us against a 170.369 sibling mean) remains unexplained across three cycles. It now sits on the dominant geometry of the dominant class, so explaining it is worth more than it was when it was a footnote to one site. (5) THE WRAPPER STILL EXCEEDS THE CONTRACTION SAVING and is not re-measured here. Cycle 17 measured +474.982 us at m4096 and +160.133 at m256 against contraction savings of 111.893 and 55.100. What the wrapper costs at population scale is unmeasured, and a 1,474.2 us contraction saving does not survive a wrapper cost of unknown size. (6) FP16 ACCUMULATION IS UNTESTED and carries the same published dense rate on Ada. The precision route was never FP8-only; this row says nothing about the alternative. (7) NO MATCHED-RUN VARIATION on either input, so nothing here may be quoted as an improvement or a ceiling under the governed-run evidence contract. Both inputs are profiled traces, not governed measurements. (8) THE SELECTION RECORD IS STALE. seat record: now-next-after.md still carries an 04:03 PM LA header saying no route is selected and the non-GEMM premise is under test; cycle 18 refuted that premise and cycle 19 characterised the route set. Rewriting it is the successor act.
hypotheses.closing: ruled REFUTED on the coverage leg with the weight leg disclosed as outlier-conditional; receipt, sensitivity and registry row all landed

events.observation: Cycle 20 named the 11,970.4 us/step fmha block as carrying no rate in the GEMM census. Querying the registry on that proposition s own nouns corrected me before I opened a duplicate: attention-block-achieved-compute-rate-20260914 [COMPLETED] already measured it with a different instrument -- forward 2,491.1 us/step over 24 kernels, backward 9,479.3 us/step over 24, combined 64.0 TF/s = 0.388 of published at the most generous convention. My cycle-20 line was true of the GEMM census and false as a statement about the campaign, and it is corrected here rather than left standing. THAT ROW S OWN not_closed LINE IS WHAT IS LIVE: "the backward is 3.8x the forward in TIME against a 2.0-2.5x FLOP ratio, so the distance is not evenly held and the backward is the term to interrogate -- successor hypothesis attention-backward-carries-the-distance." THE OBVIOUS SHAPE OF THAT SUCCESSOR IS ALREADY DEAD AND I CHECKED BEFORE OPENING. The natural move is to look for a separable sub-kernel inside the backward -- a gradient preprocessing or reduction term carrying the excess. The efficiency receipt s own backend_kernels map shows the backward is ONE symbol, fmha_cutlassB_bf16_aligned_64x64_k64_seqaligned_sm80, 144 launches over 6 windows. There is no sub-kernel to separate. WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS A QUESTION ABOUT THE EVIDENCE RATHER THAN ABOUT ATTENTION. Every figure in that row is a per-step AGGREGATE divided by a call count. An aggregate describes a population only if the population is homogeneous, and this campaign has been burned by that exact assumption twice: a graph-replay mean describing a step that does not run because the first replay costs 55 percent more than the other two, and a 2.72x dW outlier inside a four-call partition that is still unexplained three cycles later. Before any treatment is sized against "the attention backward", the question is whether there is one attention backward or several.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. 24 forward and 24 backward kernel instances per step are not 24 repetitions of one call. The decoder issues attention per document, and documents within a 4x1024 batch need not present the same causal geometry to a block-causal kernel; the backward symbol itself carries seqaligned in its name. If the instances are heterogeneous, then the block s 3.805x time ratio is an average over a mixture, a treatment priced against it is priced against a call that may not exist, and the right unit of attack is a sub-population rather than the class. If they are homogeneous, the aggregate is trustworthy and the 3.805x is a property of every call -- which makes the FLOP-ratio gap a fact about the kernel rather than about the mixture. EITHER ANSWER IS USEFUL AND I DO NOT KNOW WHICH IT IS. Unlike cycles 17, 19 and 20, where I had already performed the arithmetic and said so at predict, this instrument has NOT been run against the real trace. Its deliberate-red battery is built entirely on SYNTHETIC traces for exactly that reason: running the battery proves the refusals without showing me the answer. THE INSTRUMENT REPORTS A DISTRIBUTION AND NOTHING ELSE. seat record: attention_call_distribution.py takes every fmha_cutlassF and fmha_cutlassB kernel instance whose START falls inside a census_step window -- WHOLE, never clipped to the boundary, because clipping would manufacture precisely the spread under measurement -- and reports min, quartiles, median, max, max-over-median, q3-over-q1, top-quartile share, coefficient of variation, distinct symbols, and the per-window means. It refuses on a trace with no windows (NO_WINDOWS), a direction with no instances (NO_KERNELS), a non-positive duration (DURATION_NOT_POSITIVE), and -- load-bearing -- a per-window instance count that varies (CALLS_NOT_UNIFORM_PER_WINDOW), because a per-step figure obtained by dividing a total by the window count is not a per-step figure when the windows do not carry the same number of calls. It names no treatment, composes no ceiling, and takes no position on WHY any spread exists.

events.refuted_if: Homogeneity fails in EITHER direction on ANY of three legs, and the verdict names which leg fired. (a) SPREAD: max over median above 1.50 -- one or more instances cost half again the typical call. (b) CONCENTRATION: the top quartile of instances carries more than 0.40 of the direction s total time, against the 0.25 a uniform population gives. (c) DRIFT: the ratio of the largest to the smallest per-window mean above 1.20, which would mean the steps differ from each other rather than the calls differing within a step -- a different finding from (a) and (b) and reported as such. WHAT REFUTED WOULD MEAN. That the attention block s per-step aggregates -- including the 64.0 TF/s achieved rate and the 3.805x backward/forward ratio -- describe a mixture rather than a call, and that any treatment sized against the class must first name which sub-population it acts on. It would NOT refute the rate measurement itself, which is an aggregate over the same time either way, and it would say nothing about why the spread exists. Bounds the ROUTE, not the exit.
events.supported_if: Both directions pass all three legs: max over median at or below 1.50, top-quartile share at or below 0.40, per-window mean spread at or below 1.20. Then the aggregates describe the population, the 3.805x ratio is a property of every call rather than of a mixture, and the backward s distance from its FLOP ratio is a fact about the kernel that a single sub-population cannot explain away. --- INCONCLUSIVE BRANCHES: (a) any refusal token, reported rather than worked around; in particular CALLS_NOT_UNIFORM_PER_WINDOW would mean the per-step figures in the parent row are themselves not per-step, which is a finding about the prior measurement and not about homogeneity; (b) fewer than 8 instances per direction per step, too few for a quartile statistic to mean anything -- the parent row says 24 each, so this is a guard rather than an expectation. --- DISCLOSED BEFORE THE RUN: I have NOT run this instrument against the real trace and I do not know the answer. The three thresholds were chosen as the conventional ones -- 1.50 is the same midpoint line cycle 17 used, 0.40 against a uniform 0.25, 1.20 as a fifth -- before any number existed to fit them to. The red battery is synthetic-only so that proving the refusals could not leak the result.

INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION WORTH RECORDING: this instrument attributes a kernel instance WHOLE to the window its start falls in and never clips, which is a different attribution rule from the parent row s, and it reproduces that row s per-step aggregates exactly -- forward 2,491.1 us/step, backward 9,479.3 us/step, ratio 3.8053. events.because: SUPPORTED on the frozen criterion, all three legs, both directions, none of them close. The criterion required max-over-median at or below 1.50, top-quartile share at or below 0.40 (against the 0.25 a uniform population gives), and a per-window mean spread at or below 1.20. FORWARD: 24 instances/step, min 97.25 us, median 103.65, max 113.12 -- max/median 1.0914, q3/q1 1.0461, top-quartile share 0.2604, coefficient of variation 0.0305, per-window mean spread 1.0109 across six windows. BACKWARD: 24 instances/step, min 386.44 us, median 394.76, max 405.96 -- max/median 1.0284, q3/q1 1.0122, top-quartile share 0.2531, coefficient of variation 0.0094, per-window mean spread 1.0065. One kernel symbol per direction. The backward population is the tightest distribution this campaign has measured anywhere: a 0.94 percent coefficient of variation over 144 instances. WHAT THIS LICENSES, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE CYCLE. The attention block s per-step aggregates describe a CALL and not a mixture, so the 3.8053x backward-over-forward TIME ratio against a 2.0-2.5x FLOP ratio is a property of every one of those 24 calls rather than an average over heterogeneous geometries. The successor hypothesis the parent row registered -- attention-backward-carries-the-distance -- therefore cannot be answered by finding a sub-population, and the obvious sub-kernel framing was already dead before this cycle opened (the backward is one fused symbol, 144 launches, no separable term). WHAT IT DOES NOT DO. It explains nothing about WHY the backward sits where it does, it names no treatment, it composes no ceiling, and it does not revisit the 64.0 TF/s achieved rate, which is an aggregate over the same time either way. A SUPPORTED homogeneity result is a statement about the EVIDENCE -- that a per-step figure may be reasoned with as a per-call figure -- and not a statement about the route.

events.hypothesis: CYCLE 21 UPDATE -- what a SUPPORTED homogeneity result does NOT close. (1) IT ANSWERS NOTHING ABOUT WHY. The backward is 3.8053x the forward in time against a 2.0-2.5x FLOP ratio, and this cycle establishes only that the gap is uniform across calls. Traffic, occupancy, and the recompute question (whether this cutlass backward recomputes S = QK^T, which the parent row carries as an unverified 4-vs-5-matmul range) are all untouched, and no instrument on this campaign produces measured traffic or measured occupancy. (2) HOMOGENEITY WITHIN ONE TRACE IS NOT HOMOGENEITY IN GENERAL. Six windows of one profiled capture at one geometry, B=4 S=1024 H=16 D=64, all documents the same length. A batch with ragged document lengths would present different causal geometries to a block-causal kernel and this result says nothing about that case. The governed hour is exactly such a case and is unmeasured here. (3) IT IS A PROFILED TRACE. No matched-run variation, and the per-instance durations carry whatever per-launch cost the profiler imposes. The tightness of the distribution makes an instrumentation artefact less likely to be hiding a spread, but it does not measure the artefact. (4) THE ATTENTION ROUTE ITSELF IS UNCHANGED AND UNSELECTED. 11,970.4 us/step at 0.388 of the published dense rate, cuDNN attention available on this build and never run, flash absent from the build entirely (sdpa-flash-backend-absent-from-this-torch-build-20260914). Running one cuDNN attention arm is a GPU act and is not this cycle. (5) THE CYCLE-20 SUCCESSOR STILL STANDS AHEAD OF THIS ONE. One FP8 contraction site at m1024, the largest unmeasured block of the linear population at 10,052.7 us/step, remains the named next measurement; attention is the second-largest unadjudicated block behind it. (6) A CORRECTION CARRIED FORWARD FROM CYCLE 20. That cycle s not_closed line said the fmha population "has no comparable rate in this census at all". True of the GEMM census, false as a statement about the campaign: attention-block-achieved-compute-rate-20260914 had measured it. The line is corrected in this row rather than left standing in the registry.

events.because: ruled SUPPORTED on all three legs in both directions; receipt and registry row landed, successor registered

events.observation: Assessing whether cycle 20 s registered successor -- measure one FP8 contraction site at m1024 -- is a dispatch or an authoring job, I read the worker that produced the only FP8 contraction measurements this campaign has. It is profile_strict_fp8_projection.py in the counterpart seat s worktree, bound by binding.json in custody cia-strict-fp8-profile-20260913T230000Z. events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. The grouped row kernel partitions the ROW dimension by cumulative offsets and rounds each group up to a 64-row block, so the hardware performs up to (G-1)*63/M more row-work than the useful count -- the bound the efficiency row records. events.observation: CYCLE 26 REFUTED THE JOIN HYPOTHESIS AND ITS SIXTH NOT_CLOSED LINE NAMES THIS ONE. An exhaustive enumeration of all 1,126 composed quantities in the campaign two append-only records found every one of the 20 flagged cross-provenance compositions DECLARED by its own row. That is a finding about the ROWS. It is not a finding about how those numbers are subsequently QUOTED, and cycle 26 recorded the gap in its own words: a well-conditioned join is still a join, the declaration means the number may not be quoted BARE, and this cycle did not look for it. THE ROWS DO NOT MERELY CONDITION, THEY PROHIBIT. Read across the registry, a recurring clause is an explicit refusal of a specific downstream use: "no absolute idle microsecond figure from this capture may be quoted as governed"; "never a measured ceiling and never an impossibility premise"; "expressing it against the 175,190 us governed step would compose across the profiled/governed boundary and is not quoted"; "nothing here may be quoted as an improvement or a ceiling under the governed-run evidence contract"; "not a prediction about the governed step and not a ceiling on the precision route"; "NO STEP-LEVEL ROUTE PRICE IS QUOTED"; "THE SPAN does not transfer at all". Each of those is a named number plus a named forbidden use. AND THE PROSE SURFACES ARE WHERE THE NUMBERS ARE ACTUALLY READ, not the registry. seat record: completion-push-ledger.md is roughly 10,878 CRLF lines and is the largest of them; seat record: now-next-after.md is the routing record; seat record: *.md are the prose receipts. Every operator-facing line, every routing header and every receipt narrative draws its numbers from rows that fence them, and nothing has ever checked whether a fence survived the quotation. THE CAMPAIGN HAS ALREADY PAID FOR THIS CLASS ONCE, in the governing rule rather than in a row: the 1945-terminal-is-80k correction withdraws an impossibility sentence I wrote four lines above a clause forbidding exit-ramp language, and its own generalisation is that the shape "arrives as the last sentence of a correct derivation". That is a bare quotation of a conditioned number, caught by the counterpart seat and not by any instrument.

events.hypothesis: WHY THE QUOTING SURFACE IS WHERE THIS DEFECT WOULD LIVE, mechanically. A registry row is written at the moment of measurement, by the seat that just ran the instrument, with every limitation in working memory. A ledger block, a routing header or a chat line is written later, under compression, to say what changed. Compression is the mechanism: the number is the part that carries information and the fence is the part that costs words, so the fence is what a shorter sentence drops. Nothing in the pipeline re-reads the row. THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS EVERY DEFECT THIS CAMPAIGN HAS PRODUCED, one surface further out. A claim about the present sourced from a record of the past -- except here the record is correct and the QUOTATION of it is what drifts. The lock file, the gate D blocker, the stored count beside its enumeration, the Running clause with no process: in each case a true statement existed somewhere and the thing acted on was a lossy copy of it. WHY IT IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A DEFECT TO QUOTE A NUMBER WITHOUT ITS CONDITION. Every summary is lossy by construction and a report that restated every fence would report nothing. So the hypothesis is NOT that conditions go unrestated. It is narrower and it is checkable: that a number whose row contains an EXPLICIT PROHIBITION on a specific use is, somewhere in the prose surfaces, used in exactly the prohibited way. A prohibition is not a caveat -- it names the use and forbids it, so violating it is a binary question with a text answer rather than a judgment about how much context is enough. THE MECHANISM OF THE INSTRUMENT: extract from every CURRENT registry row the prohibition clauses it states and the numeric literals each clause fences; then enumerate every occurrence of those literals in the prose surfaces; then, for each occurrence, read the window for the prohibited use and for any fence. Mechanical extraction, adjudication by reading -- the same division cycle 26 declared, and the same reason: a pattern can find a candidate and cannot rule one.

That is: every quotation of a prohibited-use number either carries the fence, or does not make the forbidden use. Also REFUTED if the enumeration cannot be made exhaustive -- if the instrument cannot show that it read every prose surface it names and every current row, it refuses rather than reporting zero, exactly as cycle 26 instrument does. SUPPORTED requires at least one occurrence, in a prose surface, of a number whose own registry row explicitly forbids that use, quoted in that use, with no fence in its window -- shown by quoting the prohibition and the violating sentence side by side. A SUPERSEDED OR ALREADY-CORRECTED QUOTATION DOES NOT COUNT. The ledger is append-only and carries its own corrections; a bare quotation later withdrawn in the same record is evidence the mechanism worked, not that it failed, and the instrument reports those separately. events.observation: THE PRODUCTION GROUPED LAUNCHER RUNS FOUR TIMES THE PROGRAMS OF THE ONLY ARM EVER MEASURED, AND NOTHING HAS PRICED THE DIFFERENCE. Cycle 25 corrected the arm-side join and registered exactly this as an open, unpriced question in its own not_closed list: "the row kernel grid dim0 is cdiv(m,64) over the FULL row count for EVERY group, so at G=4 three quarters of the programs exist only to hit the early exit `if first < end:`. Sizing dim0 per group is a source-derived candidate treatment never before named. An empty program costs a scheduling slot, not a matmul, and NOTHING HERE MEASURES WHAT THAT SLOT COSTS. No ceiling, no sign, no arm." THE CORRECTED JOIN, from that cycle: at the production forward site [4096,1024] x [4,1024,3072], 3,842.7 us/step, the arm at G=1 launched 1,536 programs and all 1,536 worked, zero empty; production at G=4 launches 6,144 programs, the same 1,536 units of work, 4,608 empty. The arm launched 0.25x of production. READ AT SOURCE THIS TURN, in the same worktree the arm imported (src/ember/model/ember_v0_grouped_capture.py): rows() launches _rows on grid (cdiv(m,64), cdiv(n,128), groups) and the kernel opens with `group = tl.program_id(2); start = tl.load(O + group - 1, group > 0, other=0); end = tl.load(O + group); first = start + tl.program_id(0) * BM; if first < end:` -- so dim0 is sized by the whole row count and every group re-walks it. The backward weight kernel _weights launches on (cdiv(k,64), cdiv(n,128), b.shape[0]) and stores to `W + group * K * N + ...` into a db allocated at b.shape, so its OUTPUT is [G,K,N]: at G=1 the arm wrote a quarter of the weight-gradient bytes production writes. Also derivable and also never measured. WHY THIS BLOCKS THE FP8 QUESTION RATHER THAN SITTING BESIDE IT. The only FP8 ratio this campaign holds -- 1.0597x at the kernel level, plus forward 0.796 and dX 0.629 -- is a ratio against a BF16 native that ran at G=1. If the BF16 denominator itself moves at G=4, that ratio moves for a reason that has nothing to do with FP8, and no FP8 arm at the production partition can be read until the BF16 geometry term is known. Structural coverage of the grouped-expert class is 0.0 us/step of 18,068.1 either way.

events.hypothesis: THE EXPLANATION UNDER TEST is the one implicit in every reading of the 1.0597x ratio to date: that the group axis is a scheduling detail and an early-exit program is free, so the same arithmetic costs the same whether it is launched as one group of 4,096 rows or four groups of 1,024. On that account the 4,608 empty programs cost only their scheduling slots, the SMs retire them in the launch tail, and G=4 and G=1 are the same measurement. THE MECHANISM THAT WOULD MAKE IT FALSE is equally concrete. An empty program is not free: it is scheduled onto an SM, reads two int32 values from the offsets vector, evaluates a predicate and retires. At G=4 on this site that is 4,608 such programs against 1,536 real ones, a 4x occupancy of the launch queue for 1x of the work, and the row kernel is a short-lived tile kernel where per-program overhead is a large fraction of per-program work. The backward is a second and independent mechanism in the same direction: dW at G=4 writes four [K,N] slabs where G=1 writes one, which is 4x the store traffic and 4x the grid on the group axis for the same accumulated rows. WHY THE ARITHMETIC IS IDENTICAL AND THE COMPARISON THEREFORE CLEAN. The saved operand carries ONE weight of [1024,3072] and 4,096 rows of one expert. Replicating that weight across four group slabs gives every row the same weight it had at G=1, so the forward and dX results at G=4 must be BITWISE IDENTICAL to G=1: the offsets 1024/2048/3072/4096 are all multiples of BM=64, so the row tiles are the same tiles and the K loop runs in the same order; only which program computes which tile changes. That makes bit-identity a precondition the run checks rather than a result it reports, and it means any timing difference is attributable to launcher geometry alone. dW is deliberately NOT bit-identical -- at G=4 it is four per-group slabs whose sum is the G=1 slab up to BF16 rounding boundaries -- which is exactly the production shape, so dW is measured but is not under the identity check. THIS IS A MEASUREMENT-VALIDITY REPAIR, NOT A TREATMENT ARM, and its pre-run ceiling says so: it has NO ceiling on the governed number, it removes no milliseconds, and it is refused by the 1.5x bar of 1945-multiplicative-movement-only if read as a treatment. What it buys is (a) the first measurement of the grouped-expert class at the group structure production actually runs, where coverage is 0.0 of 18,068.1 us/step, and (b) the price of the empty-program slot, which cycle 25 registered as a candidate treatment with no ceiling, no sign and no arm. A sign and a magnitude here are what would let that candidate be named at all.

The arm measured dW at both group counts as a declared-but-not-criterion leg and found G=4 FASTER by 11.399 us (175.512 against 186.911, ratio 0.93901, floor 0.327), despite writing four [1024,3072] slabs against one. My working mechanism reading was occupancy: the G=1 _weights grid (16,24,1) is 384 programs on a 128-SM card against G=4's 1,536. A second leg run under the same window refutes it. NC -- the per-group chunk count, a kernel constexpr -- moved with G in the arm: 16 at G=1 against 4 at G=4. A 2x2 over G in {1,4} and NC in {4,16} separates them: g1_nc16 190.614, g1_nc4 166.359, g4_nc4 174.592, g4_nc16 212.451 us. The GRID term is POSITIVE in both directions (+8.233 us at NC=4, +21.837 us at NC=16): holding chunking fixed, MORE groups costs MORE, which is the direction the extra output bytes predict and the opposite of the occupancy reading. Separately: src/ember/model/ember_v0_fp8_linear.py has no grouped path at all -- no offsets, no groups, no 3D weight -- so the registered grouped-FP8 successor cannot run against the grouped-expert sites, and the wrapper being a per-tensor amax over the whole activation means G can only move the contraction term.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM: the wrapper's cost scales with activation BYTES while the contraction's saving scales with FLOPs, and at these shapes the byte term wins. The per-tensor amax is a reduction over the WHOLE activation executed as two unfused kernels -- an elementwise abs that reads the activation and writes a same-sized temporary, then a reduction that reads that temporary -- so it moves roughly three activation-sized buffers through DRAM per quantized tensor and is bandwidth-bound end to end. The contraction it enables is compute-bound, and its measured saving is small: 1875.145 against 1987.038 us is a ratio of 0.9437, only 5.6 percent, not the 2x the format's tensor rate suggests. So a fixed bandwidth tax is being paid to buy a small percentage of a compute term. TWO CONSEQUENCES THAT FOLLOW FROM THE MECHANISM RATHER THAN FROM THE ARITHMETIC. First, the tax is GROUP-INDEPENDENT: a per-tensor amax over the whole activation does not care how the rows are partitioned, so G can only move the contraction term, and a grouped FP8 path cannot reduce the wrapper at all. Second, the tax is SHAPE-DEPENDENT in the opposite direction to the saving: at m256 the same decomposition gives BF16 305.984 against FP8 466.117 = 250.884 contraction + 215.233 wrapper, so the wrapper is 46 percent of the candidate at the small shape against 24 percent at m4096 -- the arithmetic intensity falls and the tax grows as a share. UNSTATED PREMISE, NAMED BECAUSE IT IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE: that the m4096 contraction ratio of 0.9437 generalises to the other GEMM shapes in the step. It is measured at exactly two geometries and nowhere else, and if the ratio at the dense trunk shapes is materially better the route's ceiling changes.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. An elementwise kernel whose operands were just written by the preceding kernel, and whose per-invocation working set fits in the 72 MB L2, can be served entirely from L2; its traffic never reaches DRAM and its achieved figure is an L2 rate, not a DRAM rate. If they cost a DRAM round trip, the byte-reduction direction is worth something near the 25.2 ms the elementwise row left open. If they cost an L2 round trip, the same fusion saves L2 traffic at a fraction of the price per byte, and the 25.2 ms is not available. Two opposite valuations of the same treatment, decided by one property of the data, and nothing on disk has measured it.

events.refuted_if: MORE THAN 50 PERCENT of the elementwise class's sized device time is spent in kernel invocations whose per-invocation working set EXCEEDS 72 MB. events.because: The frozen criterion was: REFUTED IF more than 50 percent of the elementwise class's sized device time is spent in kernel invocations whose per-invocation working set EXCEEDS 72 MB. It is 12.88 percent, across 9 kernels per step, at sized coverage 0.996. The criterion is not met, so the reading is SUPPORTED exactly as frozen. AND THE MECHANISM THE HYPOTHESIS PROPOSED IS REFUSED BY THE SAME DATA, which is reported here rather than left in the receipt. The explanation offered was that the above-DRAM aggregate is an L2 effect. If it were, the population that CANNOT be L2-resident by capacity would sit at or below the 1008 GB/s reference. events.hypothesis: WHAT THE REFUTED MECHANISM DOES NOT CLOSE. (a) L2 RESIDENCY IS STILL UNMEASURED. events.hypothesis: THE CLAIM UNDER TEST IS ABOUT THE ROUTE SET, NOT ABOUT A MECHANISM: that the non-GEMM stack is the ONLY treatment combination on this campaign whose pre-stated ceiling clears 1945-multiplicative-movement-only clause 1, AND that its ceiling at perfect effectiveness still lands far short of the 80,000 terminal. Both halves matter and they point opposite ways, which is why they are tested together rather than separately. The first half says an arm is dispatchable, so the card being idle is a defect with a cure. The second half says that arm, even if it collected every microsecond it aims at, produces about 36,940 positions/s and not 80,000 -- because 0.1036 s is still 2.02x the 0.0512 s the terminal allows, and what remains inside it is 78.6 ms of GEMM and attention arithmetic already running at 91 to 96 percent of the card published bf16 rate. WHY THIS IS NOT AN IMPOSSIBILITY CLAIM AND MAY NOT BE READ AS ONE (deterministic-closeable-units clause 3, 1945-terminal-is-80k clause 4): it prices the routes that have been MEASURED. It does not price FP16 accumulation, which carries the same published dense rate on Ada and which this campaign has never measured; it does not price an FP8 path with a fused or delayed-scaling encoder, which the wrapper decomposition names and nothing has measured; it does not price fewer FLOPs per position; and it does not price positions per optimizer step, which is a CONTRACT change and the operator to rule, priced at about 1.1x because only the 16.4 ms optimizer is genuinely fixed per step. The terminal is unchanged at 80,000. Measurement selects the ROUTE, never the exit.

No duplicate. THE OBSERVATION. Cycle 30 refused the L2-residency explanation for the elementwise class above-DRAM rate on its own data: the population whose per-invocation working set EXCEEDS the 72 MB L2 achieved 1390.9 GB/s against the fitting population 1146.8, and the >256MB bucket was highest of all at 1560.3. Residency predicts the opposite ordering, so the mechanism was refused. Cycle 32 then found the numerator inflated at exactly two ops -- aten::fill_ charged two buffers where it writes one, aten::copy_ charged three where it moves two -- worth 8.89 percent of all charged bytes. THE TWO LARGEST MEMBERS OF THAT EXCEEDING BUCKET ARE THOSE TWO OPS: copy_ [4096,32768] at 1813.1 us/step and fill_ [4096,32768] at 595.5 us/step, together 2,408.6 of the 3,522.1 us in the bucket.
