events.hypothesis: MECHANISM: the residency ordering cycle 30 measured is an artifact of the byte model, not of the cache. The correction acts on the exceeding-L2 side far harder than on the fitting side for two independent reasons that compound. First the RATE: the mis-charged ops carry 68 percent of the exceeding bucket time, so removing their inflation cuts that side numerator disproportionately. Second the MEMBERSHIP: the corrected working set of a fill_ is one buffer rather than two and of a copy_ is two rather than three, so sites near the 72 MB boundary MOVE from the exceeding side to the fitting side, and they take their inflated rate with them. Under the corrected model the ordering should invert -- fitting at or above exceeding -- which is what residency predicts and what cycle 30 did not see. WHY THIS DECIDES THE CAMPAIGN SELECTION AND NOT MERELY A PAST VERDICT. Cycle 31 established that exactly one distinct treatment clears the 1.5x arm bar, and its larger half is the whole elementwise class removed as device time, 27,500 us. Whether those microseconds are collectable depends on what sets them. If the class time is bytes that must cross DRAM regardless, fusion removes launches and intermediates but not traffic and the lever is far smaller than its class size. If a material share of the class is already L2-resident and still reads above the reference, then the rate is a modelling residue rather than a traffic floor, there is real headroom, and fusion can remove device time rather than reorganise it.

That would mean the ordering cycle 30 measured survives the correction, the byte model is not what produced it, and cycle 30 refusal of the residency mechanism stands on its own merits.

Reported beside the verdict, as readings and not as part of the criterion: both corrected rates against the 1008 GB/s published reference, the share of sized class time that CHANGED SIDE under the correction, and the corrected rate of the fitting population, which is the headroom figure the fusion lever depends on.

hypotheses.ruling: The frozen criterion reads: REFUTED IF the exceeding-L2 achieved rate REMAINS AT OR ABOVE the fitting-L2 achieved rate under the corrected byte model, with the corrected charge used for both bucket membership and rate. It does not. Incumbent 1390.9 exceeding against 1146.8 fitting; corrected 1063.7 exceeding against 1075.0 fitting. The ordering INVERTS, so the criterion is not met and the hypothesis is SUPPORTED. AND THE MARGIN IS 11.3 GB/s ON FIGURES NEAR 1070, ABOUT 1.05 PERCENT, WITH NO BETWEEN-RUN FLOOR AND NO MATCHED-RUN VARIATION. A one-percent inversion from a two-op correction to an estimated byte model is not a measurement of the cache. What the verdict licenses is narrow and is stated as such: cycle 30 refused the residency mechanism BECAUSE the ordering ran the wrong way, and that reason does not survive the correction. It does not establish residency, and cycle 30 conclusion is withdrawn as UNSUPPORTED rather than replaced by its opposite. HALF OF MY OWN PREDICTED MECHANISM IS REFUTED INSIDE THIS SUPPORTED VERDICT AND IS RECORDED RATHER THAN ABSORBED. The explain stage named two compounding effects, rate and membership. MEMBERSHIP DID ESSENTIALLY NOTHING: exactly one kernel changed side, aten::fill_ [32768,1024] at 52.3 us/step, 0.19 percent of sized class time. The inversion is the rate half alone. THE READING THAT MATTERS TO THE CAMPAIGN, and it cuts against the arm rather than for it: under the corrected model the L2-CAPABLE population reads 1075.0 GB/s, which is 1.066 of the 1008 GB/s published reference, and the aggregate is 1073.6, also 1.066. That row refused row 1 AS AN IDLE-REMOVAL ARM at 1.25x, and its FIRST not_closed line is verbatim this cycle: "(a) fusing the elementwise/norm population to remove DEVICE TIME rather than gaps ... their device execution is inside the 0.1311 s union, which the 1.25x bound does not cover". Cycles 32 and 33 then showed the class aggregate reads 1.066 of the 1008 GB/s published streaming reference even after a real byte-model correction, and that both L2 sides sit above it -- so for most of the class the time is bytes that still have to move after any fusion. events.hypothesis: MECHANISM: the class contains a LAUNCH-BOUND TAIL whose device time is set by per-kernel cost rather than by traffic, and a STREAMING BODY whose time is set by bytes. A fusion treatment removes per-kernel overhead and does not remove bytes, so it can collect the tail and not the body, and the honest lever is the tail rather than the class. HOW THE TWO ARE SEPARATED, per kernel rather than by eye: compare measured device time against the time that kernel corrected bytes would take at the published reference, and call the positive difference UNEXPLAINED BY BYTES. Summed over the class that is the ceiling on what a treatment can remove while leaving traffic unchanged. THE MECHANISM PREMISE IS STATED SEPARATELY FROM THE ARITHMETIC AND IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF. That fusion removes per-kernel overhead and no bytes is a claim about what the treatment DOES; it is not measured by this cycle, and the division is meaningless without it. A treatment that also eliminated intermediate buffers would remove bytes and could exceed the ceiling; one that fused kernels while keeping every intermediate materialised would reach less. My own record says a ceiling is where I fail, so the premise is written down where it can be attacked rather than folded into a number.

events.instrument: Analysis-only, no card, no lease, no new capture, claim --no-gpu. events.because: The frozen criterion reads: REFUTED IF the elementwise class device time UNEXPLAINED BY ITS CORRECTED BYTES at the 1008 GB/s published reference is AT OR ABOVE 21,886.7 us per step, that threshold being derived from the bar before the run rather than chosen after it. Far below the threshold, so the criterion is not met and the hypothesis is SUPPORTED: the class does split. THE SPLIT IS SHARP AND IT IS THE SHAPE PREDICTED. Nothing here refutes it and nothing here sizes it." -- and nongemm-launch-consolidation-bound-is-3.9ms-not-55ms-20260914 [REFUTED] -- "(a) THE BYTE-REDUCTION DIRECTION IS UNTOUCHED and is where the ~40.6 ms lives". STALENESS CHECKED, per the clause that a not_closed line is a claim about the PAST: both rows are dated 20260914 and could not know about the 20260915 rows. The NEWEST row, cycle 34, does not close the line -- it sharpens it, saying the byte-eliminating fusion variant is "outside the ceiling by construction and unpriced". So the line is confirmed open by the newest evidence rather than merely unrefuted by the oldest. THE OBSERVATION. Cycle 34 priced the half of fusion that removes LAUNCHES at 7,017.0 us per step of the class 27,447.4, and that put cycle 31 only above-bar arm at 1.3202x. Its own top unexplained sites are the reason this cycle exists: aten::copy_ and aten::add_ at [3072,1024] and [1024,3072], 6,433.2 us of device time carrying 4,273.6 us of excess at 308-349 GB/s. Those are intermediate buffers. A fusion that keeps them in registers does not merely remove their launches, it removes their TRAFFIC -- which is the one thing cycle 34 ceiling excludes by construction, and it is the largest unpriced quantity left on the non-GEMM path.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM: the elementwise class device time is spent on two kinds of bytes. Some cross memory because a value has to REACH memory -- a residual stream, a checkpointed activation, anything a later consumer reads after other work intervenes. The rest crosses memory only because the value was materialised between two adjacent operations that could have passed it in registers. The second kind is ELIMINABLE, and eliminating it removes the traffic itself rather than the launch around it. HOW THE ELIMINABLE PART IS COUNTED, per kernel and from op identity rather than by eye. Pure MOVEMENT ops -- aten::copy_, aten::fill_, aten::zero_ -- perform no arithmetic, so a producer writing straight into the destination makes the whole kernel disappear, every traversal of it. Every other elementwise op keeps its arithmetic and can shed AT MOST ONE traversal of its largest tensor: the single crossing of the intermediate it produces or consumes. One traversal per kernel is deliberate -- each eliminated intermediate is charged exactly once, to one side of the edge, so a fused chain cannot be counted twice. THE TWO HALVES CONTEND AND ARE NOT SUMMED. A kernel removed by fusion loses its launch overhead AND its bytes, and those are the same milliseconds. So the composite is computed per kernel as min(duration, overhead_excess + eliminable_byte_time), never as the sum of the two class totals. Cycle 34 number and this one would otherwise double-count every kernel the treatment removes outright. THE MECHANISM PREMISE, STATED SEPARATELY FROM THE ARITHMETIC BECAUSE IT IS THE LOAD-BEARING HALF AND IT IS WHERE MY OWN RECORD SAYS I FAIL: this counts what MAXIMAL fusion could reach -- every intermediate held in registers, every pure copy absorbed. The rest crosses memory only because the value was materialised between two adjacent operations that could have passed it in registers. The second kind is ELIMINABLE, and eliminating it removes the traffic itself rather than the launch around it. HOW THE ELIMINABLE PART IS COUNTED, per kernel and from op identity rather than by eye. Pure MOVEMENT ops -- aten::copy_, aten::fill_, aten::zero_ -- perform no arithmetic, so a producer writing straight into the destination makes the whole kernel disappear, every traversal of it. THE TWO HALVES CONTEND AND ARE NOT SUMMED. A kernel removed by fusion loses its launch overhead AND its bytes, and those are the same milliseconds. So the composite is computed per kernel as min(duration, overhead_excess + eliminable_byte_time), never as the sum of the two class totals. Cycle 34 number and this one would otherwise double-count every kernel the treatment removes outright. events.observation: THE OBSERVATION, from cycle 35 own receipt rather than from a plan. The best stack this campaign has priced is exactly TWO levers -- all device idle at 32,700 us and maximal elementwise fusion with bytes included at 19,105.6 us -- and it reaches 1.4627x against the operator 1.5x bar. It is short by 2,781.1 us, which is 12.7 percent of the contribution the bar needs and 1.7 percent of the governed step. Every prior cycle read as "no arm is close"; this one reads as "the arm is 2,781.1 us short", and those are different campaign states. WHAT IS OBSERVED AND UNEXPLAINED: the optimizer holds roughly 16,400 us per step -- about 12.4 percent -- and in thirty-five cycles nothing has examined it as a ROUTE. It has been measured as a duration and never as a class with a floor. A not_closed line has named it three times and each time it was deferred because its bytes looked untouchable from the trace: _fused_adamw_ takes TensorLists, and the profiler records their Input Dims EMPTY, so every trace-join instrument in this sequence is structurally blind to it. So the class with the margin in it is the one class the instruments cannot see. WHY THAT IS AN OBSERVATION AND NOT A PLAN: the blindness is a property of the recorded trace that I can check, and the 2,781.1 us margin is a number already on a landed receipt. What is NOT yet stated is any mechanism -- whether the optimizer duration is bandwidth-bound at all, and whether the margin is available in it.

events.hypothesis: THE MECHANISM, named as a thing that is either true or false rather than as a restatement: the optimizer class is BANDWIDTH-BOUND OVER ITS OWN STATE FOOTPRINT, and its roughly 16,400 us per step is set by how many times that footprint crosses the memory bus, not by arithmetic and not by launch count. CONCRETELY. A fused AdamW step, per trainable parameter, READS the parameter, its gradient, its first moment and its second moment, and WRITES the parameter, both moments, and (wherever the gradient is cleared rather than reused) the gradient again. That is a fixed small number of traversals of a footprint whose size is decided by the trainable-parameter count and the dtype of each of those four tensors -- quantities the checkpoint and the optimizer-state inventory both record exactly. The arithmetic between the reads and the writes is a handful of FLOPs per element, so on this card the class cannot be compute-bound; if the mechanism is true, duration is footprint times traversals divided by achieved bandwidth, and nothing else. WHAT THE MECHANISM PREDICTS, WHICH IS WHY IT IS AN EXPLANATION AND NOT A LABEL. It predicts a FLOOR that is computable WITHOUT the trace: the necessary traffic is the footprint times the minimum traversal count a correct fused AdamW must perform. Measured duration ABOVE that floor is the removable part -- redundant traversals, an unfused path, state held in a wider dtype than the update needs, or gradient clearing as a separate pass. Measured duration AT the floor means the class is already at its bandwidth limit and supplies NONE of the 2,781.1 us the bar needs, which would close the optimizer as a route and leave the campaign needing a different third lever. WHY THIS SURVIVES THE INSTRUMENT BLINDNESS THAT DEFERRED IT THREE TIMES. The profiler records _fused_adamw_ Input Dims as EMPTY because it takes TensorLists, so every trace-join instrument in this campaign is structurally unable to size this class -- and that is exactly why it has been skipped. But the mechanism above does not need the trace: the footprint comes from the parameter and optimizer-state inventory, and the duration comes from the device timeline, which records the kernel regardless of whether its dims were captured. The two halves of the comparison come from two different sources, neither of which is the blind one.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED IF the optimizer class REMOVABLE time -- measured optimizer device time per step MINUS the bandwidth floor implied by its own state footprint -- is BELOW 2,781.1 us per step. THE THRESHOLD IS DERIVED FROM THE BAR AND NOT FROM THE DATA, and it is fixed here before any number is read: governed step 0.16376 s; 1.5x needs the step at 0.109173 s, a removal of 54,586.7 us; the two levers already priced supply all-device-idle 32,700.0 us and maximal elementwise fusion 19,105.6 us, capped composite 51,805.6; the shortfall is 54,586.7 - 51,805.6 = 2,781.1 us. That is exactly what a third lever must supply, so it is exactly the bar this class must clear to be the lever that decides the arm. THE FLOOR IS THE HONEST, MOST HOSTILE FORM OF THE COMPARISON. necessary_bytes = sum over the four AdamW tensors of trainable_elements x dtype_size, times the MINIMUM traversal count a correct fused AdamW must perform (read p, grad, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq; write p, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq), and floor_us = necessary_bytes / (1008 GB/s) x 1e6 -- 1008 being the PUBLISHED specification used to express a fraction, never a measured ceiling and never an impossibility premise. Using the published rate makes the floor as LOW as it can be and therefore the removable excess as LARGE as it can be, so the criterion is biased toward SUPPORTING the hypothesis; a refutation under it is a real refutation. SUPPORTED IF removable >= 2,781.1 us -- and the update must then say which sub-mechanism carries the excess (redundant traversals, an unfused path, state wider than the update needs, or a separate gradient-clearing pass), because "there is excess" names no treatment. INCONCLUSIVE IS RESERVED, and narrowly: only if the optimizer device kernels cannot be identified in the timeline at all, or the trainable-parameter footprint cannot be read from the inventory. A number that lands just under 2,781.1 is a REFUTATION, not an inconclusive result, and cycle 35 already proved the reverse case -- 19,105.6 against 21,886.7, ruled SUPPORTED at a 12.7 percent margin rather than softened. The same discipline binds in this direction.

DURATION: device timeline of cia-captured-trace-20260914T183257Z.json, the same 6 census windows and the same step-window clipping as cycles 33-35, filtered to optimizer kernels by symbol (fused adamw / multi_tensor / foreach) rather than by op name, since _fused_adamw_ Input Dims are EMPTY and that is precisely the blindness this design routes around. FOOTPRINT: the trainable-parameter count and the dtypes of parameter, gradient and both moments, read from the CIA hour custody checkpoint manifest and its optimizer-state identity block -- NOT from the trace. DELIBERATE RED FIRST, as every instrument in this sequence has done: run the filter against a trace window with no optimizer kernel present and require a non-zero exit with an explicit refusal rather than a zero, since a zero here would read as "the optimizer costs nothing" and support the refutation for the one reason that is not evidence.

events.because: The frozen criterion reads: "REFUTED IF the optimizer class REMOVABLE time -- measured optimizer device time per step MINUS the bandwidth floor implied by its own state footprint -- is BELOW 2,781.1 us per step." Removable is 10,234.0 us per step, so the criterion is not met and the hypothesis is SUPPORTED. THE ARITHMETIC, every width measured rather than assumed. Measured optimizer device time is 16,817.8 us/step over 46.7 kernels across three symbols (fused AdamW multi_tensor_apply 15,847.4; _ForeachUnaryOp behind _foreach_zero_ 963.9; _ForeachBinaryOpScalar 6.5). The state archive was walked as a zip with a stub unpickler: 702 bf16 moment storages, 948,060,160 elements, 1,896,120,320 bytes, exactly 2.0000 B/elem, plus 351 single-element fp32 step counters. 702 moment tensors is 351 parameters x 2 moments, giving 474,030,080 participating elements -- which the manifest independently corroborates at 474,029,824 changed elements, 0.0001 percent apart, from a field this instrument does not use in its arithmetic. The parameter width was measured as a RATIO, not assumed: core 502,858,033 bytes plus expert objects 5,662,593,375 over 3,082,539,008 declared elements is 2.0001 B/elem, resolving to bf16 within the 0.02 tolerance the script refuses outside of. The minimum correct fused AdamW traversal -- read param, grad, exp_avg, exp_avg_sq; write param and both moments -- is therefore 6,636,421,120 bytes, and at the PUBLISHED 1008 GB/s (a specification used to express a fraction, never a measured ceiling for this card and never an impossibility premise) the floor is 6,583.8 us/step. 16,817.8 - 6,583.8 = 10,234.0 us, which is 3.68x the 2,781.1 us the bar needs from a third lever. THE CRITERION WAS BIASED TOWARD THIS ANSWER AND THE RESULT SURVIVES REMOVING THE BIAS. The published rate makes the floor lowest and the excess largest, so support under it is the weakest form of support. Both hostile dtype variants were computed: gradient in fp32 raises the floor to 7,524.3 us (removable 9,293.5), and parameter and gradient both in fp32 raise it to 9,405.4 us (removable 7,412.4). Neither flips the verdict. The verdict flips only if this card sustains below 472.8 GB/s on this traffic -- 46.9 percent of the published rate -- which is a far larger correction than any dtype error could produce. THE INSTRUMENT REFUSES AN EMPTY CLASS, PROVED BEFORE THE GREEN RUN. --prove-red drops the optimizer symbols from the filter and the script exits 2 rather than publishing a zero, because zero removable time reads as "the optimizer costs nothing" (a finding) while an empty match means "this instrument did not find the optimizer" (a defect), and those are opposite in meaning and identical in arithmetic. With no counterpart seat to issue a PASS, that deliberate red and the execution of the real consumer are what this verdict rests on. WHAT THIS VERDICT IS NOT. Removable time is the distance between a measurement and a floor. It is not a ceiling on any treatment, not a claim that any mechanism collects it, and not an assertion about what this card can do. No arm is named by this ruling.

events.hypothesis: WHICH SUB-MECHANISM CARRIES THE EXCESS -- the criterion required this, and the honest answer is partial, so it is given as one measured term, one ELIMINATED candidate, and one open remainder. (1) MEASURED, 963.9 us: the separate gradient-clearing pass is real and is one of the four named candidates. _ForeachUnaryOp_cu sits behind aten::_foreach_zero_ x128 per step and costs 963.9 us/step, which is traffic no correct fused AdamW needs, since a fused step can consume the gradient in place. (2) ELIMINATED: "state wider than the update needs" is REFUTED by this cycle own split. The moments are already bf16 at exactly 2.0000 B/elem, and the parameters are bf16 too. There is no narrowing left to take; the dtype lever on this class is already spent, and any future proposal to narrow optimizer state is answered by this receipt. (3) OPEN, about 9,270 us: the fused kernel itself measures 15,847.4 us against a 6,583.8 us whole-class floor, roughly 2.4x the minimum traffic, and nothing in this cycle attributes that. Twenty-one device kernels per step carry 128 aten::_fused_adamw_ calls, so the class is decidedly NOT launch-bound at 754.6 us per kernel, which leaves redundant traversals or an unfused interior as the two surviving candidates and does not choose between them. WHAT THE REFUTATION DID NOT CLOSE, and what this SUPPORT does not open. A SUPPORTED verdict here closes nothing about routes either: it says the optimizer CONTAINS the 2,781.1 us shortfall with room to spare, not that any mechanism collects it. The three levers now priced (idle 32,700.0, elementwise 19,105.6, optimizer 10,234.0) act on different milliseconds only if they do not contend, and contention has NOT been checked -- the optimizer runs strictly after backward on one stream, which is precisely the serialization the idle lever claims, so these two may be pricing overlapping milliseconds and summing them would be the contending-ceilings error. hypotheses.observation: THE OBSERVATION, from cycle 35 own receipt rather than from a plan. It is short by 2,781.1 us, which is 12.7 percent of the contribution the bar needs and 1.7 percent of the governed step. Every prior cycle read as "no arm is close"; this one reads as "the arm is 2,781.1 us short", and those are different campaign states. WHAT IS OBSERVED AND UNEXPLAINED: the optimizer holds roughly 16,400 us per step -- about 12.4 percent -- and in thirty-five cycles nothing has examined it as a ROUTE. It has been measured as a duration and never as a class with a floor. A not_closed line has named it three times and each time it was deferred because its bytes looked untouchable from the trace: _fused_adamw_ takes TensorLists, and the profiler records their Input Dims EMPTY, so every trace-join instrument in this sequence is structurally blind to it. So the class with the margin in it is the one class the instruments cannot see. hypotheses.explanation: THE MECHANISM, named as a thing that is either true or false rather than as a restatement: the optimizer class is BANDWIDTH-BOUND OVER ITS OWN STATE FOOTPRINT, and its roughly 16,400 us per step is set by how many times that footprint crosses the memory bus, not by arithmetic and not by launch count. CONCRETELY. A fused AdamW step, per trainable parameter, READS the parameter, its gradient, its first moment and its second moment, and WRITES the parameter, both moments, and (wherever the gradient is cleared rather than reused) the gradient again. That is a fixed small number of traversals of a footprint whose size is decided by the trainable-parameter count and the dtype of each of those four tensors -- quantities the checkpoint and the optimizer-state inventory both record exactly. The arithmetic between the reads and the writes is a handful of FLOPs per element, so on this card the class cannot be compute-bound; if the mechanism is true, duration is footprint times traversals divided by achieved bandwidth, and nothing else. events.hypothesis: THE MECHANISM, stated so it is either true or false. The three levers are DISJOINT POPULATIONS of device microseconds, so their removals compose additively up to the limit of what each class contains. Concretely: idle is the complement of the busy interval union inside the census windows, so by construction it shares no microsecond with any kernel; and the elementwise and optimizer kernel sets are disjoint because the two selectors match different kernel families, so no kernel microsecond is claimed by both levers. WHAT IT DOES NOT EXPLAIN, named now rather than discovered later: disjoint POPULATIONS do not make the three removals independent ACTIONS. A shorter kernel sequence can change how much device idle exists, and a fused elementwise path changes which kernels the optimizer waits behind. events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. If the in-window device timeline is a single unbroken serialized chain -- no coincident kernels, no zero-length gaps -- then K kernels have exactly K-1 gaps. Removing R interior kernels leaves K-R kernels and K-R-1 gaps, so EXACTLY R gaps retire. Not R times two, and not the count of gaps touching a removed kernel: a removal merges its two neighbouring gaps into one, which destroys one gap and keeps the other. That is the whole correction. THE IDENTITY IS THE LOAD-BEARING PREMISE, SO IT IS VERIFIED PER WINDOW AND NOT ASSUMED. On a timeline with any concurrency the identity fails and the retirement argument fails with it, silently, producing numbers that look perfectly reasonable. The instrument therefore asserts gaps == kernels-1 in every window of every geometry and REFUSES when it does not hold, and its deliberate red injects a coincident kernel to prove the refusal fires. Cycle 37 independently established zero concurrency on this trace by a different route (sum of kernel durations equals their interval union), so the identity is expected to hold -- which is exactly why it must be checked rather than assumed. A SECOND GEOMETRY, because cycle 39 observed the identity on one trace and one observation does not establish that it generalises. Each source is checked independently. WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, and it is now the largest unverified assumption under the corrected figure: the share is still R over gaps -- a COUNT share applied to a duration total, which assumes retired gaps are of average duration. These traces cannot check that, because they span ~503,890 us per window against a 163,760 us governed step and their gap durations are instrumentation-dominated. Count survives profiling (stretching an interval neither creates nor destroys a launch boundary); duration does not, and composing it with a governed figure is what the governed-run evidence contract separation clause forbids. THE OPTIMIZER FRACTION STAYS BOUNDED. Its lever prices 10,234.0 us as measured minus a bandwidth floor -- kernels shrunk, not launches retired -- so RETIRES-NOTHING is what its receipt literally describes and RETIRES-EVERYTHING (all 46.7 kernels per step) is the extreme. That assumption is false on its face for any hole in which the device was waiting on a dependency rather than on the host: the host had already issued the closing kernel, so the hole does not close because launches became cheaper or fewer. An existing split receipt (idle-split-for-cycle41-20260915T0725Z.json) already reports DEPENDENCY_HOST_BUSY at 2,766.7 holes per step and DEPENDENCY_HOST_IDLE at 113.3, against HOST_DISPATCH at 5,026.7 -- and I have read those numbers, which is disclosed here so the criterion below is visibly derived from the BAR and not from them.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. Every device event in the trace carries a correlation id linking it to the host launch call that issued it. For the hole between device activity ending at a and resuming at b, take the CLOSER -- the device event starting at b -- and its launch call. If that launch had not returned by a, the device was waiting on the host: HOST_DISPATCH, and consistent with launch-bound execution. If the launch had already returned before a, the host was done and the device waited on something else: DEPENDENCY. A hole whose closer resolves to no launch call is UNATTRIBUTED and is never folded into either class. WHY THE HEADLINE IS A COUNT AND NOT A DURATION, which is the same principle cycles 38-41 established and which points the other way here. The trace spans ~503,890 us per window against a 163,760 us governed step, so absolute hole DURATIONS are instrumentation-dominated and the governed-run evidence contract separation clause forbids composing them with a governed figure. Hole COUNT survives profiling, because stretching an interval neither creates nor destroys a launch boundary. The prior receipt puts DEPENDENCY at 2.3% of profiled idle DURATION and about 36% of hole COUNT, and those disagree by more than an order of magnitude precisely because the profiler inflates host-side time. The duration figure is the one the profiler corrupts. THE BIAS DIRECTION IS NAMED BEFORE THE RUN AND IT RUNS AGAINST THE REFUTATION. Profiling LENGTHENS every launch call, so a launch that truly returned before a hole began can appear still-open under the profiler. That misclassifies DEPENDENCY holes as HOST_DISPATCH and never the reverse, so the measured dependency count share is a LOWER BOUND on the true one and any refutation computed from it is conservative. TWO POPULATIONS, AND THE VERDICT BINDS ON THE ONE MOST FAVOURABLE TO THE COMPOSITION. The prior split ran over all device categories (~7,906.7 holes per step); cycles 38-41 priced gaps over kernels only (7,437.7). Both are computed and the verdict uses the SMALLER dependency share, so the composition is refuted only if it fails on its better reading. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM. A DEPENDENCY hole is not unreachable idle in general -- a whole-step graph with the optimizer on a second stream targets exactly that population, and it is a DIFFERENT lever from the launch-rate one the 32,700.0 us figure prices. This measures what the IDLE LEVER AS PRICED cannot reach, and scaling it is not the same as retiring the route.

THE THRESHOLD IS DERIVED FROM THE BAR AND FROM NOTHING READ IN ANY RECEIPT: 1.5x on the 0.16376 s governed step needs 54,586.7 us removed; the elementwise and optimizer levers supply 29,339.6 us between them; cycle 41 measured the contested overlap at 0.18899 of whatever the idle lever is, so the idle lever must supply 25,247.1 / 0.81101 = 31,130.2 us of reachable idle out of its priced 32,700.0, which is 95.2% of it. events.observation: Cycle 42 audited the IDLE lever's maximal-effectiveness premise and found 36.4% of its target population unreachable by the mechanism that priced it, which refuted the three-lever 1.5x composition. The other two levers have had no such audit. This cycle audits the ELEMENTWISE lever, 19,105.6 us per step, whose own instrument states the premise in its docstring: "every intermediate held in registers, every pure copy absorbed ... It does not prove any two kernels are actually adjacent in a dataflow sense." FIRST, A QUESTION FROM THE CYCLE-42 LEDGER IS ANSWERED BY READING THE SOURCE RATHER THAN BY MEASURING, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. I wrote that the elementwise figure might already contain launch or idle time the idle lever ALSO counts. It does not: the per-kernel credit is min(dur_us, excess + eliminable_byte_time) summed over kernel DEVICE durations, so the whole 19,105.6 us is bounded by and composed of device time inside elementwise kernels. No host time and no inter-kernel hole enters it. The real overlap with the idle lever is the one cycle 41 already measured -- the gaps adjacent to retired kernels, 0.18899 of the idle lever -- and that is a different quantity, already netted out. SECOND, A FIGURE I PUBLISHED IN THAT SAME LEDGER BLOCK IS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. I wrote that the lever implies 16.3 us per removed kernel against 1,172.3 kernels, "far above a typical elementwise kernel's device time". That divides the WHOLE lever by only the fully-removed count. The receipt's own split is 1,172.3 kernels removed outright for 8,634.1 us, which is 7.365 us each and entirely ordinary; the remaining 10,471.5 us is partial credit spread across the other ~2,274.7 kernels of the 3,447.0-kernel class. There was no anomaly there.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. The byte half of the lever credits each kernel with shedding ONE traversal of its largest tensor -- the single crossing of the intermediate it produces or consumes. That traversal is elidable only if the kernel on the OTHER SIDE of that edge sits inside the same fused group. So take each elementwise kernel's immediate device PREDECESSOR and SUCCESSOR over the full in-window kernel timeline. If neither is in the elementwise class, the kernel has no in-class neighbour on either edge, no fusion within this class can hold its intermediate in a register, and the value is materialized across a class boundary: ISOLATED. At least one in-class neighbour: GROUPED, a candidate fusible edge exists. ADJACENCY IS A PROXY FOR DATAFLOW AND ITS BIAS IS NAMED BEFORE THE RUN. Two adjacent elementwise kernels need not be dataflow-connected, so adjacency OVER-counts fusibility. GROUPED is an upper bound on the genuinely fusible set and ISOLATED is a LOWER bound on the unreachable one, so every figure is conservative in the direction that spares the lever and any refutation computed from it is safe to act on. This is the same bias structure cycle 42 carried, pointing the same way. WHAT IS CHARGED, AND IT IS THE SMALLER OF TWO DEFENSIBLE ACCOUNTINGS. Only the eliminable-byte part of an isolated kernel's credit is an INTERMEDIATE claim; the excess part is device time above a published-rate byte ideal and says nothing about registers. So an isolated kernel keeps min(dur, excess) and is charged only the remainder. Charging the whole composite would have produced the larger number. THE BYTE MODEL IS INHERITED, THE DISCRIMINATOR IS AUTHORED. Byte counting, the elementwise selector, the 1008 GB/s reference and the per-kernel cap are imported from elementwise_byte_reduction_ceiling so the two receipts describe the same lever to the last microsecond; the adjacency classification is the thing under test and is written from the trace. WHY THIS IS A COUNT-ADJACENT MEASURE AND NOT A DURATION COMPOSITION. Class membership of a neighbour is a property of the kernel sequence, which profiling does not change -- stretching an interval neither creates nor destroys a kernel. The charged microseconds are DEVICE durations from within the profiled trace, the same population the 19,105.6 us figure itself is built from, so this is a re-partition of an existing quantity rather than a new composition across the governed/profiled boundary.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED IF the unreachable charge on the ISOLATED set EXCEEDS 7,452.9 us per step. THE THRESHOLD IS FROZEN FROM THE BAR AND IS NOT CHOSEN HERE: 1.5x on the 0.16376 s governed step needs 54,586.7 us removed, the naive three-lever sum supplied 62,039.6 us, so the margin the composition ever had is exactly 7,452.9 us -- the same figure cycles 38, 39, 40 and 41 used unchanged. A lever whose unreachable part alone exceeds the entire margin the composition ever held is not a ceiling that was slightly optimistic; it is a ceiling of the same kind cycle 42 found overstated by 36%. ALSO REFUSED, independently of any share, IF THE CLASSIFICATION DEGENERATES: the instrument exits non-zero when the ISOLATED set is EMPTY, because an unreachable charge of 0.0 would read as "every credited microsecond is fusible" -- a FINDING that leaves the lever at its full 19,105.6 us -- while being equally consistent with a neighbour lookup that never resolves, which is a DEFECT; and when EVERY elementwise kernel is isolated, which with this class holding roughly half of all kernels is a broken timeline join rather than a fact about fusion. A sized coverage below 0.50 also refuses, because a thin sized population makes every isolated kernel charge nothing and the lever would pass for the one reason that is not evidence. I DO NOT PREDICT THE DIRECTION OF THIS ONE, and I am saying so before the run because I predicted cycle 42's refutation in writing and that is only creditable if I also say when I cannot. The elementwise class holds roughly half the kernels in the step, which argues that most of them have an in-class neighbour and the lever largely survives; against that, the class's largest credited sites are aten::copy_ and aten::add_ on residual-stream shapes, which sit between GEMMs by construction. Those two considerations point opposite ways and I have not measured which dominates.
events.supported_if: SUPPORTED IF the unreachable charge is at or below 7,452.9 us per step: the lever's maximal-fusion premise survives an adjacency audit at the scale that matters to the composition, and the elementwise figure stands as priced apart from a correction smaller than the margin. Note that SUPPORTED here does NOT revive the 1.5x composition -- cycle 42 ruled it REFUTED at 46,199.7 us against 54,586.7 needed, and this cycle can only lower that. hypotheses.explanation: MECHANISM. The byte half of the lever credits each kernel with shedding ONE traversal of its largest tensor -- the single crossing of the intermediate it produces or consumes. That traversal is elidable only if the kernel on the OTHER SIDE of that edge sits inside the same fused group. So take each elementwise kernel's immediate device PREDECESSOR and SUCCESSOR over the full in-window kernel timeline. If neither is in the elementwise class, the kernel has no in-class neighbour on either edge, no fusion within this class can hold its intermediate in a register, and the value is materialized across a class boundary: ISOLATED. At least one in-class neighbour: GROUPED, a candidate fusible edge exists. ADJACENCY IS A PROXY FOR DATAFLOW AND ITS BIAS IS NAMED BEFORE THE RUN. Two adjacent elementwise kernels need not be dataflow-connected, so adjacency OVER-counts fusibility. GROUPED is an upper bound on the genuinely fusible set and ISOLATED is a LOWER bound on the unreachable one, so every figure is conservative in the direction that spares the lever and any refutation computed from it is safe to act on. This is the same bias structure cycle 42 carried, pointing the same way. WHAT IS CHARGED, AND IT IS THE SMALLER OF TWO DEFENSIBLE ACCOUNTINGS. Only the eliminable-byte part of an isolated kernel's credit is an INTERMEDIATE claim; the excess part is device time above a published-rate byte ideal and says nothing about registers. So an isolated kernel keeps min(dur, excess) and is charged only the remainder. Charging the whole composite would have produced the larger number. Class membership of a neighbour is a property of the kernel sequence, which profiling does not change -- stretching an interval neither creates nor destroys a kernel. The charged microseconds are DEVICE durations from within the profiled trace, the same population the 19,105.6 us figure itself is built from, so this is a re-partition of an existing quantity rather than a new composition across the governed/profiled boundary.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. This card has 72 MB of L2 and the standing explanation for three device classes reporting ABOVE the published DRAM rate -- elementwise 1.151, reduce 1.633, triton_fused 2.253 -- is a working set around 25 MB sitting inside it. So the sign of a kernel's residual against a DRAM-rate ideal is expected to track its working set. A kernel whose sized bytes fit in L2 can beat the DRAM rate, and a positive residual there is NOT explained by traffic, so it is admissible as overhead a treatment might collect. A kernel whose sized bytes EXCEED L2 must go to DRAM for the remainder, so its shortfall against the same ideal is TRAFFIC -- and traffic is already priced by the byte half of this very lever. Charging it again to the excess half is the same microseconds counted twice, inside one lever, which is exactly the defect the per-kernel cap was written to prevent between the halves and does not prevent within one of them. THREE READINGS OF THE ESTIMATOR ARE PUBLISHED so it is checkable rather than asserted: the one-sided sum at the published rate, which must reproduce 7,017.0 us or the instrument is describing a different lever; the TWO-sided sum at the same rate, which is the quantity any class-level statement about overhead actually rests on; and the one-sided sum recomputed with the reference set to the class's own measured achieved rate, so the class no longer beats its own reference. THE WORKING-SET TEST IS A PROXY AND ITS LIMIT IS NAMED BEFORE THE RUN. No L2 hit-rate counter exists in this build, so this is a working-set test and not a residency measurement: a kernel under 72 MB can still miss L2 because it shares the cache with everything else in flight, and a kernel above it can hit on part of its traffic. The first error makes the L2_RESIDENT set too large and therefore the DRAM_BOUND charge too small, which spares the lever; the second makes the charge too large. The two do not cancel and I cannot sign the net, so unlike cycles 42 and 43 this instrument does NOT carry a one-directional bias argument, and that is stated rather than manufactured.

THE WORKING-SET TEST IS A PROXY AND ITS LIMIT IS NAMED BEFORE THE RUN. No L2 hit-rate counter exists in this build, so this is a working-set test and not a residency measurement: a kernel under 72 MB can still miss L2 because it shares the cache with everything else in flight, and a kernel above it can hit on part of its traffic. The first error makes the L2_RESIDENT set too large and therefore the DRAM_BOUND charge too small, which spares the lever; the second makes the charge too large. hypotheses.criterion: REFUTED IF the one-sided excess sitting on DRAM_BOUND kernels -- those whose sized working set exceeds the 72 MB L2 capacity -- EXCEEDS 4,730.5 us per step. THE THRESHOLD IS A ROUTE-SELECTION THRESHOLD AND IS STATED AS SUCH RATHER THAN DRESSED AS THE BAR. The 1.5x question is already settled: cycle 42 ruled the three-lever composition REFUTED at 46,199.7 us against 54,586.7 needed and cycle 43 lowered it to 42,058.6 us. No further reduction of any lever can change that verdict, so a threshold derived from 1.5x could only be a criterion that cannot fail, which the loop forbids. The live question is which lever the campaign should pursue next, and the threshold that changes that answer is the one that REORDERS the two audited levers: the elementwise lever stands at 14,964.5 us after cycle 43 and the optimizer lever at 10,234.0 us, so a double-counted charge above their difference of 4,730.5 us drops elementwise below optimizer and inverts the campaign's own ranking. ALSO REFUSED, independently of any charge, IF THE PARTITION DEGENERATES: the instrument exits non-zero when the DRAM_BOUND set is EMPTY, because an excess that is 100% admissible overhead would read as "the estimator is sound" -- a FINDING that leaves the excess half fully spendable -- while being equally consistent with a size join that resolved nothing, a DEFECT; and when EVERY kernel is DRAM_BOUND, which contradicts the class achieving above the published rate and is a broken join rather than a finding. hypotheses.ruling: The frozen criterion was: REFUTED IF the one-sided excess sitting on DRAM_BOUND kernels -- those whose sized working set exceeds the 72 MB L2 -- EXCEEDS 4,730.5 us per step, the difference between the elementwise lever after cycle 43 (14,964.5) and the optimizer lever (10,234.0), because a double count above that inverts the campaign's own ranking of the two audited levers. Measured 151.2 us per step, 3.2% of the threshold and 2.2% of the 7,017.0 us excess half. The criterion is met and the verdict is SUPPORTED. THE PARTITION. Only 8.0 of 3,447.0 elementwise kernels per step have a sized working set above L2. They hold 3,469.8 us of device time -- 12.6% of the class -- and carry just 151.2 us of the one-sided excess, because they are the large aten::copy_ and aten::fill_ sites that already run near or above the published rate. The other 3,439.0 kernels fit in L2 and carry 6,865.8 us of the excess. So the mechanism I proposed is not what is behind the excess half: the double count of DRAM traffic exists and is 151.2 us, which is not material to anything. THE ONE-SIDED READING REPRODUCED THE PRICED FIGURE EXACTLY -- 7,017.0 us against the 7,017.0 us the composition spends, at sized coverage 0.9960 -- so the instrument is auditing the same quantity and not a neighbour of it. SUPPORTED HERE MEANS THE PROPOSED MECHANISM FAILED, NOT THAT THE ESTIMATOR IS SOUND. The cycle measured something larger than its own criterion and that finding is recorded in the update, unruled, because a verdict re-cut to fit numbers already in hand is chosen to fit them. The elementwise lever moves only 14,964.5 -> 14,813.3 us and the three-lever stack 42,058.6 -> 41,907.4 us against 54,586.7 needed, which changes no ranking and revives no composition.
hypotheses.not_closed: THE FINDING THIS CYCLE PRODUCED OUTSIDE ITS OWN CRITERION, AND IT IS LARGER THAN THE ONE IT RULED. The three readings of the estimator are: one-sided at the published rate +7,017.0 us per step; TWO-sided at the same rate MINUS 1,668.5 us per step; one-sided at the class's own measured 1073.6 GB/s +7,548.0 us, two-sided there +110.1 us. Per step 2,253.3 kernels carry a positive residual and 1,193.7 a negative one. So the per-kernel residual is a distribution centred within about 110 us of zero once the reference is the class's own rate, and the 7,017.0 us the composition spends is the positive half of it. That is DISPERSION, not a systematic shortfall, and the per-kernel clamp is what converts one into the other: it manufactures an 8,685.5 us difference between the one-sided and two-sided readings of the same population. WHY THAT IS NOT RULED HERE. The frozen criterion asked whether DRAM traffic explains the excess. It does not, by 151.2 us. Ruling the dispersion finding under this cycle would be choosing a criterion after seeing the numbers, so it is recorded and named as the successor instead: whether the positive dispersion is collectible at all, or whether a kernel slower than its class mean is simply a different shape or dtype with a genuinely lower achievable rate, which no fusion collects. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. (1) The dispersion question above, which is 7,017.0 us of a 14,813.3 us lever -- 47% of it. (2) THE L2 TEST IS A WORKING-SET TEST, NOT A RESIDENCY MEASUREMENT: no L2 hit-rate counter exists in this build, a kernel under 72 MB can miss L2 because it shares the cache with everything in flight, and a kernel above it can hit on part of its traffic. The two errors run opposite ways and I cannot sign the net, which is why this cycle carries no one-directional bias argument where cycles 42 and 43 both did. (3) Register and shared-memory capacity remains entirely unmeasured, so cycle 43's 14,479.6 us credited to grouped kernels is still bounded from below only. (4) THE OPTIMIZER LEVER, 10,234.0 us, still has had no audit, and it is distance to a bandwidth floor computed under this same published rate -- which this cycle has now shown the class as a whole EXCEEDS by 6.5%, so the optimizer figure inherits the question directly. hypotheses.closing: Ruled SUPPORTED against a criterion frozen from the two audited lever values before the run, with the deliberate red proved before the cycle opened. The per-kernel clamp manufactures an 8,685.5 us difference between two readings of one population. events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. A single class-wide reference rate treats every elementwise kernel as having the same achievable bandwidth, and they do not. A [2048, 1024] add and a [4096, 32768] copy differ in access pattern, cache behaviour and achievable rate, and neither figure is a property a fusion changes except by changing the shape. So a residual measured against ONE class rate mixes two quantities. BETWEEN-SITE: this shape is slower than the class average -- a property of the shape, not overhead, collectible only by changing the shape. WITHIN-SITE: this INVOCATION is slower than other invocations of the SAME op on the SAME dims -- same work, same shape, different duration, and that is where per-kernel overhead would have to live if it lives anywhere. THE DISCRIMINATOR. Group kernels by SITE = (cpu_op name, recorded input dims), so every kernel in a site does the same work on the same shapes. Give each site its OWN mean duration as its reference and recompute the one-sided residual. A site's mean residual against its own mean is zero by construction, so what survives is exactly the positive half of WITHIN-SITE dispersion, with every shape-explained difference removed. The remainder of the priced 7,017.0 us is then the between-site part by subtraction. THE BIAS DIRECTION IS NAMED BEFORE THE RUN AND IT SPARES THE HYPOTHESIS THAT OVERHEAD EXISTS. Sites are formed from recorded input dims, so two genuinely different workloads sharing a dims string are merged into one site, which INFLATES within-site dispersion. Any finding that within-site dispersion is small is therefore conservative in the direction that would have preserved the lever. Single-invocation sites have zero within-site dispersion by construction and are excluded from the within-site figure and reported separately rather than scored as zero. WHAT A RESULT WOULD AND WOULD NOT LICENSE. A small within-site residual means the excess half is shape heterogeneity, and a fusion collects shape heterogeneity only by changing shapes -- which is the BYTE half of this same lever, already priced separately, so crediting it twice would be the double count the per-kernel cap was written to prevent. A large one does NOT establish that the dispersion is removable: scheduling, clock state, cache occupancy from neighbouring work and measurement noise all produce within-site dispersion. It bounds where overhead could be, never that it is there, and the artifact says so.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED IF the WITHIN-SITE one-sided residual, over multi-invocation sites only, EXCEEDS 4,579.3 us per step -- meaning most of the priced excess survives even after every site is judged against its own mean, so it is not shape-explained and the lever's excess half remains a candidate overhead quantity. THE THRESHOLD IS A ROUTE-SELECTION THRESHOLD AND IS STATED AS SUCH, on the same basis cycle 44 used and updated for the new lever value. The 1.5x question is settled: cycles 42 and 43 ruled the three-lever composition REFUTED and no further reduction of any lever can change that, so a threshold derived from 1.5x would be a criterion that cannot fail, which the loop forbids. The live question is which lever to pursue next, and the threshold that changes that answer reorders the two audited levers: elementwise stands at 14,813.3 us after cycle 44 and the optimizer at 10,234.0 us, so 4,579.3 us is the difference. ALSO REFUSED, independently of any residual, IF THE SITE GROUPING DEGENERATES: the instrument exits non-zero when less than 50% of class device time sits in sites with more than one invocation, because within-site dispersion is 0.0 by construction for a single-invocation site and a near-zero residual would read as "the excess is entirely shape heterogeneity" -- a FINDING that retires 7,017.0 us of the lever -- while being equally consistent with a site key that grouped nothing, a DEFECT. That is the branch proved red before this cycle opened, by keying each kernel on its own start timestamp. Sized coverage below 0.50 also refuses. I PREDICT SUPPORTED, and I am saying so before the run. The class's device time is dominated by a small number of repeated residual-stream and expert shapes invoked tens of times per step, and cycle 44 already showed the two-sided residual is within 110 us of zero against the class's own rate, which is what between-site heterogeneity plus a near-symmetric within-site spread would look like. If that is right the excess half is not overhead and the elementwise lever is materially smaller than 14,813.3 us -- a prediction that costs me, which is why it is registered rather than left unstated.
events.supported_if: SUPPORTED IF the within-site one-sided residual is at or below 4,579.3 us per step: the priced excess is dominated by BETWEEN-SITE heterogeneity, which is a property of the shapes rather than per-kernel overhead, and a fusion collects it only by changing shapes -- which the byte half of this same lever already prices. SUPPORTED therefore means the excess half is substantially not a separate removable quantity, and it does NOT mean the lever is sound. INCONCLUSIVE only if the run does not discriminate -- for instance if the multi-invocation share clears its floor but the sites carrying the excess are themselves nearly all single-invocation, so the partition is computed over a population that is not the one holding the quantity. Never for a number that is merely unwelcome, and explicitly never for a result matching the SUPPORTED prediction I just registered against my own lever.

Deliberate red PROVED BEFORE this cycle opened: --prove-red keys each kernel on its own start timestamp so every site has exactly one invocation, the multi-invocation share falls to 0.0000, and the instrument exits 2 rather than publish a within-site residual of zero. events.because: The frozen criterion was: REFUTED IF the within-site one-sided residual over multi-invocation sites EXCEEDS 4,579.3 us/step. The class partitions into 118 sites and 100.0% of class device time sits in multi-invocation sites, so the degeneracy refusal did not fire and the partition is computed over the whole population rather than a corner of it; single-invocation sites hold 0.0 us/step. events.hypothesis: WHAT THIS RETIRES, AND IT IS THE LARGEST SINGLE RETIREMENT OF THE AUDIT. A fusion collects between-site heterogeneity only by changing the shapes, and changing the shapes is exactly what the BYTE half of this same lever prices -- 13,703.8 us of eliminable intermediate traversals. Crediting the between-site excess as well charges the same mechanism twice, which is the double count the per-kernel cap in the original instrument was written to prevent and did not catch, because the cap bounds a kernel against its own duration and cannot see that its two halves name one act. So 5,697.9 us/step comes off: elementwise lever 14,813.3 -> 9,115.4 us/step; three-lever stack 41,907.4 -> 36,209.5 of the 54,586.7 required, short by 18,377.2, about 1.28x. THE RANKING FLIPS, WHICH IS WHAT THE THRESHOLD WAS FOR. The elementwise lever now stands BELOW the optimizer lever (9,115.4 against 10,234.0) for the first time in this campaign. Three cycles ago it was 19,105.6 and was the largest of the three. A DEFECT IN MY OWN FROZEN CRITERION, RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY PASSED. I froze the threshold against the SURVIVING within-site residual and labelled it "the threshold that reorders the two levers". The quantity that actually reorders them is the RETIRED amount, so the exact flip condition is within-site < 2,437.7 us/step, not <= 4,579.3. The two are not the same number and I wrote them as though they were. The measured 1,319.1 clears BOTH readings, so the verdict and the reordering both stand on the arithmetic rather than on the looser wording -- but a criterion whose stated meaning and stated number disagree is a defect even when the result is insensitive to it, and it would not have been insensitive at 3,000 us. WHAT SURVIVES AND IS NOT CLOSED. The 1,319.1 us/step of within-site dispersion is NOT established as removable overhead and this cycle does not claim it is. Scheduling, clock and power state, L2 occupancy from neighbouring work, and measurement noise all produce within-site dispersion, and no counter in this build separates them from per-kernel launch cost. The number bounds where overhead COULD live -- 1,319.1 us/step, 4.8% of the class device time -- and nothing more. Also untouched: sites are keyed on recorded input dims, so two genuinely different workloads sharing a dims string merge into one site and inflate the within-site figure, which means the true within-site dispersion is at or below 1,319.1 and the retirement is if anything understated. THE SUCCESSOR IS THE OPTIMIZER LEVER AND IT INHERITS THIS EXACT QUESTION. 10,234.0 us is the last of the three with no audit at all, and it is distance to a bandwidth floor computed under the same published 1008.0 GB/s reference that this class exceeds by 6.5%. A floor computed under a rate the hardware beats is not a floor, and after this cycle it is also the LARGEST remaining lever.

events.hypothesis: TWO EXPLANATIONS, WITH OPPOSITE CONSEQUENCES FOR EVERY LEVER THIS CAMPAIGN HAS PUBLISHED. OVER-COUNT: the byte model credited the kernel with more bytes than it moved, in which case every byte figure downstream is inflated -- including the 13,703.8 us eliminable-bytes half of the elementwise lever, which is the single largest quantity in the entire audit and larger than any lever now standing. CACHE SERVICE: the bytes are real but part of the traffic never reached DRAM, in which case the byte COUNT is right and what is wrong is pricing those bytes at a DRAM rate, because some of them cost cache time instead of memory time. Both are defects; they are different defects and they are repaired differently. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS A PHYSICAL PER-KERNEL BOUND, NOT A CORRELATION. At most the whole L2 can be serving one kernel, so its DRAM traffic is at least (bytes - 72 MiB) and its apparent rate can exceed peak by at most peak * bytes / (bytes - 72 MiB). A kernel that exceeds even that cannot be explained by cache at all and its byte count must be wrong. WHY THE BOUND DISCRIMINATES RATHER THAN MERELY BOUNDING. It is a function of SIZE. A 100 MiB tensor can be 72% resident and inflate enormously; a 1 GiB tensor can be at most 7% resident and inflate by 7.6%. So the same measured inflation is innocent at one size and impossible at another, and each kernel is judged against its own size rather than the class against one number. If the defect were a fixed multiplicative error in the byte formula it would show up as inflation that does not care about size, which is exactly what this bound catches. THE BIAS IS NAMED BEFORE THE RUN AND IT SPARES THE BYTE MODEL. The ceiling assumes the entire cache is dedicated to this one kernel and hits on every byte it holds, which nothing else in flight would permit. That is maximally generous to the cache reading, so the bound is built to make refutation easy. SUPPORTED here -- the byte model over-counts -- is therefore the STRONG direction, and REFUTED is the weak one. Same bias structure as cycles 42 and 43, pointing the same way.

REFUTED is the WEAK direction here, because the bound was deliberately built to be generous to exactly this explanation, and the artifact says so rather than reading a generous bound as a clean bill of health. ALSO REFUSED, independently of any share, IF THE ABOVE-PEAK POPULATION IS THIN: fewer than 10 movement kernels above the published peak. With no above-peak population the over-count share is 0% by construction, which reads as "the byte model is sound" -- a FINDING that would license every downstream byte figure in the campaign -- while meaning the selector found nothing to test, a DEFECT. Opposite in meaning, identical in arithmetic. That is the branch proved red before this cycle opened, by dropping every above-peak kernel from the population. I PREDICT REFUTED, in writing, before the run. The measured inflation is 1240.7 over 1008.0, a factor of 1.231, and a kernel can reach that under the cache reading whenever its working set is below about 384 MiB -- 72 MiB * 1.231 / 0.231. The large copies in this trace are checkpoint- and residual-scale rather than gigabyte-scale, so I expect most of them to sit under that size and be explained. I also expect that to be the LESS useful answer, because it leaves the byte counts standing while making the rate they are divided by wrong, which is harder to repair than a multiplier.

events.hypothesis: THE BOUND FALSIFIES A CONJUNCTION AND THE HYPOTHESIS NAMED ONLY ONE OF ITS TERMS. The ceiling assumes three things at once: the byte count is right, the kernel duration is right, and 1008.0 GB/s is this card's peak. Exceeding it falsifies their conjunction, not any single term. My hypothesis named the byte model, the criterion was frozen on it, and the verdict follows the criterion -- but the artifact does not get to convert that into a proof that bytes are the guilty term, and this update says so before anything downstream quotes it. THE MAGNITUDE POINTS AWAY FROM THE BYTES, AND THAT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING HERE. To bring 1240.7 under its 1084.2 ceiling the byte count would have to be inflated by a factor of 1.144. A byte model that miscounts traversals is wrong by a WHOLE TRAVERSAL -- 2x, 1.5x, 1.33x for two, three or four traversals counted as one more or one fewer. There is no traversal arithmetic that produces 14.4%. So the shape of the error does not look like the mechanism my own hypothesis named, and the term that would explain it cleanly is the REFERENCE: if this card sustains more than 1240.7 GB/s on a 1 GiB device-to-device copy, every one of these kernels is innocent and so is the byte model, and what is wrong is the specification figure the whole campaign divides by. The remaining candidates are memory compression on the copy path, a duration that the profiler under-reports for these specific kernels, or dims that over-state the tensor -- and this cycle distinguishes none of them. events.hypothesis: WHAT THE MODEL CHARGES, READ FROM ITS OWN SOURCE RATHER THAN ASSUMED. bytes_corrected for a movement op returns TRUE_TRAVERSALS[op] * max(sizes) -- for a copy, TWICE THE LARGEST recorded operand, not the sum of the operands. So 1,073,741,824 is 2 x a 512 MiB operand: one read and one write of the same-sized tensor. WHERE THAT FORMULA IS EXACT AND WHERE IT OVER-COUNTS. For a same-dtype copy source and destination are the same size and the kernel reads one and writes the other, so 2*max is exactly right. It over-counts precisely when the operands DIFFER in size, which is what a dtype-converting copy is: reading a bf16 source and writing an fp32 destination moves max + min, not 2*max. The maximum correction available from this mechanism is 2*max/(max+min), which for a bf16/fp32 pair is 1.333 and for equal operands is exactly 1.000. WHY THAT IS THE RIGHT DISCRIMINATOR FOR THIS QUESTION. Cycle 47 established that bringing 1240.7 under 1084.2 needs a factor of 1.144, and observed that no WHOLE-traversal miscount (2x, 1.5x, 1.33x) produces 14.4%. The operand-size mechanism is the one byte-side error that can produce a NON-integer ratio, because it depends on the dtype width ratio rather than on a traversal count. So it is the byte model's best remaining defence and its last chance to be the guilty term -- and testing it needs no bandwidth figure, no cache assumption and no occupancy counter, only the same trace read twice. THE BIAS, NAMED BEFORE THE RUN, AND IT POINTS AGAINST THE BYTES. The operand sum is a LOWER bound on real traffic: a strided or non-contiguous copy touches more than the sum of its operands, and a copy that also reads an index or mask touches more still. So the corrected rate computed here is an UPPER bound on the true achieved rate, which makes it HARDER for a kernel to fall under its ceiling. The substitution is therefore conservative against the traversal-count explanation, which means a SUPPORTED here would be the STRONG direction and this REFUTED, if it comes, is the weak one -- the opposite bias structure to cycles 42, 43 and 47, and the artifact says so rather than reading a conservative bound as a clean acquittal of the bytes.

For a PURE_MOVEMENT op bytes_eliminable RETURNS bytes_corrected, so those are equal and every sized pure-movement kernel is capped BY CONSTRUCTION -- not by measurement, and not by anything about this trace. events.observation: The FLOP census put 0.9105 of issued arithmetic at GEMM sites and called it eligible for a 2x tensor rate. That eligibility is a property of the SITE CLASS, not of the SHAPE. A contraction below the cards ridge point is bound by operand traffic, and doubling the arithmetic rate of a unit that is not the bottleneck shortens nothing.

events.hypothesis: If a material share of the 8.3854 TF at eligible sites sits at contractions whose arithmetic intensity is below the ridge, the precision route is bounded by shape rather than by precision, and the route selection changes again. If nearly all of it is above the ridge, precision is the binding lever and FP16 accumulation is the cheapest first arm.

events.supported_if: SUPPORTED if 0.75 or more of the resolved arithmetic is at or above the ridge, and the stricter twice-the-ridge margin still holds 0.60 or more -- the precision route is then bound by precision rather than by shape and FP16 accumulation is the cheapest untried arm.

events.because: The frozen criterion was REFUTED if less than 0.75 of the arithmetic resolved to a contraction sits at or above the ridge point of 163.9 FLOPs per byte. Measured at 0.9999 contraction coverage: 8.7143 of 9.5406 TF/step is at or above the ridge, a share of 0.913, and the stricter twice-the-ridge margin still holds 8.1989 TF/step at 0.859 against a supported-if floor of 0.60. Both clauses are met with margin. The 0.9105 site-class eligibility carries to the recorded SHAPES: the arithmetic that sits at GEMM sites also sits at contractions where the arithmetic pipe is the binding constraint under this model, so a 2x tensor rate is bounded by precision rather than by shape. The only traffic-bound arithmetic is attention at 56.9 FLOPs per byte -- and that figure is itself UNDER-stated, because the model charges traffic for a materialised seq x seq score matrix that a fused attention kernel never writes.

events.hypothesis: WHAT THE REFUSALS BOUGHT, AND WHAT THEY DID NOT CLOSE. The instrument refused TWICE before it reported, at 0.6005 and then 0.8328 against a 0.85 coverage floor frozen before the run. Neither refusal was answered by lowering the floor. The first was cured by modelling backward contractions from their forward counterparts -- a backward records only its incoming-gradient shape -- and the second by deriving attention as the TWO contractions it actually performs (QK_T at (b*h, s, d, s) and AV at (b*h, s, s, d)) rather than charging it one averaged shape, since averaging two intensities either side of the ridge reports a boundary neither sits at. The second refusal also gained a residual listing: a refusal that does not name what it could not resolve ends the inquiry instead of directing it, and naming attention as the whole 11,970 us/step residual is what made the third run one patch away. THIS DOES NOT SAY THE GEMMS CURRENTLY RUN AT PEAK. Above the ridge means the arithmetic pipe is the binding constraint in a roofline sense, so a faster pipe CAN shorten the kernel. It is silent on whether these kernels are near their achievable rate today -- occupancy, tile quantisation, wave tails and epilogue cost are all unmeasured, and no occupancy counter exists anywhere in this campaign. So a 2x rate is an UPPER bound on what the precision route returns on this 91.3%, never a prediction of it. WHAT IT LEAVES OPEN FOR THE PRECISION ROUTE. Which of the two 2x carriers actually applies at each of these contractions is untested: FP8 is INCONCLUSIVE (row contractions measured faster than bf16 at forward 0.796 and dX 0.629 at m=4096, arm slower end to end on the wrapper and one dW event 2.72x its siblings) and FP16 ACCUMULATION has never been attempted at all and needs a cublasLt CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F binding authored first. Nothing here adjudicates the #1413 loss bar for either. THE TAIL IS SMALL AND IS NOT ZERO. 0.8263 TF/step is traffic-bound, dominated by attention; mm at n=16 and n=1 and the two bmm rows are at 15.5, 1.0 and 0.7 FLOPs per byte and are rounding error in arithmetic while being real device time. aten::addmv_ at 10.7 us/step resolves no contraction at all.

events.observation: 91.3 percent of issued arithmetic is arithmetic-bound at the ridge, so a faster arithmetic pipe can shorten it, and bf16 does not fit the budget at any utilisation. Two carriers reach the published 2x rate on this card. FP8 is inconclusive. FP16 accumulation has never been attempted because torch does not expose the accumulator type -- torch.mm on half inputs always requests a 32F compute type, and the one precision harness in the tree binds _scaled_mm rather than cuBLASLt.

events.hypothesis: If cuBLASLt accepts CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F for these operands and the resulting kernels run materially faster than the fp32-accumulate reference at the six contractions holding the most device time, then the 2x carrier with the smaller learning risk is reachable and the arm is worth a governed window. If it rejects the compute type, or accepts it and delivers no rate, the carrier is closed and FP8 is the only 2x route left.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED if cuBLASLt rejects CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F at every one of the six measured shapes, OR if the median speedup over the fp32-accumulate reference across the accepting shapes is below 1.50x. The 1.50x line is arithmetic, not taste: at 60 percent end-to-end utilisation the measured 9.2100 TF/step costs 92.9 ms in bf16, and applying a speedup s to the 0.9105 eligible share gives 92.9 times (0.0895 plus 0.9105 over s), which is 64.7 ms at s equal to 1.5 and over the 51.2 ms budget. Below 1.5x this carrier cannot reach the terminal at a realistic utilisation.
events.supported_if: SUPPORTED if the compute type is accepted at the shapes holding the most device time and the median speedup is at or above 1.50x, with the relative L2 against the fp32-accumulate reference reported per shape and no tolerance asserted.

events.because: The frozen criterion was: REFUTED if cuBLASLt rejects CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F at every one of the six measured shapes, OR if the MEDIAN speedup over the fp32-accumulate reference across the accepting shapes is below 1.50x -- justified by the arithmetic that at 60 percent utilisation the measured 9.2100 TF/step costs 92.9 ms in bf16 and applying a speedup s to the 0.9105 eligible share gives 92.9 x (0.0895 + 0.9105/s). THE CRITERION IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT AND THIS RUN FELL IN THE GAP. All six shapes accepted the compute type, so the first clause is not met. The median is 1.5270x, which CLEARS the 1.50x line. But the arithmetic the criterion quotes to justify that line applies s to a SHARE OF DEVICE TIME, and the time-weighted speedup those same six measurements give is 33,138.4 -> 23,951.3 us/step = 1.3836x, which FAILS it. The statistic I froze does not answer the question the arithmetic I froze asks, so this run does not settle the route in either direction. Ruling SUPPORTED on the median would be selecting the favourable statistic after seeing the data, and ruling REFUTED on the time-weighted figure would be re-cutting a frozen criterion after seeing the data. The defect is mine and it is in the criterion, not in the measurement.

events.hypothesis: WHAT THIS RUN DID ESTABLISH, WHICH IS NOT NOTHING. (1) The binding exists: cuBLASLt is reachable by ctypes from the library torch itself loaded, and CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F is ACCEPTED at all six measured contractions on this card. The carrier is not closed by the API. (2) The accumulator is GENUINELY HALF, proved numerically rather than assumed: the 16F path differs from the fp32-accumulate reference by 1.68e-03 relative L2 at every shape, against 0.0 to 3.3e-05 for the 32F path -- a separation of roughly two orders of magnitude, which is what a half accumulator looks like and what a silent fallback cannot produce. (3) Four of six shapes gain materially: 1.512x, 1.553x, 1.724x, 1.542x. THE FINDING THAT QUALIFIES THIS MORNING SHAPE RESULT, AND IT IS THE VALUABLE ONE. At m=2048 k=1024 n=1024 the 16F accumulator is ACTIVE -- its relative L2 is the same 1.68e-03 as everywhere else -- and it delivers 0.997x. No speedup at all. That contraction sits at 409.6 FLOPs per byte, two and a half times the 163.9 ridge, so the roofline classed it arithmetic-bound and predicted a faster pipe would shorten it. It did not. At m=1024 k=1024 n=256 (170.7 FLOPs per byte, just above the ridge) the gain is 1.114x. SO THE 91.3 PERCENT ARITHMETIC-BOUND SHARE IS AN UPPER BOUND ON WHAT THE PRECISION ROUTE CAN TOUCH, NOT A PREDICTION OF IT. Being above the ridge is necessary and is not sufficient; the registry row for that cycle already said a 2x rate is an upper bound and never a prediction, and this is the first measurement that shows the gap is real and large. THE INSTRUMENT DEFECT, CURED. The printed median took sorted()[n//2] on an even-length list, which is the UPPER middle value: it read 1.5419x where the median is 1.5270x. Favourable direction, again. Cured in place, with the arithmetic-versus-statistic requirement written into the docstring so the successor cannot inherit it. WHAT IS NOT CLOSED. The six shapes are the top of the census, not the census: they hold 33,138.4 of 71,674.3 us/step of eligible-site time, so 54 percent of it is unmeasured and the grouped-expert backward, the attention path and the 4,608-kernel m=1024 n=256 row are all outside the probe. Nothing here adjudicates the #1413 loss bar -- the relative L2 figures are reported with NO tolerance asserted, and a half accumulator over a full training step is a different question from one over a single contraction. And this is an ISOLATED-SHAPE probe: the FP8 arm had faster row contractions and was slower end to end.

hypotheses.ruling: The frozen criterion was: REFUTED if cuBLASLt rejects CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F at every one of the six measured shapes, OR if the MEDIAN speedup over the fp32-accumulate reference across the accepting shapes is below 1.50x -- justified by the arithmetic that at 60 percent utilisation the measured 9.2100 TF/step costs 92.9 ms in bf16 and applying a speedup s to the 0.9105 eligible share gives 92.9 x (0.0895 + 0.9105/s). THE CRITERION IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT AND THIS RUN FELL IN THE GAP. All six shapes accepted the compute type, so the first clause is not met. The median is 1.5270x, which CLEARS the 1.50x line. But the arithmetic the criterion quotes to justify that line applies s to a SHARE OF DEVICE TIME, and the time-weighted speedup those same six measurements give is 33,138.4 -> 23,951.3 us/step = 1.3836x, which FAILS it. The statistic I froze does not answer the question the arithmetic I froze asks, so this run does not settle the route in either direction. Ruling SUPPORTED on the median would be selecting the favourable statistic after seeing the data, and ruling REFUTED on the time-weighted figure would be re-cutting a frozen criterion after seeing the data. The defect is mine and it is in the criterion, not in the measurement.
hypotheses.not_closed: WHAT THIS RUN DID ESTABLISH, WHICH IS NOT NOTHING. (1) The binding exists: cuBLASLt is reachable by ctypes from the library torch itself loaded, and CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F is ACCEPTED at all six measured contractions on this card. The carrier is not closed by the API. (2) The accumulator is GENUINELY HALF, proved numerically rather than assumed: the 16F path differs from the fp32-accumulate reference by 1.68e-03 relative L2 at every shape, against 0.0 to 3.3e-05 for the 32F path -- a separation of roughly two orders of magnitude, which is what a half accumulator looks like and what a silent fallback cannot produce. (3) Four of six shapes gain materially: 1.512x, 1.553x, 1.724x, 1.542x. THE FINDING THAT QUALIFIES THIS MORNING SHAPE RESULT, AND IT IS THE VALUABLE ONE. At m=2048 k=1024 n=1024 the 16F accumulator is ACTIVE -- its relative L2 is the same 1.68e-03 as everywhere else -- and it delivers 0.997x. No speedup at all. That contraction sits at 409.6 FLOPs per byte, two and a half times the 163.9 ridge, so the roofline classed it arithmetic-bound and predicted a faster pipe would shorten it. It did not. At m=1024 k=1024 n=256 (170.7 FLOPs per byte, just above the ridge) the gain is 1.114x. SO THE 91.3 PERCENT ARITHMETIC-BOUND SHARE IS AN UPPER BOUND ON WHAT THE PRECISION ROUTE CAN TOUCH, NOT A PREDICTION OF IT. Being above the ridge is necessary and is not sufficient; the registry row for that cycle already said a 2x rate is an upper bound and never a prediction, and this is the first measurement that shows the gap is real and large. THE INSTRUMENT DEFECT, CURED. The printed median took sorted()[n//2] on an even-length list, which is the UPPER middle value: it read 1.5419x where the median is 1.5270x. Favourable direction, again. Cured in place, with the arithmetic-versus-statistic requirement written into the docstring so the successor cannot inherit it. WHAT IS NOT CLOSED. The six shapes are the top of the census, not the census: they hold 33,138.4 of 71,674.3 us/step of eligible-site time, so 54 percent of it is unmeasured and the grouped-expert backward, the attention path and the 4,608-kernel m=1024 n=256 row are all outside the probe. Nothing here adjudicates the #1413 loss bar -- the relative L2 figures are reported with NO tolerance asserted, and a half accumulator over a full training step is a different question from one over a single contraction. And this is an ISOLATED-SHAPE probe: the FP8 arm had faster row contractions and was slower end to end.
hypotheses.closing: Ruled INCONCLUSIVE against a criterion whose statistic and whose arithmetic disagree across the decision line. The successor carries a TIME-WEIGHTED criterion over the whole eligible share, frozen before its own run, so the gap cannot recur. The binding, the numerical proof that the accumulator is genuinely half, and the above-the-ridge-yet-no-gain finding all stand and are registered.

events.hypothesis: WHAT THIS REFUTATION DOES NOT CLOSE. It does not close FP8, which stands INCONCLUSIVE with row contractions measured FASTER than bf16 (forward 0.796, dX 0.629 at m=4096) and an arm slower end to end on the wrapper plus one dW event 2.72x its siblings -- a different carrier with a different failure mode, and this result says nothing about it. It does not close the combination of FP16 accumulation with anything else: 1.3591x composed with the 1.828x scheduling floor is not 1.3591x, and no measurement here speaks to whether they contend. And it adjudicates no loss bar: the relative differences above are reported as accumulator IDENTITY evidence with no tolerance asserted, so #1413 is untouched. THE FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE VERDICT. Five of thirteen contractions, holding 8,531.0 us/step or 19.8 percent of the timed set, gain nothing: m=2048 k=1024 n=1024 at 1.008x (409.6 FLOPs/byte), m=1024 k=32768 n=1024 at 0.970x (504.1), m=1024 k=256 n=1024 at 0.929x (170.7), and two small rows.
