THAT is the measurement the next cycle should be about, because it governs every remaining precision candidate rather than one carrier. FOUR INSTRUMENT DEFECTS, ALL FOUND BY ITS OWN GATES BEFORE ANY RATE WAS PUBLISHED, AND ONE OF THEM WAS AN OVER-CORRECTION OF ANOTHER. (a) The timing-agreement gate was symmetric and relative, so it refused on four small-output shapes where cuBLASLt was FASTER than torch by 5 to 11 us -- one dispatch, constant in absolute terms. Repaired directionally, which is stricter where a real defect would show. (b) That gate ran FIRST and pre-empted the deliberate red, so the red exited at a timing check instead of at the discriminator it exists to prove -- the identical defect the predecessor harness was repaired for one day earlier. Numerical gates now run first. (c) Each shape was timed ONCE; per-shape factors move by up to 0.21x on identical work, so timing is now 5 interleaved repeats with the spread reported and the estimator applied symmetrically to both arms. (d) The discriminator went through three forms and THE MIDDLE ONE WAS WORSE THAN THE FIRST: against torch fp16 it certified 12 of 13 shapes and failed at k=32768 on torch split-K ordering; against a common fp32 product it certified only 3 of 13, because both paths then pay the same 2.08e-04 fp16 output rounding as a common-mode term. The form that works removes the third party entirely -- 16F output against 32F output of the same binding, floor at the fp16 rounding unit 2**-11, derived from the format and not fitted to any observation.

events.observation: The time-weighted FP16 cycle closed REFUTED at 1.3591x and left behind a finding that governs more than the carrier it came from. Five of thirteen timed contractions -- 8,531.0 us/step, 19.8% of the timed set -- gained NOTHING from a demonstrably active half accumulator, and the roofline had classed every one of them arithmetic-bound, two of them at 2.5x and 3.1x the 163.9 FLOPs/byte ridge. m=2048 k=1024 n=1024 sits at 409.6 F/B and returns 1.008x. m=4096 k=1024 n=1024 sits at 455.1 F/B and returns 1.647x. Those two differ in m alone. So being above the ridge is NECESSARY and NOT SUFFICIENT, and the 91.3% arithmetic-bound share measured this morning is an UPPER BOUND on what any precision carrier can reach rather than a prediction of it. Every remaining precision candidate on this campaign -- FP8 included -- is sized against that share, so what actually decides the difference is worth more than the carrier that exposed it.

events.hypothesis: CANDIDATE MECHANISM: machine fill. A GEMM is tiled into T_m x T_n output tiles, each one CTA. This card has 128 SMs. A contraction producing fewer CTAs than that leaves SMs idle outright; one producing barely more runs a single wave plus a ragged tail. In either case the kernel is bounded by how much of the machine it occupies and by a prologue and epilogue it has no other wave to hide behind -- neither of which the arithmetic pipe's RATE touches. Doubling the rate of a pipe that is not saturated does nothing. CTAs = ceil(m/T_m) * ceil(n/T_n) is computable from shapes already recorded, so this needs no card, no counter and no profile. WHAT IS PREMISED: the tile. cuBLASLt selects it per shape and this instrument cannot observe that choice, so the claim is required to hold at THREE canonical tiles or it is a property of one guessed tile. WHAT IS MEASURED: the speedups and device times, from the rate receipt. THE PRIOR THIS GUARDS AGAINST: registry row the-empty-program-is-free-on-the-grouped-forward-and-costs-8-2-us-on-dw-20260915 records me reading a CTA count on 128 SMs as an occupancy win -- 384 programs against 1,536 -- and a 2x2 refuting it, with the grid term positive in both directions and the whole effect belonging to a different lever. A CTA count is a quantity that looks explanatory and has already misled this campaign once, which is why the criterion below carries a rival clause rather than only a separation clause.

events.refuted_if:
REFUTED if machine fill, computed as CTAs/128 from the recorded m and n, fails to separate the two groups at ANY of the three canonical tiles 128x128, 128x64 and 64x64 -- that is, if the MINIMUM wave count among contractions gaining 1.40x or more is not strictly above the MAXIMUM wave count among those gaining under 1.10x. Requiring it at all three tiles is what stops the result being a property of a tile I guessed.

ALSO REFUTED, and this is the clause that matters more, if any RIVAL quantity separates the same two groups just as cleanly: kernel duration, total FLOPs, output elements m*n, arithmetic intensity, contraction depth k, or census weight us/step, each asked in EITHER direction. A separation that a correlated quantity would also have produced explains nothing and cannot direct a measurement. The prior row above is exactly what an unguarded separation looks like when it is wrong.

SUPPORTED requires BOTH: fill separates at every tile AND no rival separates at all. Anything else -- fill separates but a rival does too, or fill separates at two tiles of three -- is at most INCONCLUSIVE, and the verdict will say which clause failed.

WHAT A SUPPORTED VERDICT WOULD AND WOULD NOT LICENSE. It would NOT prove the mechanism. Achieved occupancy, register pressure, shared-memory footprint, split-K decisions and the actually-selected tile are all unmeasured, and no counter for any of them exists anywhere in this campaign. It would license exactly one thing: that an occupancy measurement is the next instrument worth building, rather than one guess among several. That is a claim about where to point, and the criterion is frozen here, before the instrument runs, in both directions.

events.because:
THE MEASUREMENT IS CLEAN AND MY CRITERION IS NOT, SO THE VERDICT IS INCONCLUSIVE AND THE DEFECT IS MINE -- FOR THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE CYCLE.

What the instrument found. Machine fill separates the two groups at ALL THREE canonical tiles, with the same factor-of-two gap at each: 128x128 gaining 2.00-16.00 waves against flat 0.06-1.00; 128x64 gaining 4.00-32.00 against flat 0.06-2.00; 64x64 gaining 8.00-64.00 against flat 0.12-4.00. The boundary is MORE THAN ONE FULL WAVE of CTAs, and it does not depend on which tile is premised. The deliberate red -- the measured speedups reassigned in reverse rank, so the labels scramble while every geometric quantity stays exactly as measured -- refuses at all three tiles.

And the rival check, which is worth more than the separation: ARITHMETIC INTENSITY DOES NOT ORDER THESE GROUPS. Gaining spans 455.1-646.7 FLOPs/byte and the flat group includes 504.1 and 409.6, sitting INSIDE that range. Nor does kernel duration -- gaining spans 0.0586-0.435 ms and a flat shape sits at 0.409. Nor total FLOPs, nor contraction depth k, nor census weight. The roofline own variable fails to predict which contractions a faster arithmetic pipe shortens, and the count of output tiles succeeds.

WHY THIS IS NOT RULED SUPPORTED. The criterion I froze says two things that cannot both be applied: 'ALSO REFUTED ... if any RIVAL quantity separates the same two groups just as cleanly', and then 'Anything else ... is at most INCONCLUSIVE'. One rival did separate -- output elements m*n -- so the first clause says REFUTED and the second says INCONCLUSIVE, and the frozen text does not decide between them.

I also know which answer I would prefer, which is exactly why I am not taking it. m*n is not an independent rival: waves is ceil(m/T_m)*ceil(n/T_n)/SMs, a monotone function of m*n up to tile rounding, so it separates whenever fill does and its agreement is arithmetic rather than evidence. That is true, it was true before the instrument ran, and I only wrote it down AFTER the first red run showed the column fire. Excluding a rival from the frozen list after watching it fire is selecting the criterion to fit the data -- the identical move I refused in the FP16 cycle four hours ago and ruled INCONCLUSIVE for.

SO: INCONCLUSIVE, on the ground that the frozen criterion is internally inconsistent, not that the measurement failed. The measurement did not fail. Every number above stands on its own and none of it is withdrawn.

TWO INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT CRITERIA IN TWO CONSECUTIVE CYCLES IS A MECHANISM DEBT, NOT CARELESSNESS. Both have one shape: I wrote the criterion as PROSE, and prose admits two readings that only diverge once real numbers arrive. The cure is not more careful prose. It is that the instrument must COMPUTE and PRINT the verdict token from the frozen clauses, so the verdict is produced by code before I read any of it and cannot be adjudicated by interpretation afterwards. Applied to this instrument the same turn, so the successor inherits it.

events.hypothesis:
WHAT THIS CYCLE ESTABLISHED, INDEPENDENT OF THE VERDICT WORD.

1. ARITHMETIC INTENSITY DOES NOT PREDICT PRECISION GAIN AT THESE SITES, AND OUTPUT SIZE DOES. That is the campaign-level consequence and it is larger than the carrier that exposed it. Every precision candidate still standing -- FP8 above all -- has been sized against the morning 91.3% arithmetic-bound share, a figure computed entirely from FLOPs per byte. This cycle says that share is an upper bound on reach and not a prediction of it, and names the variable that does the predicting instead. Any future FP8 ceiling quoting an intensity-derived eligible share without a machine-fill filter is quoting a number this cycle has already shown over-predicts.

2. THE BOUNDARY IS ONE FULL WAVE, AND IT IS TILE-INVARIANT. Flat maxes at exactly one wave and gaining minimums at exactly two, at every premised tile. The invariance is what makes it worth anything: the tile is the one premise this instrument cannot observe, and the result does not depend on it.

WHAT IS NOT CLOSED.

3. THE MECHANISM IS NOT IDENTIFIED AND NO SHAPE ARITHMETIC CAN IDENTIFY IT. Machine fill and any other cost scaling with output size -- epilogue work per output element, store traffic, write-allocate behaviour -- are indistinguishable by construction here, because both are functions of m*n. hypotheses.explanation: CANDIDATE MECHANISM: machine fill. A GEMM is tiled into T_m x T_n output tiles, each one CTA. This card has 128 SMs. A contraction producing fewer CTAs than that leaves SMs idle outright; one producing barely more runs a single wave plus a ragged tail. In either case the kernel is bounded by how much of the machine it occupies and by a prologue and epilogue it has no other wave to hide behind -- neither of which the arithmetic pipe's RATE touches. Doubling the rate of a pipe that is not saturated does nothing. CTAs = ceil(m/T_m) * ceil(n/T_n) is computable from shapes already recorded, so this needs no card, no counter and no profile. WHAT IS PREMISED: the tile. cuBLASLt selects it per shape and this instrument cannot observe that choice, so the claim is required to hold at THREE canonical tiles or it is a property of one guessed tile. events.because:

The largest jump is +0.236x (m=2048 -> m=2304) and the runner-up is +0.234x (m=1024 -> m=1536). 0.236 is 1.009x the runner-up, not 1.6x. What survives is the weaker and better-supported statement: the gain from a faster accumulator rises with output elements, smoothly, across a 32-fold range of m.

events.hypothesis:
WHAT THIS REFUTATION DOES NOT CLOSE.

(1) THE m=2048 DIP, which is the only thing in the data that behaves like a boundary effect and which the frozen test could not see. The sweep reads 1.658x at m=1792 (0.88 waves), then 1.007x at m=2048 (exactly 1.00 waves), then 1.244x at m=2304 (1.12 waves). That is a fall of -0.651x and a recovery, sitting precisely at the one-wave boundary -- and the dominance test ranks RISES, so a sharp DIP is invisible to it by construction. It is a single point, the 16F timing spread over five repeats reaches 36%, and -0.651x is far outside that spread, so noise is an unlikely but unmeasured explanation -- no repeat-level statistic was frozen for it. The next cycle measures the neighbourhood of m=2048 densely (2016, 2032, 2048, 2064, 2080) with a pre-registered outlier criterion, and it must ask whether the dip tracks the CTA count crossing 128 or tracks m crossing a power of two, because at this tile those two coincide exactly and nothing here separates them.

The ramp is consistent with epilogue work, store traffic and write-allocate behaviour, and equally consistent with anything else monotone in m. No byte of device-memory traffic has been measured in this campaign; the store-traffic reading is a hypothesis with no counter behind it.

The frozen criterion said verbatim: 'REFUTED if at EITHER shape fewer than 0.50 of the copies are matched by an add within the adjacency window. The two ops are then not a producer/consumer pair, the byte-eliminating fusion does not apply at these sites, and the 7,017 us ceiling stands as the honest figure for this class.'

At [3072,1024]: 344 copies, 232 adds, 158 matched within 50 us = 0.459 of copies. That is below 0.50 and the clause fires. At [1024,3072]: 172 copies, 116 adds, 109 matched = 0.634, which is in the middle band, but the criterion is EITHER-shape and one shape is enough. The instrument computed REFUTED from the same clauses before the table was printed and the receipt carries the token.

The counts also fail the balance half independently, and by the same ratio at both shapes: 344/232 and 172/116 are both 1.483. Copies outnumber adds by three to two at each site, so even if every add were matched the population cannot be one producer feeding one consumer.

So the byte-eliminating fusion does not apply at these four sites, and the elementwise class ceiling stays 7,017.0 us/step of device time unexplained by bytes rather than rising to the 6,433.2 us the not-closed line left open.
hypotheses.not_closed:
WHAT THE REFUTATION DOES AND DOES NOT CLOSE.

It closes the specific proposition that a copy_/add_ pair at these two shapes is a producer feeding a single consumer whose intermediate a fusion could delete. It does NOT close the elementwise lever generally, and it does not say these sites are cheap.

(1) THE 3:2 COUNT RATIO IS ITSELF UNEXPLAINED AND IS THE STRONGEST NEW THREAD. 344 copies to 232 adds at [3072,1024] and 172 to 116 at [1024,3072] -- identical ratio, exactly 1.483, at two different shapes. A coincidence of shape would not reproduce a ratio. Something structural issues three copies for every two adds at both sites and nothing here identifies it. The cheap next read is the source at the captured commit, not another trace pass.

(2) MY OWN RED IS DEGENERATE ON THE ADJACENCY CLAUSE, AND I FOUND THAT ONLY BY READING BOTH LEGS. The red forces every timestamp to 0.0, which makes every add trivially adjacent to every copy -- so the red reported a HIGHER matched fraction (0.674) than the real run (0.459), and it held only because the count-balance clause failed. A red that raises the quantity it is meant to destroy is not exercising the clause it was written for. The adjacency clause therefore has no proven red, and the cure is a red that scatters timestamps rather than collapsing them.

(3) THE DURATIONS HERE ARE NOT THE PRIOR ROW'S DURATIONS AND THE GAP IS NOT ADJUDICATED. This instrument sums the trace's `dur` field on aten:: operator events: 626.8 + 532.7 + 324.4 + 197.8 = 1,681.7 us per census window. The row that sent me here cites 6,433.2 us of DEVICE time at the same four sites. Those are different quantities read from the same trace -- host-side operator duration against attributed kernel time -- and which one belongs in a fusion estimate is not settled by this run. Neither is quoted as a governed number; the trace was captured under profiling instrumentation.

(4) THE CENSUS WINDOW COUNT DOES NOT DIVIDE THE POPULATION. 344, 232, 172 and 116 are none of them multiples of the 6 windows passed on the command line, so the per-step figures above are averages over a population that is not uniform per step, or the window count is wrong. The counts are the measured quantity; the per-step division is a presentation and is the weaker half of the table.

(5) NOTHING ABOUT REMOVABILITY WAS EVER REACHABLE HERE and the prediction said so before the run. A trace records no dataflow. This refutes a necessary condition, which is why a negative is decisive and a positive would not have been.

NO GATE MOVES. No occupancy, register-pressure, shared-memory or split-K counter exists in this build or anywhere in this campaign. One capture, one process, no matched-run variation.
hypotheses.closing: Ruled REFUTED against the frozen criterion: at [3072,1024] 158 of 344 copies matched an adjacent add, 0.459 against the 0.50 floor, and the counts fail balance at both shapes by the same 1.483 ratio. The instrument computed the same token before its table was read. The byte-eliminating fusion does not apply at these four sites and the elementwise ceiling stays 7,017.0 us/step. Carried forward as not-closed: the unexplained 3:2 copy-to-add ratio, a degenerate red on the adjacency clause, and an unreconciled host-versus-device duration basis.

The cycle closed minutes ago found that every lever this campaign has MEASURED -- all device idle, all elementwise time unexplained by bytes, and the FP16 contraction saving -- stacks to 1.7000x against the 3.4217x gate A needs. All three are the same KIND of lever: they run the same computational graph faster or with fewer gaps. The operator's distinction names the other kind, changing the graph so the same learning objective needs less work, and no cycle in this campaign has ever measured a candidate of that kind.

One is already half-visible in a landed receipt. optimizer-state-bytes-20260914T2041Z records, as an observation it explicitly did not investigate, that 844 of the 1,195 parameters in the optimizer param group have NEVER TAKEN A STEP at this head -- audio, image, all 14 router tensors, and experts 2 through 24, two of which the counter receipt lists as ACTIVE. It sized the stepped population at 474 M elements rather than 702 M, and then said in as many words that whether those tensors are meant to be receiving gradients is a separate question with a separate owner. With no second seat, that owner is me.

The registry query on this proposition's own nouns -- padding, masked positions, processed positions, redundant work, param groups never stepped -- returns nothing at all, and the source grep returns only membership constructions, no prior instrument.

events.hypothesis:
A parameter that never takes an optimizer step has no use for a gradient. If the backward computes one anyway, the arithmetic that produced it is device work that changes nothing: not work scheduled badly, not work in the wrong precision, but work that does not need to exist. Removing it is a change to the computational graph, which is the class of lever the stack result says the campaign must now find.

torch's autograd engine emits exactly one AccumulateGrad node per leaf tensor that actually receives a gradient in a backward pass. Counting them per optimizer step and comparing against the 351 tensors that carry AdamW state answers the question directly, from a trace already on disk, with no model of what the backward ought to do and no card.

SUPPORTED if AccumulateGrad nodes per optimizer step exceed 1.20 times the stepped tensor count read from optimizer-state-bytes-20260914T2041Z. The backward then produces gradients for parameters nothing updates, and that work is removable by construction.

REFUTED if the ratio is at or below 1.05. Essentially every gradient the backward produces belongs to a parameter that is stepped and there is no work-removal lever at this site.

INCONCLUSIVE between the two lines, or if the optimizer receipt carries no stepped_set_composition, or if the trace carries no Optimizer.step# annotation to divide by.

THE DENOMINATOR IS DELIBERATELY THE LARGEST PLAUSIBLE ONE. Every distinct Optimizer.step# timestamp counts as a step, so if the profiler emits more than one annotation per real step the per-step figure and the ratio are UNDERSTATED -- the direction that argues AGAINST this hypothesis. My own record says both of my errors on an unwanted result ran favourable, so the bias is chosen against the result I expect rather than left to chance.

A one-element router tensor and a 33 M element expert weight each produce exactly one AccumulateGrad. A positive establishes that gradient work EXISTS for parameters nothing updates; it does not size that work, state a ceiling, license an arm, or produce a figure for what removing it would save. Sizing needs the per-tensor element counts joined to the backward contractions that produce them, which is a separate instrument that does not exist.

Whether those tensors are MEANT to be frozen at this head is a question about the training contract, and a frozen tensor that still receives a gradient is a defect while a tensor deliberately held out of the optimizer may be correct. The frozen criterion said verbatim: 'SUPPORTED if AccumulateGrad nodes per optimizer step exceed 1.20 times the stepped tensor count read from optimizer-state-bytes-20260914T2041Z. The backward then produces gradients for parameters nothing updates, and that work is removable by construction.'

5,364 AccumulateGrad nodes over 12 distinct Optimizer.step# annotations is 447.0 per step against 351 tensors carrying AdamW state: ratio 1.2735, above the 1.20 line. Ninety-six tensors per optimizer step receive a gradient that no optimizer state consumes. The instrument computed the same token from the same clauses before its tables were printed.

THE MARGIN IS NARROW AND IS REPORTED AS NARROW. 1.2735 clears 1.20 by 0.07, not by a factor. A denominator of 6 rather than 12 real steps would put the ratio at 2.55 and a denominator of 24 at 0.64, which is the REFUTED side -- so the verdict depends on the step count being what the annotations say it is. The instrument takes every distinct Optimizer.step# timestamp as a step, which is the largest plausible denominator and therefore the smallest plausible ratio; a profiler emitting more than one annotation per real step makes the true ratio LARGER, not smaller. The bias was chosen before the run against the result I expected, because my own record says both of my errors on an unwanted result ran favourable.

BOTH BRANCHES WERE PROVED REACHABLE. Dropping every AccumulateGrad reports REFUTED; collapsing the denominator to one step reports SUPPORTED at 15.28.

events.hypothesis:
WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES. The backward at this head produces gradients for about 96 tensors per optimizer step that carry no AdamW state and therefore take no step. That arithmetic is device work whose output is discarded. It is the first candidate this campaign has measured in the class the lever-stack result said it must now find: work that does not need to exist, rather than work that is scheduled badly or executed in the wrong precision.

WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH, AND THE FIRST ITEM IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS.

(1) IT SIZES NOTHING. The instrument counts TENSORS. A one-element router tensor and a 33 M element expert weight each produce exactly one AccumulateGrad, so 96 tensors could be microseconds or could be a large share of the backward, and nothing here distinguishes those. No ceiling is stated, no arm is licensed, and no figure for what removal would save exists. The successor is the instrument that joins these 96 to their element counts and to the backward contractions that produce them -- that is where a ceiling would come from and it does not exist yet.

(2) WHICH 96 IS UNKNOWN. The receipt names none of them. 844 tensors never step, so 748 of them correctly receive no gradient and 96 do; the split is measured and the membership is not. The optimizer receipt's own list of groups with no state -- audio, image, all 14 router tensors, experts 2 through 24 -- is where to look, and the routers are the obvious suspect because routing output is consumed by the forward whether or not the router learns.

(3) IT IS NOT A RULING THAT ANYTHING IS MISCONFIGURED, and that was registered before the run. A tensor deliberately held out of the optimizer while still receiving gradients may be exactly what the training contract intends; a tensor meant to be frozen that still computes gradients is a defect. This cycle measures which gradients exist and adjudicates neither, because the adjudication is a question about the learning contract.

(4) THE MARGIN DEPENDS ON THE STEP COUNT. 1.2735 clears the frozen 1.20 by 0.07. The denominator is 12 distinct Optimizer.step# annotations and the census elsewhere treats this trace as 6 windows; if 12 annotations are 6 real steps the ratio is 2.55, and if they are 24 the ratio is 0.64 and the verdict inverts. The chosen denominator is the largest plausible one and therefore the most conservative, but reconciling the annotation count against the real step count is owed and is not done here.

(5) NO RATE, NO SHARE, NO GATE. The trace was captured under profiling instrumentation and this instrument quotes no duration at all. No occupancy, register-pressure, shared-memory or split-K counter exists in this build or anywhere in this campaign. One capture, one process, no matched-run variation.

hypotheses.observation:
The cycle closed minutes ago found that every lever this campaign has MEASURED -- all device idle, all elementwise time unexplained by bytes, and the FP16 contraction saving -- stacks to 1.7000x against the 3.4217x gate A needs. All three are the same KIND of lever: they run the same computational graph faster or with fewer gaps. The operator's distinction names the other kind, changing the graph so the same learning objective needs less work, and no cycle in this campaign has ever measured a candidate of that kind.

One is already half-visible in a landed receipt. optimizer-state-bytes-20260914T2041Z records, as an observation it explicitly did not investigate, that 844 of the 1,195 parameters in the optimizer param group have NEVER TAKEN A STEP at this head -- audio, image, all 14 router tensors, and experts 2 through 24, two of which the counter receipt lists as ACTIVE. It sized the stepped population at 474 M elements rather than 702 M, and then said in as many words that whether those tensors are meant to be receiving gradients is a separate question with a separate owner. With no second seat, that owner is me.

The registry query on this proposition's own nouns -- padding, masked positions, processed positions, redundant work, param groups never stepped -- returns nothing at all, and the source grep returns only membership constructions, no prior instrument.
hypotheses.explanation:
A parameter that never takes an optimizer step has no use for a gradient. If the backward computes one anyway, the arithmetic that produced it is device work that changes nothing: not work scheduled badly, not work in the wrong precision, but work that does not need to exist. Removing it is a change to the computational graph, which is the class of lever the stack result says the campaign must now find.

torch's autograd engine emits exactly one AccumulateGrad node per leaf tensor that actually receives a gradient in a backward pass. Counting them per optimizer step and comparing against the 351 tensors that carry AdamW state answers the question directly, from a trace already on disk, with no model of what the backward ought to do and no card.
hypotheses.criterion:
The criterion is computed IN CODE and printed as a verdict token before the tables are read. This states the same clauses in prose so a reader can check the implementation against them.

SUPPORTED if AccumulateGrad nodes per optimizer step exceed 1.20 times the stepped tensor count read from optimizer-state-bytes-20260914T2041Z. The backward then produces gradients for parameters nothing updates, and that work is removable by construction.

REFUTED if the ratio is at or below 1.05. Essentially every gradient the backward produces belongs to a parameter that is stepped and there is no work-removal lever at this site.

INCONCLUSIVE between the two lines, or if the optimizer receipt carries no stepped_set_composition, or if the trace carries no Optimizer.step# annotation to divide by.

THE DENOMINATOR IS DELIBERATELY THE LARGEST PLAUSIBLE ONE. Every distinct Optimizer.step# timestamp counts as a step, so if the profiler emits more than one annotation per real step the per-step figure and the ratio are UNDERSTATED -- the direction that argues AGAINST this hypothesis. My own record says both of my errors on an unwanted result ran favourable, so the bias is chosen against the result I expect rather than left to chance.

THIS COUNTS TENSORS, NOT ELEMENTS AND NOT MICROSECONDS, and that is registered before the run so a SUPPORTED cannot be read as more than it is. A one-element router tensor and a 33 M element expert weight each produce exactly one AccumulateGrad. A positive establishes that gradient work EXISTS for parameters nothing updates; it does not size that work, state a ceiling, license an arm, or produce a figure for what removing it would save. Sizing needs the per-tensor element counts joined to the backward contractions that produce them, which is a separate instrument that does not exist.

IT IS ALSO NOT A RULING THAT ANYTHING IS MISCONFIGURED. Whether those tensors are MEANT to be frozen at this head is a question about the training contract, and a frozen tensor that still receives a gradient is a defect while a tensor deliberately held out of the optimizer may be correct. This cycle measures which gradients exist and adjudicates neither.

WHAT NO OUTCOME LICENSES. No rate: the trace was captured UNDER PROFILING INSTRUMENTATION and this instrument quotes no duration at all. No occupancy, register-pressure, shared-memory or split-K counter exists in this build or anywhere in this campaign. One capture, one process, no matched-run variation. No model contract changes, no applied position, and no gate moves either way.

hypotheses.not_closed:
WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES. The backward at this head produces gradients for about 96 tensors per optimizer step that carry no AdamW state and therefore take no step. That arithmetic is device work whose output is discarded. It is the first candidate this campaign has measured in the class the lever-stack result said it must now find: work that does not need to exist, rather than work that is scheduled badly or executed in the wrong precision.

WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH, AND THE FIRST ITEM IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS.

(1) IT SIZES NOTHING. The instrument counts TENSORS. A one-element router tensor and a 33 M element expert weight each produce exactly one AccumulateGrad, so 96 tensors could be microseconds or could be a large share of the backward, and nothing here distinguishes those. No ceiling is stated, no arm is licensed, and no figure for what removal would save exists. The successor is the instrument that joins these 96 to their element counts and to the backward contractions that produce them -- that is where a ceiling would come from and it does not exist yet.

(2) WHICH 96 IS UNKNOWN. The receipt names none of them. 844 tensors never step, so 748 of them correctly receive no gradient and 96 do; the split is measured and the membership is not. The optimizer receipt's own list of groups with no state -- audio, image, all 14 router tensors, experts 2 through 24 -- is where to look, and the routers are the obvious suspect because routing output is consumed by the forward whether or not the router learns.

(3) IT IS NOT A RULING THAT ANYTHING IS MISCONFIGURED, and that was registered before the run. A tensor deliberately held out of the optimizer while still receiving gradients may be exactly what the training contract intends; a tensor meant to be frozen that still computes gradients is a defect. This cycle measures which gradients exist and adjudicates neither, because the adjudication is a question about the learning contract.

(4) THE MARGIN DEPENDS ON THE STEP COUNT. 1.2735 clears the frozen 1.20 by 0.07. The denominator is 12 distinct Optimizer.step# annotations and the census elsewhere treats this trace as 6 windows; if 12 annotations are 6 real steps the ratio is 2.55, and if they are 24 the ratio is 0.64 and the verdict inverts. The chosen denominator is the largest plausible one and therefore the most conservative, but reconciling the annotation count against the real step count is owed and is not done here.

(5) NO RATE, NO SHARE, NO GATE. The trace was captured under profiling instrumentation and this instrument quotes no duration at all. No occupancy, register-pressure, shared-memory or split-K counter exists in this build or anywhere in this campaign. One capture, one process, no matched-run variation.

The rival explanation is that the two names mark different, non-overlapping work, in which case their sum is a legitimate count of gradient-related nodes and the predecessor's unit stands.

A third event name containing the substring would have made the two-class model wrong and the instrument refuses on one; there is none.

SO THE PUBLISHED RATIO WAS DOUBLE. On the engine-node unit the backward performs 235.5 gradient accumulations per optimizer step against 351 tensors carrying AdamW state: ratio 0.6709. On the inner-op unit it is 211.5 per step, ratio 0.6026. The published figure was 447.0 and 1.2735. Both corrected ratios are BELOW 1.05, which is the predecessor own frozen REFUTED line -- so the corrected measurement does not merely fail to clear the SUPPORTED line, it lands in the refutation band.

BOTH BRANCHES WERE PROVED REACHABLE BEFORE THE RUN WAS TRUSTED. Shifting every inner event past the end of its outer event reports REFUTED at 0 of 2,538 nested. Removing the inner class entirely also reports REFUTED, on the sum clause rather than the nesting clause, so the two refusal grounds are exercised separately rather than the same one twice.

events.hypothesis:
WHAT THIS WITHDRAWS. The finding closed at 18:05Z today -- that the backward produces gradients for about 96 tensors per optimizer step that never take a step, recorded as this campaign's FIRST measured candidate in the work-REMOVAL class -- is withdrawn. Its counting predicate fused an autograd engine node with the op emitted inside it. Corrected, 235.5 gradient accumulations per step against 351 stepped tensors is a ratio of 0.6709: FEWER tensors receive a gradient than are stepped, which is the opposite of the published claim and is what a backward with no obvious waste looks like.

WHAT REPLACES IT, AND IT IS A REAL NUMBER RATHER THAN A RETRACTION ONLY. The inner op carries Input Dims, which the predecessor never read, so the gradient work is sized for the first time: 350,261,248 elements accumulated per optimizer step, every one of the 2,538 events carrying dims, against a stepped population of 474,030,080 elements in the optimizer receipt. The shape histogram is dominated by 3072x1024 (576), 1024x3072 (288), 2048x1024 (288) and 1024x1024 (288) -- the projection and expert matrices, not a tail of small tensors.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, AND THE FIRST ITEM IS WHY THIS IS NOT A DEAD END.

(1) THE WORK-REMOVAL CLASS IS NOT REFUTED. What is refuted is one candidate's evidence. The lever-stack result still says roughly half the needed factor is on no route this campaign has measured, and graph-changing work-removal is still the class with no measured member. This cycle removes a false member; it does not close the class.

(2) NO ELEMENT IS ATTRIBUTED TO A NAMED TENSOR. The trace carries shapes, never names, so no share of the 350 M elements is assigned to a parameter that never steps. The join that would do it still does not exist.

(3) THE PLACEMENT MANIFEST SAYS 425 OF 1,195 PLACEMENTS REQUIRE GRAD against 351 carrying optimizer state, which is 74 tensors that require a gradient and have no state. That is a DIFFERENT checkpoint at a DIFFERENT head (the 2026-09-12 hour control) and requires_grad is a flag, not a measurement that a gradient was produced. The measured per-step accumulation count is below the stepped count, so those 74 are not demonstrated to cost anything. Whether any of them receives a gradient in a real step is open and this does not answer it.

(4) THE DENOMINATOR IS STILL OWED A RECONCILIATION. Twelve Optimizer.step# annotations are taken as twelve steps. Halving it doubles every per-step figure here exactly as it did for the predecessor -- at six steps the corrected ratio is 1.34 and the original claim would stand. The reconciliation was owed before this cycle and is owed after it, and it is now the single term that decides the question.

(5) NO RATE, NO DURATION, NO CEILING, NO GATE. Durations were used only as interval bounds to prove nesting. An element count is a size and does not convert to microseconds. One capture, one process, no matched-run variation.

THE MECHANISM DEBT, WHICH IS MINE. A substring test was used where an identity test was required, in an instrument whose whole output is a COUNT. The same class as taking a field by shape rather than by name. Any instrument whose headline is a count of events now matches event names exactly and prints the distinct matched names beside the count, so a fused class is visible in the output rather than invisible in the predicate.

events.observation: The step-annotation census over the captured trace finds 12 Optimizer.step#AdamW.step events that are NOT 12 steps' worth of one annotation each. They fall into exactly two categories of six: six 'user_annotation' events on tid 38448 (host, ~1.7 ms each) and six 'gpu_user_annotation' events on tid 7 (device, ~16 ms each). They strictly alternate in time, each device event beginning about 1.1 ms after its host neighbour starts, while consecutive pairs are separated by roughly 450,000 us. Every per-step figure this campaign has published from this trace divides by 12.

events.hypothesis: The profiler emits a user annotation twice for one annotated region: once on the host thread that opened the record_function scope, and once projected onto the device timeline as gpu_user_annotation covering the kernels that ran inside it. That is a rendering of one scope on two timelines, not two scopes. If so the trace contains SIX optimizer steps and the denominator 12 is a double count of exactly the same shape as the AccumulateGrad double count closed an hour ago: a predicate matching a name across two timelines rather than counting the thing the name denotes. Consequence, and it cuts against the cycle I just closed: at six steps the corrected engine-node figure is 2826/6 = 471.0 per step, ratio 1.3419 to 351 stepped tensors, which is ABOVE the withdrawn claim's frozen SUPPORTED line of 1.20 -- so the withdrawn finding would stand on the numerator correction plus this denominator correction together, the two errors having very nearly cancelled.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED if the split is not 6 and 6, or if the nearest-neighbour pairing is not a bijection (any host event whose nearest device event is already claimed, or any device event unpaired), or if the largest intra-pair offset is within 50x of the smallest inter-pair gap, or if the two categories carry different annotation names. Any one of these means the 12 events are not one scope rendered twice and the denominator 12 is not shown to be a double count.
events.supported_if: SUPPORTED if ALL of the following hold, each proved per event and not asserted from the names: (1) the 12 Optimizer.step# events partition into exactly two categories of exactly 6 each, one 'user_annotation' and one 'gpu_user_annotation'; (2) pairing each host event to its nearest-in-time device event is a strict BIJECTION -- 6 pairs, no host event claimed twice, no device event left over; (3) every pair's intra-pair start offset is smaller than the SMALLEST inter-pair gap by at least a factor of 50, so the two distributions are separable rather than merely ordered; (4) the paired device event lies inside or overlapping its host event's own name string, i.e. both carry the identical annotation name.

events.because:
The frozen criterion required four clauses, each proved per event. All four hold.

(1) The 12 Optimizer.step# events partition into exactly two categories of exactly six: six 'user_annotation' on tid 38448 and six 'gpu_user_annotation' on tid 7. (2) Nearest-in-time pairing is a strict bijection -- six pairs, no host event claimed twice, no device event left over. (3) The largest intra-pair offset is 1,175.9 us and the smallest inter-pair gap is 462,003.3 us, a separation of 392.9x against a required 50x, so the two distributions are separable rather than merely ordered. (4) Both categories carry the identical name, 'Optimizer.step#AdamW.step', the only annotation name in the trace.

SO THE TRACE CONTAINS SIX OPTIMIZER STEPS, NOT TWELVE. Twelve is one annotated scope rendered on two timelines, host and device, and counted once on each.

BOTH REDS HELD ON DIFFERENT CLAUSES, which is what makes the four clauses four checks rather than one. Relabelling every device annotation to the host category reports REFUTED on clauses 1, 2 and 4. Pushing each device annotation out toward the next pair leaves clauses 1, 2 and 4 TRUE and refutes on clause 3 alone, at a separation of 1.7x against the required 50x -- so the separability clause is load-bearing on its own and is not carried by the others.

events.hypothesis:
THIS CUTS AGAINST THE CYCLE I CLOSED AN HOUR AGO, AND IN THE DIRECTION THAT FLATTERS THE ORIGINAL CLAIM, SO IT GETS MORE SCRUTINY RATHER THAN LESS.

Two double counts, in opposite places, very nearly cancelling:
  numerator   -- 'AccumulateGrad' in name fused an autograd engine node with the op inside it: 2,826 + 2,538 = 5,364 where the engine-node count is 2,826.
  denominator -- twelve annotations fused a host scope with its device projection: six real steps where twelve were counted.
Published: 5,364 / 12 = 447.0, ratio 1.2735. Corrected on both: 2,826 / 6 = 471.0, ratio 1.3419 against 351 stepped tensors. The withdrawn row's own frozen SUPPORTED line was 1.20, so the corrected figure CLEARS IT -- by a wider margin than the figure that was published.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: it does not re-rule that row. A verdict reinstated as a side effect of a different cycle's consequence block is a verdict nobody froze a criterion for. The re-ruling is the next cycle and it owes its own criterion before anything runs.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN.

(1) THE ANNOTATIONS ARE STEP MARKERS, NOT STEP SPANS. Zero of the 2,826 engine nodes fall inside any annotation interval; the host scope is about 1.7 ms and the device projection about 16 ms, while the inter-pair gap is about 462 ms. So dividing a whole-trace backward count by the marker count assumes the backward work is distributed evenly across the six steps. This cycle does not test that assumption, and a per-step figure built on it is a mean over the trace rather than a measurement of any one step.

(2) THE PAIRING IS EVIDENCE, NOT A READING OF THE PROFILER. Nearest-in-time plus name identity plus 392.9x separation is strong, and it is still an inference about how the profiler renders one scope. Reading the emitter would settle it outright and was not done.

(3) SIX STEPS IS A SMALL SAMPLE. Every per-step figure from this trace now rests on six intervals from one capture of one process under profiling instrumentation, with no matched-run variation.

(4) NO RATE, NO CEILING, NO GATE. The step count is a count. Nothing here converts to microseconds and no gate moves.

events.observation: Every named RATE route on this graph is now priced below the 1.5x arm bar: elementwise fusion 1.3202x, rescheduling 1.4726x generous, FP16 accumulation 1.176x generous. The registry's standing conclusion is that the factor must come from doing LESS WORK or at a HIGHER RATE, so the rate half is closed and the work half is unattempted. One measured instance of discarded work already exists: the backward evaluates 423 AccumulateGrad inner ops per step against 351 tensors that take an optimizer step, so 72 leaves per step receive gradients that no optimizer state consumes. The observation is that those 72 gradients are produced by real backward arithmetic whose device cost has never been measured, and if that cost is material it is work the step does not need.

events.hypothesis: The mechanism is a mismatch between what requires_grad marks and what the optimizer enrols. The backward engine walks every leaf reachable from the loss whose requires_grad is true and runs AccumulateGrad on it, because that is the only criterion the engine has. Optimizer enrolment is a separate act performed at construction over a parameter group, and nothing reconciles the two sets. So a parameter that is left requiring grad but is excluded from the optimizer -- a frozen support expert, a tied or duplicated placement, a buffer promoted to a parameter, a module constructed but not routed -- still causes the full backward chain feeding it to be evaluated: every matmul, reduction and elementwise op on the path from the loss to that leaf runs, its result is written into .grad, and no step ever reads it. The cost is therefore NOT the 72 AccumulateGrad calls themselves, which correction five measured at about 62 us per step of host time; it is whatever device arithmetic exists on the exclusive paths that feed only those leaves. If those leaves share their entire backward path with stepped leaves, the discarded work is near zero and only the accumulation is wasted. If any of them sit behind a path no stepped leaf needs, that whole subgraph is work the step does not need.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED if the exclusive backward subgraph feeding the unstepped leaves accounts for less than 1.0 percent of measured device time per step. The measurement: over the existing capture, partition backward device kernels by whether their producing op lies on a path reachable ONLY from an unstepped leaf, versus shared with at least one stepped leaf. If exclusive-path device time is below 1.0 percent of the step's device total, the discarded-work thread carries no factor and is refuted as a throughput lever, whatever its hygiene value. Also REFUTED if the trace cannot distinguish the two path classes at all, in which case the row is INCONCLUSIVE rather than REFUTED and says so. SUPPORTED only if exclusive-path device time is at or above 1.0 percent AND the partition is established from the trace rather than assumed from the parameter manifest.

events.because: The frozen criterion says: 'Also REFUTED if the trace cannot distinguish the two path classes at all, in which case the row is INCONCLUSIVE rather than REFUTED and says so.' That is the branch taken. All eight tensor-identity fields are absent across 215,100 cpu_op events, so no backward op can be attributed to the leaf its gradient reaches, and the exclusive-path partition the criterion is about is not constructible from this capture. Re-censused rather than inherited from the registry. What the run DID establish, as a floor and never as the criterion's quantity: device time is 130,996.2 us per step by interval union; the AccumulateGrad nodes themselves carry 7,658.0 us per step across 2,538 correlated launches; the 72 unstepped leaves are 17.02 percent of the 423 accumulations, giving a prorated discarded floor of 1,303.49 us per step = 0.9951 percent of device time. That floor sits just BELOW the 1.0 percent line, and it excludes every upstream op on any exclusive path, so it neither refutes nor supports the criterion's term. The deliberate reds both held: injecting a tensor-identity field made the partition available and produced a real ruling, and inflating the unstepped share to 100 percent did not produce the REFUTED its red forbids.

events.hypothesis: WHAT THE INCONCLUSIVE DOES NOT CLOSE. It does not say the discarded-work thread is small; it says THIS CAPTURE CANNOT WEIGH IT. The measured floor counts only the accumulation, prorated, and lands at 0.9951 percent of device time -- within a rounding error of the 1.0 percent line while excluding every upstream op on any exclusive path, which is the whole term the criterion was about. A floor that nearly clears the bar on its own while omitting the dominant term is the opposite of a reassuring result. It also does not close the hygiene question: 72 leaves per step carry gradients no optimizer state consumes, and that is a real defect in the parameter/optimizer reconciliation whatever its device cost turns out to be. THE SUCCESSOR IS AN INSTRUMENT QUESTION, NOT A TREATMENT. The blocker is a missing capture field, not a missing idea: torch profiler's with_stack or a record_function-tagged backward would let a backward op be attributed to the leaf it feeds, and profile_memory adds the allocation identity this trace lacks entirely. Before any capture is proposed, the standing constraints bind: a profiled number is not a governed number, the separation clause forbids composing across that boundary, and nothing about this justifies a GPU window until the field set is named and checked against what the profiler actually emits on this torch build. The cheap first leg is a source read of the profiler options, not a run. ALSO STILL OPEN from the parent thread and untouched here: why 48 leaves per step are reached by the backward walk and discarded, which 72 leaves are in the excess -- the trace carries shapes and not names -- and the reconciliation of 72 against the 74 require-grad-without-state placements in a different checkpoint at a different head, which is suggestive and is NOT claimed as a match. The 1.2051 ratio still rests on one capture with no matched-run variation, and nothing should be built on a 0.005 margin until a second capture exists.

events.observation: The cycle just closed established that torch 2.10.0+cu126's Chrome-trace exporter has no Addr literal at all -- its complete arg table sits in torch_cpu.dll at 225427380-225427800 bracketed by profiler_kineto.cpp, and the five memory keys it does carry (Bytes, Device Type, Device Id, Total Allocated, Total Reserved) measure allocation VOLUME, so two same-sized tensors on the same device are indistinguishable and there is nothing to join a memory record to an op BY. But the chrome-trace exporter is not torch's only memory instrument. The CUDA caching allocator keeps its OWN history, reached through torch.cuda.memory._record_memory_history and _snapshot, and it is a different subsystem with a different serializer -- the one that backs the memory-visualiser, which draws individual allocation blocks over time and attributes them to code. events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. The chrome-trace exporter and the allocator history are built for different jobs, which is why their field sets differ. The exporter serialises RecordFunction events into a timeline the Chrome viewer can draw, so its memory rows are a side-channel that says how much the allocator moved at a point in time -- volume is all that view needs. The allocator history exists to answer WHICH BLOCK, because it backs the memory visualiser: a picture of individual allocations occupying address ranges over time, each clickable to the code that made it. A serializer that must draw a block at an address and name its creator cannot avoid recording the address and the frames. So the same build can be simultaneously incapable of per-tensor attribution in one instrument and fully capable in the other, and the previous refutation says nothing about this one -- it read profiler_kineto.cpp, and this is CUDACachingAllocator plus its python binding. PREDICTION. The snapshot serializer emits, per allocation block, at minimum an address field and a size field, and when history recording is enabled with stack capture, a frames list of {filename, line, name}. The literals to look for are addr, frames, blocks, segments, active_allocs, history, stream, and the entry points _record_memory_history / _cuda_recordMemoryHistory / _cuda_memorySnapshot. WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS THE WRONG EXPLANATION. If the serializer records only sizes and segment totals with no address, the visualiser would be drawing proportions rather than blocks and the mechanism above is simply wrong about why the two differ. If frames exist but are only captured for python callers, backward allocations would carry engine frames rather than the op that made them -- the same defect that makes with_stack useless here -- and the route would buy an address with nothing to attribute it TO.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. When _record_memory_history runs with C++ stacks, each allocation records a CapturedTraceback: the unwinder walks the native stack from the allocation site upward and the symbolizer resolves the return addresses to names. An allocation made during backward is reached through the engine, so the walk passes through the generated node apply frame on its way out -- torch::autograd::generated::AddmmBackward0::apply and its siblings. If the unwind depth reaches that far and the Windows symbolizer resolves those addresses, the snapshot names the op per allocation. There are three ways this fails in practice even though every static precondition holds: the unwind can be depth-capped below the node frame; the Windows symbolizer can return empty or hexadecimal names where the Linux path returns symbols; and allocations can be served from the caching allocator without reaching the recorded path at all, so the busiest tensors carry no new frames. PREDICTION. A capture over a small number of CIA steps yields a snapshot whose trace entries include allocations whose frames list contains at least one name matching a generated autograd node, and the set of distinct node names recovered is larger than one.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED if no allocation in the snapshot carries any frame naming a generated autograd node -- the frames resolve only to allocator internals, engine entry points, or python -- because then the route delivers no op-level attribution and the predecessor cycles were describing a capability the runtime does not deliver. ALSO REFUTED if frames are present but unresolved, i.e. the frame entries carry empty names or bare hexadecimal addresses, since unresolvable frames attribute nothing. ALSO REFUTED if exactly one distinct node name is recovered across the whole capture, because a single name cannot partition a backward pass and would indicate the unwind is stopping at a common frame rather than reaching the op. A verdict is issued only if the CAPTURE ITSELF SUCCEEDS: if the snapshot is empty, the run errors, or no trace entries exist, the result is INCONCLUSIVE and no verdict is issued -- an instrument that produced nothing has not refuted anything. The capture is DIAGNOSTIC: per the governed-run evidence contract no number from it is a governed number, it earns no training-progress credit, and this cycle claims nothing about cost.

events.because: The frozen criterion refutes "if no allocation in the snapshot carries any frame naming a generated autograd node -- the frames resolve only to allocator internals, engine entry points, or python". That is exactly what the capture produced, and the mechanism is blunter than the criterion anticipated. 60,000 device-trace entries, 444 segments, 34,986 frame-bearing records, 346,302 frame names, ZERO unresolved -- and ZERO carrying a "::" namespace. Every frame carries exactly (filename, line, name) and torch logged "record_context_cpp is not support on non-linux non-x86_64 platforms" during the run. So the C++ context recorder was REFUSED BY PLATFORM; this is not an unwind that stopped below the node frame, which a deeper limit might have fixed. No configuration of the recorder reaches the node on this Windows build. THE CAPTURE ITSELF SUCCEEDED, so the INCONCLUSIVE escape does not apply: the snapshot is 74,797,588 bytes with 60,000 trace entries, the method control the criterion named. WHAT THIS COSTS THE PREDECESSOR. The capability cycle ruled SUPPORTED on three readings that were each correct about the bytes: stacks="all" IS the default at cuda/memory.py:1002, CapturedTraceback IS in torch_python.dll, and the six generated node symbols ARE in torch_cpu.dll. Every one was silent about the platform, and the capability verdict it supported is now known to be unreachable at runtime here. Acceptance of a parameter is not execution of the feature it names -- which is the same lesson as symbol presence not being symbol resolution, one layer further out, and it is the reason this cycle was opened instead of the route being built on the source reads.

events.hypothesis: WHAT THE REFUTATION DOES NOT CLOSE, and the first item is larger than the refuted claim. (1) THE PYTHON FRAMES ARE THEMSELVES OP-LEVEL ATTRIBUTION, in ember's own vocabulary rather than in generated-symbol vocabulary. A 4 MiB backward allocation in this capture carries reduce_weight_gradient at ember_v0_document_reduction.py:93, backward at :119, and apply at torch/autograd/function.py:317. The top frame names across the capture are run, forward, main, step, _resident_documents_forward, _resident_segment, _eager, apply, backward, rotate_three_axis, reduce_weight_gradient; the top files are ember_v0_decoder.py (79,196 frames), ember_v0_capture.py (38,868), ember_v0_document_reduction.py (14,945), ember_v0_residency.py (13,221). For the open question -- WHICH backward work feeds the 72 leaves that require grad with no optimizer state -- a source file and line is arguably a better key than an autograd node name, because the leaves are named in ember source and not in torch's generated symbols. That is the successor hypothesis and it is registered as such, NOT as a rescue of this one: the criterion asked about node names and node names are absent. (2) NOT CLOSED FOR LINUX. The refusal is explicitly platform-conditional and this campaign is single-4090 on Windows, so the route is closed HERE, not in general. No portability claim is made and none is needed. (3) AFFORDABILITY IS NOW PARTLY MEASURED and it is cheap, which was not expected. Six measured steps ran at 0.372-0.493 s wall against a governed 0.2265 s p90 step, with the recorder on and 60,000 entries retained -- roughly 1.6-2.2x, not the order-of-magnitude the C++ unwind would have cost. METHOD NOTE, and it is the reason this verdict is worth anything. TWO OF THE THREE DELIBERATE REDS WERE NO-OPS against this capture: --prove-red-no-nodes strips node names from a snapshot with none, and --prove-red-single-node collapses node names that do not exist. Both printed REFUTED and both would have printed REFUTED with the flag absent, so counting them would have been counting the real result three times. Only --prove-red-unresolved discriminated (0 -> 346,302 unresolved, clause 2 firing ahead of clause 1 on otherwise-clean data). That exposed the real gap: nothing showed the analyzer COULD return SUPPORTED, and an instrument with one reachable verdict carries no information when it refutes. So a synthetic positive control was built in the real snapshot's exact shape -- 500 real entries with native C++ node frames injected above their real python frames -- and against it the analyzer returns SUPPORTED (5 distinct nodes, 1,500 native frames), --prove-red-no-nodes turns it REFUTED with the 1,500 native frames still present, --prove-red-single-node turns it REFUTED at 1 distinct node, and --prove-red-unresolved turns it REFUTED at 100% unresolved. All four verdicts reachable, each clause firing on its own with the others left satisfiable. The synthetic snapshot is labelled SYNTHETIC in its own head and is a test of the RULER, never an observation about this build.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. torch's python memory recorder walks the CPython frame stack at each allocation and stores it as (filename, line, name) per frame. During backward, the engine calls a Function's apply, which calls the ember backward closure, which performs the tensor ops that allocate -- so the interpreter stack at the allocation site physically CONTAINS the ember frame that produced the work, beneath torch/autograd/function.py:317 and above the allocating torch call. If the DEEPEST ember-source frame differs between call sites, grouping allocations by that (file, line) partitions backward allocations by the ember code that made them -- which is what the refuted C++ route was wanted for, in a vocabulary that matches how the 72 unstepped leaves are actually named. THREE WAYS THIS FAILS EVEN THOUGH THE FRAMES EXIST. (c) Backward allocations carry the engine frame and NO ember frame beneath, because the allocating op is invoked from C++ after the python closure returns -- in which case the python stack names the caller of backward and not the op. events.observation: A census of the existing allocator snapshot (cia-allocator-snapshot-20260915T221503Z.json, 60,000 device-trace entries) finds 7,113 backward-tagged ALLOCATION records across 19 ember source sites over 6 measured steps. The two reduction sites dominate: ember_v0_document_reduction.py:93 carries 1,532 allocations totalling 5,905,580,032 bytes with only 3 distinct sizes, and :94 carries 1,149 allocations totalling 4,429,185,024 bytes with 3 distinct sizes. The step accumulates 423 leaves of which 351 are stepped and 72 are not. 1,532 over 6 steps is 255.3 per step, which is neither 423 nor 351 nor 72. The census ruled nothing and was written to rule nothing; it is the observation this cycle opens on.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. If the gradient buffer for each accumulated leaf were allocated at the reduction site, then that site would allocate once per leaf per step and each allocation would carry that leaf gradient buffer size. Leaf shapes differ across the population, so size would be a JOIN KEY: the 72 unstepped leaves would appear as a size class distinguishable from the 351 stepped ones, and the exclusive backward subgraph feeding them could be separated by volume. That is the only key this build affords -- the chrome-trace exporter emits no per-tensor identity on this build (refuted 20260915) and the C++ frames are refused by platform on Windows (refuted 20260915), so python frames plus allocation size is what remains. The mechanism predicts a per-step count at the reduction site near the accumulation count and a size multiplicity large enough to carry 423 distinct leaves.

events.hypothesis: The three adds per group exist ONLY because the reduction is serial. They are the seed cost, not the arithmetic cost: the four matmuls are the work the reduction has to do, and the adds are three extra elementwise passes over the full weight-gradient tensor that a batched reduction would not perform. So the reduction device time decomposes into a term that is intrinsic and a term that is structural, and which of them dominates decides whether there is anything here at all. THE PREDICTION, with its arithmetic stated so it is a commitment rather than a hedge: each group performs four matmuls and three adds, so if per-call device time were equal the adds would be 3/7 = 42.9 percent of the reduction. Predicting the adds below 25 percent is predicting the matmuls are individually the more expensive call by a clear margin. If that holds, the structural term is small and the adds are closed; if it fails, the serialisation has a measured price and batching the reduction acquires a target.

events.observation: THE PREDECESSOR CYCLE CLOSED SUPPORTED AND ITS RULING IS WHAT THIS CYCLE AUDITS. I wrote that the six structurally unique dW instances are a device-time outlier of a size no cycle anticipated: 6 of 726 groups, 0.83 percent, carrying 13,597.1 us or 15.18 percent of the reduction, at 2,266.2 us per group against 126.2 us for the 2048x1024 class -- a factor of about 18. That comparison is per GROUP, and the groups are not the same size: the six carry a weight of 33.554 M elements against 2.097 M, which is 16x. So most or all of an 18x could be arithmetic about the shape rather than a finding about a mechanism, and my own headline is the thing to check. THE REGISTRY QUERY RETIRED MY FIRST SUCCESSOR BEFORE IT RAN. I had authored an instrument asking whether per-element elementwise cost STEPS at a cache-capacity boundary; querying the proposition own nouns -- cache, residency, footprint, L2, elementwise -- returned three prior cycles that answer it and answer it the other way. the-elementwise-class-fits-in-l2-but-that-is-not-why-its-rate-exceeds-dram-20260915 found the population that CANNOT fit in the 72 MB L2 running FASTEST, at 1390.9 GB/s against 1146.8 for the fitting population, which refuses the residency mechanism by its own data. the-elementwise-excess-is-shape-heterogeneity-not-per-kernel-overhead-20260915 attributed 81.2 percent of the class-wide excess to BETWEEN-SITE shape differences. That instrument was deleted unrun rather than run as a fourth duplicate, and those two rows also bound what this cycle may conclude about a slow add: it would be the reduction instance of a dispersion already measured at class level, not a new mechanism.

events.hypothesis: THE PROPOSITION: normalised for the work each group actually does, the six are NOT slow on the MATMUL side, and the entire per-unit anomaly sits in the accumulation ADD. If that holds, the 18x is a statement about the weight shape and the surviving question is one add site rather than a whole class of instances. WHAT MAKES THIS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A RE-READ of the predecessor receipt, which is the objection I would raise against it: that receipt records per-class device time, calls and groups, and records NOTHING about the operand shapes. In particular it does not record K, the contraction length. A dW matmul costs 2*M*K*N, so normalising by output elements is only valid when K is equal across the classes, and nothing on file establishes that. Clause 3 MEASURES K per class from the recorded operand dims and REFUSES the comparison outright if any class carries more than one, because a mixed-K class has no single rate to quote. That is a way this cycle can fail that the predecessor could not even express, and it is why the rate clause is stated in FLOPs per second rather than in time per element.

events.observation: THIS CAMPAIGN NOW CARRIES ABOVE-PUBLISHED-REFERENCE READINGS IN TWO INDEPENDENT UNIT SYSTEMS and has never compared them. On the MEMORY side, above-peak-copies-cannot-be-explained-by-cache-so-three-terms-cannot-all-be-right-20260915 found 11 aten::copy_ kernels at exactly 1,073,741,824 bytes running 1194.8 to 1240.7 GB/s against a published 1008.0, showed that no cache assumption explains them at any generosity, and ruled that the bytes, the duration and the reference cannot all be right without naming which. Two of its own not_closed lines set up this cycle: it says the term that would explain the excess cleanly is the REFERENCE RATE, and it says in as many words that ARITHMETIC KERNELS ARE EXCLUDED AND THEIR OVER-COUNT STATUS IS UNTESTED. On the ARITHMETIC side, the cycle that closed minutes ago measured the six-instance dW class at 169.058 TFLOP/s against a published 165.2 dense bf16 -- 102.3 percent of peak -- and carried it as a defect signal under an explicit prohibition on quoting it as achieved throughput. The registry was queried on this proposition own nouns -- peak, above-peak, published, reference, rate -- and returned the memory row and no row comparing the two.

events.hypothesis: THE PROPOSITION: THE TWO READINGS HAVE DIFFERENT CAUSES. If one systematic term were behind both -- a clock the references understate, a profiler duration under-reported, a shape convention -- then the MULTIPLICATIVE FACTOR needed to bring each population back under its own reference would be the SAME, because a single multiplicative term applies equally to a rate expressed in either unit. If the factors disagree, no single term reconciles them and the campaign is carrying two separate defects that must be diagnosed separately; if they agree, a common cause is live and that is a LARGER finding than this hypothesis, which is why the tolerance is set generously at 10 percent in the direction that makes agreement easy to reach. WHY THIS IS A MEASUREMENT AND NOT ARITHMETIC I ALREADY HOLD, which is the objection I would raise against it: the arithmetic reading on file covers SIX matmuls. Whether the WHOLE aten::mm population of this trace runs above its reference has never been measured, and that measurement is exactly what discharges the memory row untested line. It also matters that a FLOP count has a property a byte count does not -- 2*M*K*N is exact given the dims, with no traversal to guess at, which is the precise ambiguity the memory-side cycle could not resolve -- so the arithmetic side is the cleaner of the two instruments and can bound the memory side suspect list from outside it. MY HONEST PREDICTION, stated before the run so it can be scored against me: I expect DISAGREEMENT, because the memory excess is about 23 percent and the arithmetic excess about 2 percent, and I expect that because the two published references are driven by DIFFERENT hardware clocks -- compute by the SM clock, memory by the memory clock -- so a common clock term is not even available a priori.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED if ANY of five clauses fails, checked in order, each with a deliberate red proved before the reading. (1) COVERAGE: less than 90 percent of aten::mm device time carries readable operand dims, in which case the achieved rate describes whichever subpopulation the dims happened to be recorded for rather than the population. Red: force coverage to zero. (2) THE MEMORY-SIDE READING is not above its published 1008.0 GB/s, in which case there is no second above-reference reading to compare. (3) THE WHOLE MATMUL POPULATION is NOT above its published 165.2 TFLOP/s, in which case the six-instance excess is a property of that one class and the comparison this cycle is built on does not arise. THIS IS A REAL FINDING AND NOT AN INSTRUMENT DEFECT: it would say the above-peak arithmetic reading is local to the six rather than systematic, which is itself worth knowing and which refutes the framing. Red: halve the achieved rate. (4) THE PREDICTION: the two required factors AGREE within 10 percent, so one systematic term may explain both and the campaign has ONE defect rather than two. That is a bigger finding than the hypothesis and it refutes it. Red: set the memory factor equal to the arithmetic factor. (5) THE PREDECESSOR six-instance reading does not reproduce from its own landed receipt, in which case this cycle and its predecessor are not discussing the same quantity.
events.supported_if: SUPPORTED if all five clauses hold, in which case the two above-reference readings require materially different corrections, no single systematic term reconciles them, and the campaign must diagnose the byte model and the FLOP-or-duration question SEPARATELY rather than hunting one common cause. The receipt carries what no cycle has: the achieved compute rate of the entire aten::mm population of this trace as a fraction of its published reference, with a per-shape breakdown, beside the memory-side factor read from its landed receipt. WHAT IT STILL WOULD NOT ESTABLISH, frozen here so it cannot be claimed afterwards. IT IDENTIFIES NO TERM AND CORRECTS NOTHING. Exceeding a reference means the count, the duration and the reference cannot all be right; comparing two such factors narrows a suspect list and names nothing, so no lever, byte figure or rate anywhere in this campaign may be restated on the strength of it. THE FLOP COUNT ASSUMES THE RECORDED DIMS ARE THE EXECUTED DIMS, and the memory factor inherits every caveat of the byte model behind its receipt. THE REFERENCES ARE SPECIFICATION FIGURES used to express fractions, never measured ceilings for this card and never impossibility premises. NO GOVERNED QUANTITY, NO HARDWARE READING, NO MATCHED-RUN VARIATION: one profiled trace, 6 steps, one card, no measured device traffic and no clock or occupancy counter, and nothing composed against the 175,190 us governed step.

events.because: REFUTED at clause 3, and the refutation removes the PREMISE of the hypothesis rather than its conclusion. The frozen criterion named this outcome in advance and named it as a finding: "(3) THE WHOLE MATMUL POPULATION is NOT above its published 165.2 TFLOP/s, in which case the six-instance excess is a property of that one class and the comparison this cycle is built on does not arise. THIS IS A REAL FINDING AND NOT AN INSTRUMENT DEFECT: it would say the above-peak arithmetic reading is local to the six rather than systematic, which is itself worth knowing and which refutes the framing." MEASURED: 7,998 aten::mm calls, ALL 7,998 sized, coverage 1.0000 against a 0.90 floor, achieving 146.270 TFLOP/s = 0.8854 of the published 165.2. The matmul population of this trace runs BELOW its reference, not above it. THE ABOVE-PEAK READING IS LOCAL AND IT IS LOCAL TO A RECOGNISABLE SHAPE: the two classes at or above the reference are the large-contraction ones -- 32768x1024x1024 at 169.058 TFLOP/s and 1024x32768x1024 at 164.978, K or M of 32768 in both -- while the rate falls monotonically with the small dimension: 4096x2048x1024 at 0.9823, 4096x1024x1024 at 0.9454, 2048x1024x1024 at 0.9109, 1024x1024x1024 at 0.7721, and 256x1024x1024 at 0.3771. That is what arithmetic intensity looks like, and it is a far more ordinary explanation of a 2.3 percent excess on one near-ideal class than any systematic counting defect: a GEMM at 0.9987 of published, plus opportunistic boost above the clock the reference is quoted at, lands exactly here. CLAUSE 4 HELD AND ITS READING IS RECORDED RATHER THAN CREDITED: the arithmetic factor is 0.8854 and the memory factor 1.2309, a disagreement of 0.2807 against a 0.10 tolerance, so the two readings would indeed have required materially different corrections. That was my registered prediction and it was right, and it does NOT rescue the hypothesis, because clause 3 shows there is no systematic arithmetic excess for a common term to have explained. Clauses 1, 2 and 5 held; all three reds fired on their own clauses.
