Two of its own not_closed lines set up this cycle: it says the term that would explain the excess cleanly is the REFERENCE RATE, and it says in as many words that ARITHMETIC KERNELS ARE EXCLUDED AND THEIR OVER-COUNT STATUS IS UNTESTED. On the ARITHMETIC side, the cycle that closed minutes ago measured the six-instance dW class at 169.058 TFLOP/s against a published 165.2 dense bf16 -- 102.3 percent of peak -- and carried it as a defect signal under an explicit prohibition on quoting it as achieved throughput. The registry was queried on this proposition own nouns -- peak, above-peak, published, reference, rate -- and returned the memory row and no row comparing the two.
hypotheses.explanation: THE PROPOSITION: THE TWO READINGS HAVE DIFFERENT CAUSES. If one systematic term were behind both -- a clock the references understate, a profiler duration under-reported, a shape convention -- then the MULTIPLICATIVE FACTOR needed to bring each population back under its own reference would be the SAME, because a single multiplicative term applies equally to a rate expressed in either unit. If the factors disagree, no single term reconciles them and the campaign is carrying two separate defects that must be diagnosed separately; if they agree, a common cause is live and that is a LARGER finding than this hypothesis, which is why the tolerance is set generously at 10 percent in the direction that makes agreement easy to reach. WHY THIS IS A MEASUREMENT AND NOT ARITHMETIC I ALREADY HOLD, which is the objection I would raise against it: the arithmetic reading on file covers SIX matmuls. Whether the WHOLE aten::mm population of this trace runs above its reference has never been measured, and that measurement is exactly what discharges the memory row untested line. It also matters that a FLOP count has a property a byte count does not -- 2*M*K*N is exact given the dims, with no traversal to guess at, which is the precise ambiguity the memory-side cycle could not resolve -- so the arithmetic side is the cleaner of the two instruments and can bound the memory side suspect list from outside it. MY HONEST PREDICTION, stated before the run so it can be scored against me: I expect DISAGREEMENT, because the memory excess is about 23 percent and the arithmetic excess about 2 percent, and I expect that because the two published references are driven by DIFFERENT hardware clocks -- compute by the SM clock, memory by the memory clock -- so a common clock term is not even available a priori.
hypotheses.criterion: REFUTED if ANY of five clauses fails, checked in order, each with a deliberate red proved before the reading. (1) COVERAGE: less than 90 percent of aten::mm device time carries readable operand dims, in which case the achieved rate describes whichever subpopulation the dims happened to be recorded for rather than the population. Red: force coverage to zero. (2) THE MEMORY-SIDE READING is not above its published 1008.0 GB/s, in which case there is no second above-reference reading to compare. (3) THE WHOLE MATMUL POPULATION is NOT above its published 165.2 TFLOP/s, in which case the six-instance excess is a property of that one class and the comparison this cycle is built on does not arise. THIS IS A REAL FINDING AND NOT AN INSTRUMENT DEFECT: it would say the above-peak arithmetic reading is local to the six rather than systematic, which is itself worth knowing and which refutes the framing. Red: halve the achieved rate. (4) THE PREDICTION: the two required factors AGREE within 10 percent, so one systematic term may explain both and the campaign has ONE defect rather than two. That is a bigger finding than the hypothesis and it refutes it. Red: set the memory factor equal to the arithmetic factor. (5) THE PREDECESSOR six-instance reading does not reproduce from its own landed receipt, in which case this cycle and its predecessor are not discussing the same quantity.
hypotheses.criterion_supported_if: SUPPORTED if all five clauses hold, in which case the two above-reference readings require materially different corrections, no single systematic term reconciles them, and the campaign must diagnose the byte model and the FLOP-or-duration question SEPARATELY rather than hunting one common cause. The receipt carries what no cycle has: the achieved compute rate of the entire aten::mm population of this trace as a fraction of its published reference, with a per-shape breakdown, beside the memory-side factor read from its landed receipt. WHAT IT STILL WOULD NOT ESTABLISH, frozen here so it cannot be claimed afterwards. IT IDENTIFIES NO TERM AND CORRECTS NOTHING. Exceeding a reference means the count, the duration and the reference cannot all be right; comparing two such factors narrows a suspect list and names nothing, so no lever, byte figure or rate anywhere in this campaign may be restated on the strength of it. THE FLOP COUNT ASSUMES THE RECORDED DIMS ARE THE EXECUTED DIMS, and the memory factor inherits every caveat of the byte model behind its receipt. THE REFERENCES ARE SPECIFICATION FIGURES used to express fractions, never measured ceilings for this card and never impossibility premises. NO GOVERNED QUANTITY, NO HARDWARE READING, NO MATCHED-RUN VARIATION: one profiled trace, 6 steps, one card, no measured device traffic and no clock or occupancy counter, and nothing composed against the 175,190 us governed step.
hypotheses.ruling: REFUTED at clause 3, and the refutation removes the PREMISE of the hypothesis rather than its conclusion. The frozen criterion named this outcome in advance and named it as a finding: "(3) THE WHOLE MATMUL POPULATION is NOT above its published 165.2 TFLOP/s, in which case the six-instance excess is a property of that one class and the comparison this cycle is built on does not arise. THIS IS A REAL FINDING AND NOT AN INSTRUMENT DEFECT: it would say the above-peak arithmetic reading is local to the six rather than systematic, which is itself worth knowing and which refutes the framing." MEASURED: 7,998 aten::mm calls, ALL 7,998 sized, coverage 1.0000 against a 0.90 floor, achieving 146.270 TFLOP/s = 0.8854 of the published 165.2. The matmul population of this trace runs BELOW its reference, not above it. THE ABOVE-PEAK READING IS LOCAL AND IT IS LOCAL TO A RECOGNISABLE SHAPE: the two classes at or above the reference are the large-contraction ones -- 32768x1024x1024 at 169.058 TFLOP/s and 1024x32768x1024 at 164.978, K or M of 32768 in both -- while the rate falls monotonically with the small dimension: 4096x2048x1024 at 0.9823, 4096x1024x1024 at 0.9454, 2048x1024x1024 at 0.9109, 1024x1024x1024 at 0.7721, and 256x1024x1024 at 0.3771. That is what arithmetic intensity looks like, and it is a far more ordinary explanation of a 2.3 percent excess on one near-ideal class than any systematic counting defect: a GEMM at 0.9987 of published, plus opportunistic boost above the clock the reference is quoted at, lands exactly here. CLAUSE 4 HELD AND ITS READING IS RECORDED RATHER THAN CREDITED: the arithmetic factor is 0.8854 and the memory factor 1.2309, a disagreement of 0.2807 against a 0.10 tolerance, so the two readings would indeed have required materially different corrections. That was my registered prediction and it was right, and it does NOT rescue the hypothesis, because clause 3 shows there is no systematic arithmetic excess for a common term to have explained. Clauses 1, 2 and 5 held; all three reds fired on their own clauses.
hypotheses.not_closed: (1) MY OWN PREDECESSOR NOT_CLOSED LINE IS NARROWED BY THIS AND MUST BE READ WITH IT. the-six-are-16x-bigger-not-18x-slower-20260915 carries "THE ABSOLUTE RATE IS ABOVE PUBLISHED PEAK AND THAT IS A DEFECT SIGNAL" and names it the successor. That line stands as a caution against quoting the number as achieved throughput, and its DEFECT framing is weakened: the population around it runs at 0.8854 of published, the excess is confined to the two large-contraction classes, and 2.3 percent on a class already at 0.9987 is what boost clock and arithmetic intensity produce without any counting error. NOTHING HERE PROVES the FLOP count is right -- it shows the excess does not generalise, which is a different and weaker claim. (2) THE MEMORY-SIDE QUESTION IS UNTOUCHED AND IS UNCHANGED. 11 copies at 1240.7 GB/s against 1008.0, unexplained by any cache assumption, stands exactly as its row left it. What this cycle removes is the hope of explaining it with one term shared with the arithmetic side; it must be diagnosed on its own evidence. (3) THE RATE SPREAD IS THE SUCCESSOR AND IT IS LARGE. 256x1024x1024 runs 1,152 calls and 9,927.3 us at 62.300 TFLOP/s -- 0.3771 of published -- and 1024x1024x1024 runs 1,152 calls and 19,395.4 us at 0.7721. Whether that spread is explained by arithmetic intensity alone, or whether some of it is launch, tail or wave quantisation that a shape change could collect, is unmeasured and is the named successor. NO SAVING IS IMPLIED: a rate below a reference is a distance, never a promise that a mechanism collects it. (4) NO TERM IS IDENTIFIED ANYWHERE. Exceeding or missing a reference means the count, the duration and the reference cannot all be right, and this cycle names none of them. (5) THE FLOP COUNT ASSUMES THE RECORDED DIMS ARE THE EXECUTED DIMS, and the memory factor is read from a landed receipt and inherits every caveat of the byte model behind it -- including that the receipt key was absent and the figure came from the row own condition line, which the instrument records rather than hides. (6) NO GOVERNED QUANTITY, NO HARDWARE READING, NO MATCHED-RUN VARIATION: one profiled trace, 6 steps, one card, no measured device traffic and no clock or occupancy counter, nothing composed against the 175,190 us governed step. (7) THE TWO STRUCTURAL QUESTIONS STILL STAND UNTOUCHED: why the six exist at all, and why exactly 726 of the 1,452 backward instances carry no reduction group.
hypotheses.closing: Closed REFUTED against the receipt. The hypothesis lost its premise rather than its conclusion: the whole 7,998-call matmul population runs at 0.8854 of published, so there is no systematic arithmetic excess for a common term to explain, and the above-peak reading is confined to the two large-contraction classes where arithmetic intensity and boost clock account for it ordinarily. The predicted disagreement between the two factors -- 0.8854 against 1.2309 -- held and is recorded without being credited. The memory-side above-peak question is unchanged and must be diagnosed alone. Successor named in not_closed item 3: the matmul rate spread from 0.3771 to 0.9987 across shapes.

Read as a roofline that says those sites should run at or near the published 165.2 TFLOP/s. events.hypothesis: THE PROPOSITION: THE ROOFLINE DOES NOT PREDICT THE ACHIEVED RATE OF THIS POPULATION, AND WHERE IT DISAGREES IT OVER-PREDICTS. The model is min(165.2 TFLOP/s, intensity x 1008 GB/s) per shape, built from the same two published figures the campaign already uses to express every fraction. If the model predicts the reading, the 91.3 percent eligibility figure is a PREDICTION and the precision route inherits it as headroom. If it over-predicts, that figure is an UPPER BOUND that the campaign has been reading as a forecast, and the difference is carried by terms nobody here has measured. WHY THIS IS WORTH A CYCLE AND IS NOT ARITHMETIC I COULD HAVE ASSERTED: the objection I would raise against it is that everyone knows a roofline over-predicts small shapes, so the answer is foregone. It is not, for two reasons. The interesting population is not the small shapes -- it is 2048x1024x1024 at intensity 409.6, TWO AND A HALF TIMES the ridge, which the model says should run at the full 165.2 and which the receipt reads at 150.488. And the byte model is deliberately a LOWER bound on traffic, which makes intensity an upper bound and the prediction as HIGH as it can defensibly be, so the instrument is built to make its own finding harder to reach. MY PREDICTION, stated before the run: OVER-PREDICTION EVERYWHERE, worst at the shapes with a small M, and present even well above the ridge.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED if ANY of five clauses fails, checked in order, each with a deliberate red proved before the reading. (1) COMPLETENESS: the per-shape table does not reconstruct the population totals -- 249,504.435 us and 7,998 calls -- to within a microsecond and exactly in calls. This clause exists because the predecessor row published eight of fourteen shapes as if they were the population; completeness is now PROVED every run rather than assumed. Red: add a microsecond. (2) REPRODUCTION: the reconstructed population rate does not equal the landed receipt 146.26964172669605 to 1e-9 relative, in which case this cycle and its predecessor are not discussing the same quantity. Red: scale it by 1.5. (3) THE HYPOTHESIS: the roofline DOES predict the achieved rate within 10 percent for at least half of above-ridge device time. THIS IS A REAL FINDING AND NOT AN INSTRUMENT DEFECT: it would license the 91.3 percent eligibility figure as a prediction rather than an upper bound, which is a bigger result than the hypothesis and refutes it. Red: set every achieved rate equal to its prediction. (4) DIRECTION: any above-ridge shape reads MORE than 10 percent ABOVE its model, in which case the model is not an upper bound at all and OVER-PREDICTS is the wrong description of the gap. Red: double every reading. (5) SHARE: the above-ridge population carries less than half of matmul device time, in which case a statement about it is not a statement about this population. Red: force the share to zero.
events.supported_if: SUPPORTED if all five clauses hold, in which case the roofline over-predicts the achieved rate of this trace whole matmul population, the 91.3 percent arithmetic-bound eligibility figure is an UPPER BOUND on what a precision route could touch rather than a forecast of it, and the gap is carried by terms this campaign has never measured. The receipt carries what no cycle has: derived intensity, model prediction and measured achieved rate side by side for every shape of the population, with completeness proved against the population totals. WHAT IT STILL WOULD NOT ESTABLISH, frozen here so it cannot be claimed afterwards. IT NAMES NO MECHANISM. Occupancy, tile and wave quantisation, launch and tail effects, cache behaviour and clock are all candidates and NONE is measured anywhere in this campaign; the gap is a residual, not an attribution. IT NAMES NO SAVING AND NO CEILING. A shape running below a reference is a DISTANCE, never a promise that any mechanism collects it, and nothing here may be quoted as headroom. THE BYTE MODEL IS DERIVED FROM RECORDED SHAPES, NOT MEASURED TRAFFIC, and its lower-bound direction is what makes SUPPORTED the WEAK direction rather than the flattering one. THE FLOP COUNT ASSUMES THE RECORDED DIMS ARE THE EXECUTED DIMS. THE TWO REFERENCES ARE SPECIFICATION FIGURES, never measured ceilings for this card and never impossibility premises. NO GOVERNED QUANTITY: one profiled trace, 6 steps, one card, no matched-run variation, nothing composed against the 175,190 us governed step, and no gate moves.

events.because: REFUTED at clause 3, the criterion pre-committed to this being a finding rather than a defect, and MY REGISTERED PREDICTION WAS WRONG. The frozen line reads: "(3) THE HYPOTHESIS: the roofline DOES predict the achieved rate within 10 percent for at least half of above-ridge device time. THIS IS A REAL FINDING AND NOT AN INSTRUMENT DEFECT: it would license the 91.3 percent eligibility figure as a prediction rather than an upper bound, which is a bigger result than the hypothesis and refutes it." MEASURED: the model predicts within 10 percent for 0.8142 of above-ridge device time. I predicted "OVER-PREDICTION EVERYWHERE, worst at the shapes with a small M, and present even well above the ridge." The second half is right and the first is wrong, and the first was the claim. THE VERDICT DOES NOT REST ON THE TOLERANCE, WHICH IS THE OBJECTION I WOULD RAISE AGAINST IT. Two shapes clear the frozen 10 percent narrowly -- 2048x1024x1024 at 8.91 percent error and 1024x1024x2048 at 9.33 -- so the share was recomputed across tolerances after the verdict, as disclosure and not as adjudication: 0.8142 at 10 percent, 0.8142 at 15, 0.8142 at 20, 0.8923 only at 30. There is a clean GAP between the worst passing error, 9.33 percent, and the best failing one, 29.5, so every tolerance from 10 to 29 percent returns the identical verdict. It would have held the other way below about 5 percent (share 0.4877 at 5 percent, against the 0.50 floor), and that is stated because the frozen 10 was chosen before the reading and is the only number the verdict may use. THE SEPARATION IS SHARPER THAN EITHER OUTCOME I ANTICIPATED AND IS THE SUBSTANTIVE RESULT. Arithmetic intensity separates the predicted from the missed PERFECTLY, with no overlap: every shape the model predicts has intensity 409.6 or above (409.6, 409.6, 455.1, 504.1, 504.1, 585.1, 585.1, 799.2) and every shape it misses has 341.3 or below (341.3, 170.7, 170.7, 170.7). So the threshold at which this population begins behaving like its roofline is NOT the published ridge of 163.9 FLOPs per byte -- it is roughly 400, about 2.4 times the ridge. Above the ridge is necessary and not sufficient, which the fp16-accumulation row asserted from two isolated probe shapes; it is now measured on the whole population of a real trace, and it comes with a number. Clauses 1, 2, 4 and 5 held: the fourteen shapes reconstruct 249,504.435 us and 7,998 calls exactly, the reconstructed population rate equals the landed 146.26964172669605 to 1e-9, no reading exceeds its model beyond tolerance, and the above-ridge population is 0.9952 of matmul device time. All five reds fired on their own clauses.

events.hypothesis: IT NARROWS THE 91.3 PERCENT ELIGIBILITY FIGURE RATHER THAN LICENSING IT, AND THE NARROWING IS THE USEFUL PART. the-2x-rate-eligibility-survives-the-recorded-shapes-at-91-percent-arithmetic-bound-20260915 reports 91.3 percent of eligible-site device time at or above the 163.9 ridge. This cycle shows the ridge is the wrong threshold for predicting behaviour: the model only tracks the reading from about 400 FLOPs per byte. Anything between 163.9 and 400 counts as eligible in that row and does NOT behave like its roofline here. That row figure is not withdrawn -- it measures what it says it measures -- but it may not be read as a forecast of achieved rate, and the fp16 row caution stands with a number attached. THE MISSED SET IS 46,140.0 us, 18.58 PERCENT OF ABOVE-RIDGE DEVICE TIME, AND IT IS WHERE ANY COLLECTIBLE TIME WOULD BE IF ANY IS. 1024x1024x1024 at 19,395.4 us runs 1.295 below its model; 256x1024x1024 at 9,927.3 us runs 2.652 below; 1024x1024x256 at 9,707.1 us, 2.593; 1024x256x1024 at 7,110.2 us, 1.899. The three shapes carrying a 256 dimension hold 26,744.6 us between them. NO SAVING IS IMPLIED AND NONE MAY BE QUOTED: a gap between a model and a reading is a distance, and nothing here shows any mechanism collects it. NO MECHANISM IS NAMED ANYWHERE IN THIS CYCLE. Occupancy, tile and wave quantisation, launch and tail effects, cache behaviour and clock are all candidates for the gap and for the 400-FLOPs-per-byte threshold, and NOT ONE of them is measured anywhere in this campaign. The 400 figure is a boundary observed in fourteen points, not a derived quantity, and fourteen points with a gap between 341.3 and 409.6 locate it only to that interval. THE BYTE MODEL IS DERIVED FROM RECORDED SHAPES, NEVER MEASURED TRAFFIC, and charges each operand read once and the output written once -- a LOWER bound, so intensity is an UPPER bound and the prediction as high as it can defensibly be. That direction favoured the hypothesis, and the hypothesis lost anyway, which makes the refutation the STRONG direction rather than the flattering one. TWO SHAPES READ ABOVE THEIR MODEL and clause 4 admitted them because they are inside the tolerance: 4096x1024x32768 and 32768x1024x1024, both at 1.0234 of published. Those are the forward and dW of one site, carrying identical FLOPs and differing by 0.3 us, and their excess over a published specification figure is still unexplained by anything measured here. THE FLOP COUNT ASSUMES THE RECORDED DIMS ARE THE EXECUTED DIMS. One profiled trace, 6 steps, one card, no matched-run variation, no measured device traffic, no clock or occupancy counter, and nothing composed against the 175,190 us governed step. NO GATE MOVES.

events.because: Closed REFUTED against the receipt, and the refutation is more useful than the hypothesis would have been. The roofline predicts the achieved rate within 10 percent for 0.8142 of above-ridge matmul device time, so the model works for the bulk of this population and my registered prediction of over-prediction everywhere was wrong. What the cycle produces instead is a threshold: intensity separates predicted from missed with no overlap, at roughly 400 FLOPs per byte -- 2.4 times the published ridge of 163.9. Above the ridge is necessary and not sufficient is now a measured statement on a real population with a number, rather than an inference from two probe shapes. The verdict is stable for any tolerance from 10 to 29 percent. Successor named in not_closed item 2: the 46,140.0 us missed set, and in particular the 26,744.6 us carried by the three shapes with a 256 dimension.

The only scoreable group, intensity 170.7 with a gap spread of 1.396, contains 1024x1024x256 at output 262,144 with gap 2.593 and 256x1024x1024 at output 262,144 with gap 2.652. Same output. Arbitrary order. Scored as a rise. THREE CONSECUTIVE CYCLES IN THIS THREAD HAVE NOW BEEN REFUTED BY A STRICT-ORDER CLAUSE MEETING A TIE IN A FOURTEEN-POINT POPULATION, and that is a fact about how I write clauses rather than about the trace. WHAT THE PREDECESSOR DID ESTABLISH AND WHAT THIS CYCLE INHERITS: clause 3 HELD. With intensity ties excluded rather than counted, the gap falls monotonically as intensity rises across six comparisons with one inversion inside the allowed one, and that inversion is 1.001 to 1.020, a 1.7 percent reversal. So intensity DOES order the gap across genuinely different intensities.
hypotheses.explanation: THE PROPOSITION SEPARATES THE TWO CASES THE PREDECESSOR CLAUSE FUSED, AND MAKES THE TIE CASE CARRY ITS OWN FALSIFIABLE CONTENT INSTEAD OF BEING SILENTLY EXCLUDED. Inside an intensity tie, a pair of members whose output element counts DIFFER by at least a factor of 1.5 is ORDERED: a fill account predicts the larger output runs closer to the model. A pair whose output counts are EQUAL is not ordered at all -- it is checked for AGREEMENT, because on any account where intensity and fill together decide the gap, two shapes agreeing on both should sit the same distance from the model. THAT AGREEMENT CLAUSE IS THE NEW CONTENT AND IT CAN GENUINELY FAIL, which is the point: if two shapes matching on both quantities run materially different gaps, then neither quantity nor the pair of them decides it, and the finding needs no ordering and no tie-breaking to state. Excluding the tie without testing it would have been the comfortable repair and would have thrown away the strongest single observation the population offers. WHAT I AM DELIBERATELY NOT DOING: the predecessor stands REFUTED, its ruling is unchanged, and clause 3 is carried across VERBATIM rather than relaxed, so a regression in it would be visible here. MY PREDICTION, stated before the run: clause 3 holds again with the same single 1.7 percent inversion; the 170.7 group supplies two ordering pairs and both fall, 2.593 and 2.652 at 262,144 elements against 1.899 at 1,048,576; two output-tied pairs exist, 170.7 at 262,144 agreeing to about 1.023 and 409.6 at 2,097,152 agreeing to about 1.005, and both sit inside the 1.10 tolerance. I expect SUPPORTED, and I expect it to rest on one scoreable group of three points, which is thin.

Red: empty the group list. (3) ACROSS: with ties excluded, the gap is STILL not ordered by intensity over group medians, allowing at most one inversion. THIS WOULD BE A REGRESSION AGAINST THE PREDECESSOR HELD READING AND IS CARRIED HERE UNCHANGED SO IT CANNOT HIDE. Red: swap the gaps in every comparison. (4) ORDERING: some pair inside a scoreable tie group whose output sizes differ by at least 1.5x has the gap RISING with output, in which case fill does not order the gap even with intensity held exactly constant -- or no such pair exists at all, in which case the ordering is untestable and the clause refuses rather than passing vacuously. events.hypothesis: WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, and the list is longer than what it closes. (1) FP8 AS A ROUTE IS UNTOUCHED. What is refuted is that a usable implementation already exists for the canonical architecture. The machinery does exist and is reusable: DynamicFp8Projection, the torch._scaled_mm dispatch, the arm switch, the dispatch receipt, the post-optimizer refresh, the SM89 layout check, and the #2173 per-tensor encoding that folds both scales into the kernel epilogue and removes the separate output rescale pass -- which is the cure for the wrapper cost the prior decomposition measured at 586.875 us, of which the unfused abs+reduce amax pair alone was 346.590. THREE CONSTANTS bind it to the wrong model: _FP8_W5_LAYER_COUNT 14 against 24 decoder layers, DynamicFp8UpGateProjection._shape_holds at 8H against a 2H shared_ffn, and DynamicFp8DownProjection._shape_holds at 4H against a 3072 expert_ffn_dim which is 3H. Those are ratio constants, not a rewrite. (2) THE MEASURED STEP'S OWN SITES ARE SIZED AND UNADDRESSED: contractions at the CIA shared-FFN width carry 0.2712 of leaf arithmetic, the vocabulary projection at 1024-to-32768 carries 0.0452 over 6 forward calls, and neither has ever had an FP8 arm pointed at it. (3) THE FORWARD-ONLY LIMIT IS THE STRUCTURAL ONE AND IT IS ARCHITECTURE-INDEPENDENT: _DynamicFp8ScaledMm.backward computes both dX and dW in the master dtype, so even a correctly-shaped arm caps at the 0.3334 forward share, and two thirds of the arithmetic is out of its reach by construction. An FP8 BACKWARD is a new mechanism, not an overlooked one, and it is where the remaining arithmetic lives. (4) FP16 ACCUMULATION carries the same published dense rate on this card, is not shape-bound in the same way, and nothing here speaks to it. (5) THE #1413 MATCHED-LOSS BAR IS UNCHANGED; the W5 canary cleared it at worst relative 1.169e-3 against a 1e-2 limit, but it cleared it on the 14-layer 8H model, so that adjudication does not transfer to CIA-3B any more than the installer does. (6) NO CEILING IS COMPOSED and no arm is proposed. The instrument refused to compose one and that refusal is the finding.

A forward-only design is bounded by the forward share, already measured at 0.3334; a design that also converts dX and dW is bounded by 1.0 and is unadjudicated against the #1413 loss bar.
hypotheses.criterion: Less than 0.90 of leaf arithmetic maps to a named CIA-3B weight width, in which case the partition omits an unknown amount of what a precision change must act on and no budget may be quoted from it. The instrument REFUSES at that floor rather than reporting a budget over the classified part.
hypotheses.criterion_supported_if: 0.90 or more of leaf arithmetic maps to a named width, the four classes account for the step, and the forward/backward split per class reproduces the predecessor total of 12.1658 forward against 24.3291 backward TFLOP.
hypotheses.instrument: seat record: how_much_arithmetic_is_reachable_by_precision_at_all.py
hypotheses.ruling: The frozen criterion reads: REFUTED-IF less than 0.90 of leaf arithmetic maps to a named CIA-3B weight width; SUPPORTED-IF 0.90 or more maps, the four classes account for the step, and the forward/backward split per class reproduces the predecessor total of 12.1658 forward against 24.3291 backward TFLOP. Measured classified 1.0000 with only two residual shapes totalling 0.00001 TFLOP, both named rather than bucketed. Totals 12.1658 and 24.3291 exactly. Every class is independently 1:2 forward to backward, which is the no-recompute signature holding per class and not only in aggregate. The budget: shared FFN at the 2048 width 0.6101 of leaf arithmetic, attention and square-1024 contractions 0.2543, the vocabulary projection 0.1356. A forward-only precision design is bounded by 0.3334 under a premise measured false, and only a design that converts the backward reaches beyond it.
hypotheses.not_closed: WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. (1) A SHARE IS NOT A SAVING AND NEITHER BOUND IS A CEILING ON THE TARGET. Converting arithmetic to a faster format is not making the step faster: the prior wrapper decomposition measured an FP8 arm SLOWER end to end at m4096 while its contractions were faster. No time figure follows from any share here. (2) SITE CLASS IS INFERRED FROM SHAPE and the attention_or_square_1024 class is the coarsest cell: it admits any contraction with two extents of 1024 regardless of the third, so 1024x1024x256, 1024x256x1024, 256x1024x1024 and 2048x1024x1024 all land there and some of them may not be attention. Only the module graph separates them and that read is the named successor. (3) A GENUINELY NEW ABSENCE, UNEXPLAINED: NO CONTRACTION IN THE CAPTURE CARRIES A 3072 EXTENT, so the expert FFN at expert_ffn_dim 3072 contributes zero measured arithmetic at this geometry -- while the prior strict-FP8 work profiled experts.0.layers.13.down.weight at [4096,1024,3072]. Either the experts do not execute a 3072-width contraction on the measured path, or they execute through a grouped path presenting different dimensions, and the 256 extents are the candidate. This is an OPEN QUESTION about what the governed step actually computes and it is the strongest thread this cycle produced. (4) THE #1413 BAR IS UNCHANGED AND AN FP8 BACKWARD HAS NEVER BEEN ADJUDICATED AGAINST IT. The 1.0 bound is arithmetic, not a licence; the whole numerics question sits on the two thirds it adds. (5) FP16 ACCUMULATION is untouched here and carries the same published dense rate. (6) NOTHING IS MEASURED ABOUT TRAFFIC OR OCCUPANCY at any of these classes, so whether a class is even arithmetic-bound is unestablished, and a precision change acts on nothing in a bandwidth-bound class.
hypotheses.closing: budget reported at classified 1.0000, ruled SUPPORTED against the frozen criterion, successor named: read the module graph to separate the coarse 1024-square class and explain the absent 3072 width

events.observation: Two of my own receipts disagree. The row-1 refutation states this path launches zero cudaGraphLaunch; an earlier split on this campaign reported 14,291 kernels issued from cudaGraphLaunch against 615 eager. They cannot both describe the same execution, and the run receipt names the mode resident-dynamic-capture.

events.hypothesis: A profiler records the runtime call that issued each kernel and links the two by correlation id, so which API launched the work is a reading rather than an inference. A graph-executed step shows its kernels under cudaGraphLaunch and shows the graph being built at least once under cudaStreamBeginCapture and cudaGraphInstantiate. An eager step shows neither. The disagreement is therefore settleable from the artifact at no cost.

events.refuted_if: more than a tenth of device kernels fail to join a launching runtime call by correlation id, or the graph-issued share falls between the frozen eager ceiling of 0.05 and the frozen captured floor of 0.80 -- either way the path is not readable as one regime and no word describing it would be a reading rather than a choice

events.because: The frozen criterion refuted-if reads: more than a tenth of kernels fail to join, or the graph share falls between 0.05 and 0.80. NEITHER fired. 43,984 of 44,632 kernels join, a 1.5 percent residual against a 10 percent clause, and the graph share is 0.0000, below the eager ceiling rather than between the bounds. The path is EAGER: 37,264 cudaLaunchKernel and 6,720 cuLaunchKernel, zero graph launches, and zero capture-construction calls of any kind. Both deliberate reds refuse on distinct clauses. The disagreement is settled for this trace and the row-1 clause is the one that was right.

events.observation: The harness that produced the trace every device-level measurement on this campaign reads binds a SegmentedStep and calls zero_grad and record() on it and never calls capture(). The governed runner calls capture() at cia_step_runner.py line 1434. If both readings hold, the campaign device evidence describes a path the governed treatment arm does not run.

events.hypothesis: SegmentedStep.captured returns _graphed is not None, and _graphed is assigned only inside _graph, which capture() calls. So a bound-but-uncaptured step has captured false and its step function runs the eager forward, which is exactly what the trace shows: 43,984 of 44,632 kernels joined to eager launch calls, zero graph launches, zero capture-construction calls. The runner writes capture.receipt() to capture.json, so whether the governed side captured is a READ of that file rather than an inference from its source.

The competing account is that the captured arm has its own idle from dependencies, internal streams and resource availability, in which case the lever survives at reduced size and the enumeration is merely overstated rather than void.

events.observation: Between the eager trace and the captured trace at the same head and geometry, total device time RISES from 130,566.6 to 167,963.6 us per step, +28.6 percent, on a kernel-count increase of only 6.75 percent. Capture is supposed to remove launch overhead, not add device work. Every captured-priced lever in the route set, including the 1.6940x admitted arm, is denominated in this larger device total, so if the rise is an artifact of the capture-trace instrumentation rather than a property of the path, every one of those levers is overstated and the admitted arm falls below the operator 1.5x bar.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM UNDER TEST: the rise is PER-KERNEL DURATION INFLATION on kernels common to both traces -- an instrument-side property of how the captured trace was collected (CUPTI attribution across graph replay, different profiler options, or clock/attribution differences inside a replayed graph) -- rather than the path executing different or heavier work. The discriminating fact is that 6.75 percent more kernels carry 28.6 percent more time, so mean duration rose about 20 percent, and mean duration can rise for exactly two reasons: the same kernels got slower, or the MIX shifted toward heavier kernels. Those two are separable by matching kernels across the traces BY EXACT NAME and comparing invocation-weighted mean duration on the common population only, which holds the mix constant by construction. RIVAL EXPLANATION, which the same instrument scores: graph replay genuinely changes device work -- capture can defeat a fusion, force a materialization, or alter the allocator pool so access patterns worsen -- in which case the rise is a property of the path, the captured denominators are correct, and the admitted arm stands.

events.refuted_if: FROZEN BEFORE ANY TRACE READ. Match kernels across the two traces BY EXACT SYMBOL NAME and form the COMMON population -- names present in both. For each common name compute mean duration = total device us / invocation count, in each trace separately, then the invocation-weighted mean ratio R = (sum over common names of eager_count * captured_mean) / (sum over common names of eager_count * eager_mean), which holds the MIX constant at the eager trace's own kernel counts by construction. REFUTED IF R < 1.10 -- the same kernels run at essentially the same speed, the rise is a mix or count change, and it is therefore a property of the PATH, the captured denominators stand, and the admitted arm is not threatened. SUPPORTED IF R >= 1.10. COVERAGE FLOOR, frozen here and not adjustable after the read: the common population must carry at least 0.60 of EACH trace's total device time; below that the populations are too disjoint for a matched comparison to decide anything and the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE, never REFUTED and never SUPPORTED. TIE AND MARGIN DISCIPLINE per a-strict-order-clause-meets-a-tie: no ordering clause is used at all here, only a ratio, so there is no sort and no tie to mishandle; the per-name detail is reported for the top 15 common names by eager device time so a single dominant kernel driving R is visible rather than hidden inside the weighted mean. RESIDUAL per an-op-name-filter-is-a-classifier: the instrument reports the eager-only and captured-only populations as first-class numbers with their device-time shares, and the report REFUSES if the common population falls under the floor rather than publishing the readable half.

events.because: The frozen criterion said SUPPORTED IF R >= 1.10, where R is the invocation-weighted mean duration ratio over names present in BOTH traces, weighted by the EAGER counts so the mix is constant by construction. R = 1.2889, and the coverage floor of 0.60 is not merely cleared but nearly vacuous: the common population is 143 names carrying 1.0000 of the eager device sum and 0.9975 of the captured device sum, with ZERO eager-only names and three captured-only names worth 0.25 percent. So the two traces execute the same kernel population, the kernel count rises only 1.0313x, the device sum rises 1.2822x, and the whole of that rise is per-kernel duration: 1.2889 predicted against 1.2822 observed, agreeing to 0.5 percent. Not one of the top fifteen kernels by eager device time is faster in the captured trace; the ratios run from 1.102 to 1.570 and the two largest are the grouped-expert contractions _rows and _weights at 1.570 each. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, and the criterion could not: duration inflation is consistent with CUPTI attribution across graph replay AND with a genuine device slowdown under replay, and this instrument does not separate them. Both readings are bad for the captured route pricing and they are bad in different ways, so the next cycle separates them rather than assuming the flattering one.

events.hypothesis: NOT CLOSED, and the first line is a reading that points the OPPOSITE way from the hypothesis title, which is why it is named here rather than left for whoever wants the route reopened. The title says profiler-not-path. SUPPORTED establishes duration inflation on an identical kernel population; it does NOT establish that the inflation is instrumentation. The competing reading is physical and fits the coverage numbers better: the eager trace has device coverage 0.227 at a wall of about 1.762 s per step, so its kernels run ISOLATED on a cool idle card at full clocks, while the captured trace has coverage 0.843 at a wall of about 0.187 s, near the governed step, so its kernels run back to back under sustained load with the clocks, power and L2 that implies. On that reading the captured durations are the FAITHFUL ones and the eager 131 ms was the artifact -- an underestimate produced by measuring kernels in isolation -- and the admitted arm is denominated in the better unit rather than an inflated one. That direction is favourable to me and my own record says favourable-direction errors get less scrutiny, so it is registered as a hypothesis with a test, never adopted. SUCCESSOR, analysis-only and available from the captured trace already on disk: within ONE trace, regress per-invocation duration of a single high-count kernel against the size of the device gap immediately preceding it. If duration rises with density -- shorter preceding gap, longer kernel -- the inflation is load-dependent and physical; if duration is flat against gap size, the load explanation fails and instrumentation is back in front. A single-trace test removes every between-trace confound the comparison just ran could not. So the same symbol can be observed issued eagerly and issued from inside a replayed graph, in the same session, on the same card, under the same profiler configuration. The observation this cycle tests is that mean duration for a given symbol at a given grid and block DIFFERS between the two issue modes. A SCHEMA PROBE ONLY was run before the criterion was frozen -- category counts and runtime-event names, to establish that the correlation join exists at all -- and no duration was read. Freezing a criterion against a field that does not exist wastes a cycle; reading the response variable first would be choosing the criterion to fit the answer, and that was not done.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM UNDER TEST, the INSTRUMENT reading: CUPTI attributes device time differently for kernels executed inside a replayed CUDA graph than for kernels launched one at a time, because the concurrent-kernel tracing that produces per-kernel begin and end timestamps interacts with graph replay -- serializing nodes that would otherwise overlap, or charging launch and node-traversal time into the node's own duration. If that is what produces the 1.2889x, then WITHIN the captured trace a symbol issued from a graph is measured longer than the SAME symbol at the SAME geometry issued eagerly, and the gap is the size of the artifact. RIVAL, the LOAD reading, which the same instrument scores in the opposite direction or not at all: if the 1.2889x is sustained-load physics -- clocks, power averaging, warm L2 -- then issue mode is irrelevant and the two populations agree, because a kernel does not care how it was enqueued once it is resident on the SMs. A THIRD possibility the instrument must be able to report rather than misattribute: the two populations may not be comparable at all, because the eager-issued kernels inside the captured trace are exactly the ones the capture could NOT absorb, so they may be a different kind of work in different regions of the timeline. That is a selection confound, it is named before the run, and the instrument reports the density context of each population so a reader can see it rather than take the ratio at face value.

events.because: The frozen criterion said INCONCLUSIVE if fewer than three groups are scoreable, OR the scoreable groups carry less than 0.20 of device sum, OR the unattributed population carries more than 0.10. All three fire. One scoreable group, carrying 0.0011, with 0.7531 of device time unattributed against a 0.10 ceiling. The instrument refuses. THE RESIDUAL IS THE FINDING, and it says my attribution rule was wrong in a way the numbers make exact rather than probable. Of 48,929 device events in the trace, 4,793 join to an eager launcher and 156 join to a cudaGraphLaunch, leaving 43,980 with no runtime parent at all. The eager figure is exact to the event: 3,695 cudaLaunchKernel plus 1,026 cudaMemcpyAsync plus 72 cudaMemsetAsync is 4,793. The graph figure is exact too, and that is the tell -- 156 kernels for 156 cudaGraphLaunch calls is a ONE-TO-ONE join, which is not what a graph launch does: one replay issues thousands of nodes. So a correlation id identifies a CPU-side launch call, and a kernel executed as a graph NODE has no CPU-side launch call to be correlated with. The 43,980 unattributed are not a measurement gap, they are the graph nodes, and 43,980 of 48,929 is 0.899, consistent with the 0.9224 graph share of joined kernels recorded at this head. MY RULE TREATED ABSENCE OF A PARENT AS ABSENCE OF INFORMATION when absence of a parent IS the information, which is the same shape as reading an unexpressed class as a zero. The repair is not applied to this instrument: the predecessor verdict stands INCONCLUSIVE and the corrected attribution is frozen in a named successor.

events.observation: Optimizer work (17.0 ms fused-arm median, f415) runs strictly after backward on one stream; the 72 shared-FFN owners' gradients are final at their post-accumulate hook well before the last backward kernel, so their optimizer step can shadow the remaining backward on a second stream (packet 4cb14053; dependency-idle bound 9.2 ms says L3 alone <=1.118x, <=1.06x on the idle term).

events.hypothesis: Mechanism: on one stream the step is serialized as forward -> backward -> optimizer, and the optimizer's 17.0 ms is bandwidth-bound while the backward tail is compute-bound, so the tensor cores idle during the optimizer and DRAM idles during the backward tail. Parameters whose gradient is FINAL before the backward ends (the 72 shared-FFN owners, final at their post-accumulate hook once the last chunk's backward of that layer completes) can have their fused AdamW issued on a second stream at that hook, ordered by an event recorded after the accumulate; the second stream's work overlaps the remaining backward kernels of earlier layers. The step boundary then waits on both streams once. Ceiling: at most the optimizer share that becomes hidden, bounded by the dependency-idle term 9.2 ms (<=1.06x) up to the whole 17.0 ms (<=1.118x) on f415 numbers; on K4's 165.3 ms step the same terms are smaller shares and MUST be re-measured on that source (the counterpart seat 37885: f415 is not a bound here). L3 is sub-1.5x alone by its own arithmetic and is authored only as a STACK member (rows 1+3), never dispatched as a lone arm (1945-multiplicative-movement-only clause 1).

events.refuted_if: On the K4 source (the seat's 24,190.653 governed head), a 64-update instrumented pair (control vs L3 stack member with the second-stream AdamW issued at the 72 shared-FFN owners' post-accumulate hook) shows EITHER (a) the interval union of second-stream AdamW kernels overlapping backward kernels is below 50% of those owners' measured optimizer device time, OR (b) the median complete-step wall of the treatment is not shorter than the control by at least 0.5 x that shadowed optimizer time, OR (c) the update-1 parameter/optimizer tensors differ from control beyond the licence consumer v4 floor (a reordering that changes the update is not a scheduling treatment).
events.supported_if: Overlap union >= 80% of the shadowed owners' optimizer device time AND step-median delta >= 0.8 x that time AND update-1 tensors within the v4 floor; the resulting gain is recorded as the stack member's contribution, never as a lone-arm number (sub-1.5x by its own ceiling).

events.observation: K1 (SRL1 skip/read/learn, fixed (16,8) phases) had no ceiling: its row in the fifteen reads 'undefined until the census'. The no-card census now prices it. Over the controller's own 56 phase templates the (16,8) family leaves 8 LEARN + 8 READ + 40 SKIP of 56 optional sites, removing 70.75 percent of the dimension-derived product FLOPs of the 60-site layer population (baseline 2,113,929,216 FLOP/position = 8.658 TF/update at 4,096 positions, which independently corroborates the campaign's 8.8648 TF linear count). Residual 0.0: every site in the population is priced.

events.hypothesis: LEARN costs 3x its forward products, READ 2x (parameter_for_mode detaches only the parameter view and retains the input adjoint, so dX runs and dW does not), SKIP 0x (the decoder branches before the Q/O or FFN products; attention K/V and normalisation stay mandatory). Converting that FLOP reduction to time needs the device share of the classes those products occupy: gemm_bf16 0.4103 + gemm_grouped_expert 0.1799 + softmax 0.0290 + gemm_other 0.0017 = 0.6209 of the captured trace's 157,668.8 us/step device union. Pricing out the LM head (which K1 never touches) leaves 0.6460 of all product FLOPs removed, so the device-time reduction is 0.4011 and the ceiling is 1.670x. ASSUMED, NOT MEASURED: device time inside a product class distributes as that class's FLOPs do; a per-site kernel join would settle it and has not run. Biased UP by crediting the priced products with their FLOP share of gemm_bf16; biased DOWN by pricing none of the elementwise/norm/triton work a skipped site also elides. The class table is a PROFILED trace at a different head, so this selects a route and is not a governed quantity.

events.refuted_if: The governed 1,024-measured-update run of the prepared K1-CAPTURED packet (run e499c436269c40fdb9cce00135ab0dbb, 4,096 positions/update, candidate 1945-K1-SRL1-16-8-captured-regions-v1) yields a nearest-rank p10 below 25,400 applied positions/s, i.e. below 1.05x the standing governed 24,190.653. A number at or above that is SUPPORTED as a throughput result ONLY; K1 changes what is computed rather than how, so it carries no tensor-equivalence claim and the no-worse-learning licence remains a SEPARATE unmet gate that no p10 discharges.

events.because: The frozen criterion reads: p10 below 25,400 applied positions/s REFUTES. The owned governor stopped the run at 104 accepted prefix rows (103 measured updates after the warm row) with a durable receipt whose order-statistic upper bound on the FINAL nearest-rank p10 over all 1,024 updates is 3,952.81 applied positions/s. That is a mathematical bound, not a projection: no completion of the remaining 921 updates could lift the p10 to 25,400. So the criterion is met by a factor of 6.4, and the campaign terminal of 80,000 by a factor of 20.2. K1-CAPTURED as implemented runs about 7x SLOWER than the standing governed 24,190.653, not 1.67x faster. There is NO governed 1,024-update number here: full_1024_rate is null and incomplete_1024 is true, so this arm does not join the count of the fifteen that carry one, and gate A does not move.

events.hypothesis: WHAT THE REFUTATION DOES NOT CLOSE, and the defect is MINE. The census priced what K1 REMOVES and never priced what it ADDS. treatment-selection-states-its-ceiling's 2026-09-12 amendment says in as many words that a replacement's own cost is an unknown the selection owes as a MEASUREMENT, never inferred from the incumbent and NEVER ASSUMED TO BE ZERO -- and my 1.670x assumed exactly zero. The SRL controller's own runtime is absent from every line of that arithmetic: 16 decisions per update, a policy and value forward per 256-position segment, the H=8 rollout bookkeeping, and the per-site branching the captured-regions caller must perform before each Q/O or FFN product. Measured 3,952.81 upper bound against a 24,190.653 incumbent is a 7x REGRESSION, so the unpriced additions dominate the priced removals by roughly an order of magnitude. NOT CLOSED: (a) the 70.75 percent FLOP reduction itself, which is arithmetic from frozen dimensions and stands unrefuted -- what is refuted is that it reaches the timeline through THIS caller; (b) the K1 MECHANISM, since a caller whose branching cost is proportional to site count is not the only possible one and this measures one implementation; (c) K2, K3', J1 and J3, which the order file prices off this census -- their rows inherit the same unpriced-addition defect and must not quote 1.670x; (d) whether the controller cost is fixed per update or scales with sites, which decides whether any caller can recover the reduction and is one no-card measurement away.

events.observation: K1-CAPTURED measured a roughly 7x regression where its FLOP census projected a 1.670x gain, and the census assumed the replacement's own cost to be zero. Nothing on record prices the SRL controller's own per-update runtime. Source read at the measured head: propose() computes features = causal_features(...).cpu().clone(), so every decision forces a device-to-host transfer, and the runtime's default capacity is 16 decisions per update matching 4,096 positions in 256-position segments.

events.hypothesis: A step whose design target is zero host syncs is being asked to perform 16 forced device-to-host transfers per update, each one a synchronisation against queued device work, plus 16 policy and value forwards and the H=8 rollout bookkeeping. If that machinery is a material share of the measured 1.10 s K1 row wall, the unpriced addition IS the controller and no choice of caller recovers the 70.75 percent FLOP reduction. If it is a small share, the controller is exonerated and the per-site branching in the captured-regions caller owns the regression, which makes a different caller a live arm.

events.refuted_if: The controller's own median per-update runtime, measured alone with no decoder, is below 55 ms, i.e. below 5 percent of the 1.10 s K1-CAPTURED measured row wall. That would mean the controller is NOT the dominant unpriced addition, would exonerate it, and would point the whole regression at the per-site branching of the captured-regions caller. At or above 55 ms the controller is a material term and every K-row ceiling priced off the FLOP census must carry it.
events.instrument: seat record: census_srl_controller_runtime.py

events.observation: The K1 arm ran in a custody named 1945-campaign-K1-CAPTURED and produced a measured row wall of ~1.10 s against K4's 0.1653 s governed step: a ~7x regression. Its own model.json records execution_mode: null, and its custody contains NO capture receipt. A census of all 11 campaign custodies shows every arm whose NAME contains CAPTURED has execution_mode null (K1, J2, SRL8-4), while the three L6/L7 arms record resident-dynamic-capture. The controller has just been exonerated as the dominant term at 11.265 ms/update (1.02 percent of the K1 row), so the ~7x is owned by something else.

events.hypothesis: SRL1's propose path performs three device-to-host transfers per decision (features .cpu().clone(); probabilities .cpu().cumsum; searchsorted .item()), 48 per update at 16 decisions. A CUDA graph cannot contain a device-to-host sync. So a K1 step CANNOT be captured across its decision boundaries, and the arm may have executed fully eager while carrying CAPTURED in its custody name. The campaign's own measured eager-versus-captured split is the right order of magnitude for a 7x, and it would mean K1's FLOP reduction was never the question: the arm changed execution regime, not arithmetic.

events.refuted_if: The K1 arm's own custody carries an AFFIRMATIVE assertion that capture executed -- a capture receipt with captured true, a nonzero cudaGraphLaunch or graph-replay count, or a runner field produced BY the capture call rather than by the caller's request -- in which case K1 ran inside the captured regime and the eager/captured regime change does NOT explain the ~7x, which then belongs to the per-site branching inside capture. Equally REFUTED if the three L6/L7 arms that record resident-dynamic-capture turn out to carry no affirmative capture assertion either, because then execution_mode null distinguishes nothing between the arms and the field is not evidence about K1 at all. SUPPORTED only if K1 carries no affirmative capture assertion AND at least one comparison arm on the same runner does, establishing that the assertion is producible and absent here.

events.because: Both conjuncts of the SUPPORTED clause hold on a 12-custody census. (1) The K1 arm carries NO affirmative capture-execution assertion: zero capture-named files, zero captured/segments/graph-launch fields, and model.json execution_mode null. (2) The assertion IS producible on this runner: L6-20260921T092627Z and L7-20260921T073649Z both carry capture.json with captured true and segments 13. The first REFUTED clause does not fire because K1 has no such assertion; the second does not fire because two of the mode-recording arms do carry it. Recorded against my own favour: L6-074048Z and L6-091935Z record the resident-dynamic-capture MODE and carry no capture.json either, so execution_mode is NOT the discriminator -- capture.json presence is, and the mode string remains a request rather than an event exactly as the standing rule says. This verdict establishes that the K1 arm's capture is UNEVIDENCED, not that it was eager; absence of an assertion is absence, never false.

events.hypothesis: Successor: read cia_step_runner at the K1 arm commit and determine whether capture() was CALLED on the SRL1 path and, if called, whether it refused on a device-to-host sync. That decides eager-vs-captured outright, where this census only establishes the assertion is absent. Still open: (1) absence of an assertion is absence, never proof of eager execution; (2) capture.json presence, not execution_mode, is the discriminator -- two mode-recording arms carry no capture.json, so the campaign has three regimes on record (mode+assertion, mode-only, neither) and only the first is evidenced; (3) J2-CAPTURED and SRL8-4-CAPTURED carry the same null and the same missing assertion, so every arm I have named CAPTURED shares this defect and their numbers inherit it; (4) no step-time attribution here -- if K1 did run eager, how many of the ~7x milliseconds that accounts for is unmeasured; (5) the per-site branching cost inside the caller remains unpriced either way.

events.because: Criterion met and ruled SUPPORTED on a 12-custody receipt census; the successor (runner source read at the arm commit) is registered and belongs to a fresh cycle.

events.observation: Every stack ceiling computed on this campaign EXCLUDES dense bf16 GEMM by assumption, treating it as the mandatory arithmetic no scheduling, fusion, consolidation or overlap treatment can touch. Today that assumption became the binding one. The exposed-time table puts dense GEMM at 50,322.0 us/step, 31.9 percent of the 157,668.8 us captured device union and the largest single class. The exact leave-N-out table says the terminal needs ELEVEN of the remaining classes removed perfectly, and the required-effectiveness scan says the two-member bar-clearing stack needs 99.5 percent removal of both members while at a realistic 50 percent no stack up to six members clears the 1.5x bar at all, topping out at 1.4020x. So the removable classes do not reach the bar at achievable effectiveness, and the one quantity every table has set aside by construction is the largest one. The route-set enumeration of 2026-09-15 already names FP16 accumulation as a route OUTSIDE the enumeration because nothing has measured it, records that it carries the same published dense rate on Ada as FP8, and records that I previously and wrongly described it as unavailable. It has still never been measured.

events.hypothesis: Mechanism: on Ada consumer silicon the tensor cores run half-rate when a 16-bit matmul accumulates in FP32, and full-rate when it accumulates in 16-bit, which is why FP8 and FP16 are quoted at the same published dense figure. CIA-3B dense projections run bf16 inputs with FP32 accumulation, so if the published relationship holds at the shapes this model actually executes, an FP16-input FP16-accumulate matmul would roughly halve the dense GEMM class. CEILING, stated before authoring per treatment-selection-states-its-ceiling and computed against the captured union: at a perfect 2.0x rate the class falls 50,322.0 -> 25,161.0 us and the step becomes 132,507.8 us, which is 1.190x. At the 1.5x rate this hypothesis sets as its floor the step is 140,895.1 us, which is 1.119x. BOTH ARE BELOW THE OPERATOR 1.5x BAR, so this is a MEASUREMENT that sizes a lever, never an arm, and it may not be dispatched as a lone arm under 1945-multiplicative-movement-only clause 1. Its value is that it is the only lever anyone has named on 31.9 percent of the timeline, it is cheap, and a refutation removes the largest standing unknown. The FP8 precedent is the reason the floor is set below the published premise rather than at it: the 2.0x tensor-rate premise was NOT observed at either measured FP8 site, so a published rate is a hypothesis about this card and not an input.

events.refuted_if: At the dense projection shapes actually executed in the captured trace, enumerated from the trace operand dimensions rather than chosen, an FP16-input FP16-accumulate matmul measured against a bf16-input FP32-accumulate matmul at the SAME shapes, same layout, same device, with warmup discarded and the median of at least 30 timed repeats per shape, shows a geometric-mean achieved-rate ratio BELOW 1.50. A ratio below 1.50 refutes the hypothesis that this class is compressible by accumulation width on this card, and the class stays mandatory in every table.
events.supported_if: The geometric-mean achieved-rate ratio over the enumerated dense shapes is AT OR ABOVE 1.50, with the per-shape ratios published so a single favourable shape cannot carry the mean. SUPPORT sizes the lever and licenses nothing further: it makes FP16 accumulation a candidate STACK MEMBER whose numerical admissibility under the unchanged #1413 loss bar is a separate question this probe does not touch, and whose ceiling stays below the bar alone.
events.instrument: seat record: fp16_accumulate_rate_at_the_dense_shapes.py -- an isolated-shape probe, no governed run, no capture, shapes enumerated from the captured trace; the GPU window is opened against this hypothesis id through gpu_window.sh

events.note: fp16-accumulate isolated-shape rate probe over 14 certified dense shapes, deliberate red first, ~6 min

events.because: The frozen criterion reads: shows a geometric-mean achieved-rate ratio BELOW 1.50. A ratio below 1.50 refutes the hypothesis that this class is compressible by accumulation width on this card. The measured geometric mean is 0.9731, which is below 1.50 -- and it may NOT be read as the refutation that clause describes, because the clause presupposes that FP16 accumulation executed and the instrument proved it did not. The probe's own execution-fingerprint clause refused at 2 of 2 large-K shapes: the treatment arm's relative error came out 8x SMALLER than baseline (3.60e-04 against 2.88e-03, err_ratio 0.13) where FP16 accumulation requires it LARGER. The cause is an instrument defect of mine, not a property of the card: the treatment arm changes TWO things against the baseline, operand dtype bf16->fp16 AND accumulation width, and fp16 carries 10 mantissa bits against bf16's 7, so input precision dominates the error and structurally masks any accumulation signal. The deliberate red and the real run are indistinguishable on the fingerprint (0.126 against 0.125 at the same shape), which is the direct proof that the clause does not discriminate its control from its treatment. Reporting 0.9731 as REFUTED would be exactly the defect this probe was built to prevent -- a hypothesis refuted by an instrument that never tested it. INCONCLUSIVE is the run that did not discriminate, which is what this is.

events.hypothesis: WHAT THE INCONCLUSIVE DOES NOT CLOSE. (1) It does not refute FP16 accumulation on the dense class. The lever is UNMEASURED on this card, not measured and found wanting, and the registry row says so. (2) It does not show the two arms ran the same kernel -- at M=1024 K=32768 N=1024 the real run scored 4.64e-04 against the red run's 3.63e-04 at the identical shape, so the flag DID change something at large K. It changed too little to be an accumulation-width change, which fits what the flag actually governs. (3) It leaves the flag's true scope identified but unproven: allow_fp16_reduced_precision_reduction permits reduced precision in the SPLIT-K REDUCTION, not in the tensor-core accumulate type, and torch.mm may expose no knob for the latter at all. That is a source claim and it is unread. (4) The rate half is a real negative and survives on its own terms: fp16 and bf16 operands run at the same rate on this card across all 14 shapes, geometric mean 0.9731 with no shape above 1.37. A dtype swap alone buys nothing, so any FP16 win must come from accumulation width, which is precisely what was not tested. (5) The 14-shape certified set, the timing harness and the fingerprint METHOD all stand; only the fingerprint's arm construction is defective. THE SUCCESSOR holds input dtype CONSTANT at fp16 in both arms and varies only accumulation, so the error difference can carry no mantissa-width component. Since torch.mm does not select compute type, the treatment arm must reach cuBLAS directly through ctypes with CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F against CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F, and the fingerprint becomes: same operands, same shape, treatment error materially larger at large K. It ships with the same deliberate red and it does not inherit this criterion -- a criterion is never amended after the numbers arrive, so the successor freezes its own before it is authored. Gate A unmoved, UNMET, p10 24,190.653.

events.observation: The class-name audit reads the attention kernels by symbol: fmha_cutlassB_bf16_aligned_64x64_k64_seqaligned_sm80 PyTorchMemEffAttention AttentionBackwardKernel at 10,690.1 us/step over 24 calls, and fmha_cutlassF_bf16_aligned_64x64_rf_sm80 AttentionKernel at 3,655.1 us/step over 24 calls, together 14,345.3 us = 22.17 percent of the gemm_bf16 class. Two facts sit beside that. First, a receipted hypothesis measured the attention block at 0.31-0.39 of this card published dense bf16 rate and was REFUTED for it, while the s1688 dense kernels and the grouped expert path run near 0.92. Second, these are the MEM-EFFICIENT cutlass kernels compiled for sm80 running on an sm89 card, and cia_step_runner.attention_context already carries an unused SDPBackend.CUDNN_ATTENTION branch plus a --attention-backend dispatcher flag. The governed arm leaves the selection at unforced, which resolved to mem-efficient.

events.hypothesis: Mechanism: SDPA backend selection is made by a dispatcher heuristic, not by measurement on this card. The unforced path resolved to the PyTorch mem-efficient cutlass FMHA implementation, whose kernels here are sm80 tiles at a fixed 64x64 block with a 2.92x backward-to-forward time ratio (10,690.1 vs 3,655.1 us). cuDNN fused attention ships sm89-tuned kernels and a different backward formulation. If backend selection is where the efficiency gap lives, forcing CUDNN_ATTENTION at the same shapes should raise achieved rate materially; if it is not, the gap is algorithmic or shape-driven and backend selection is not the lever. CEILING, stated before authoring per treatment-selection-states-its-ceiling: the whole attention class is 14,345.3 us of a 157,668.8 us captured device union, so driving attention time to ZERO is at most 1.100x on the step. This is therefore SUB-1.5x by arithmetic and is NOT dispatchable as a lone arm under 1945-multiplicative-movement-only clause 1. What is authored here is a LEVER-SIZING MEASUREMENT at isolated shapes, the same shape as the fp16-accumulation probe, never an arm.

events.refuted_if: At the attention operand shapes actually executed in the captured trace, enumerated from the trace records rather than chosen, cuDNN fused attention measured against the mem-efficient cutlass FMHA path at the SAME shapes, same dtype, same causal convention, same device, forward and backward scored SEPARATELY, with warmup discarded and the median of at least 30 timed repeats per shape, shows a geometric-mean rate ratio (mem_efficient_us / cudnn_us) BELOW 1.25 on the FORWARD+BACKWARD total. Below 1.25 refutes the hypothesis that backend selection is where the attention efficiency gap lives, and the 0.31-0.39 of published figure then stands as algorithmic or shape-driven rather than as a selection defect. The bar is 1.25 because attention runs at 0.31-0.39 of published while the dense s1688 kernels run near 0.92; closing even one third of that gap requires about 1.25x, and a ratio below it means the backend is not the explanation. EXECUTION IS PROVEN BY KERNEL SYMBOL, NOT BY THE FLAG: the treatment arm must emit kernel symbols containing cudnn and must emit ZERO fmha_cutlass symbols; if the dispatcher silently falls back to mem-efficient, both arms ran the same kernel and the run REFUSES rather than reporting a ratio. Per-shape ratios are published so one favourable shape cannot carry the mean.

events.note: cudnn vs mem-efficient attention rate at the one executed shape, deliberate red first, ~4 min

events.because: The frozen criterion reads: REFUTED IF the geometric-mean rate ratio (mem_efficient_us / cudnn_us) on the FORWARD+BACKWARD total is BELOW 1.25. Measured 1.0043, and the forward-only ratio is 0.9258 meaning cuDNN is SLOWER in the forward direction. Both are below 1.25, so the hypothesis is REFUTED. The verdict is trustworthy because the execution fingerprint PASSED on the real run and FIRED on the deliberate red: the treatment emitted cudnn_generated_fort_native_sdpa_sm80_flash_fprop_wmma_f16 and flash_bprop plus two cudnn::fusion kernels with ZERO fmha_cutlass symbols, while the unforced red arm emitted only fmha_cutlass and was refused before any ratio was computed. So this compared two genuinely different kernels and found them within 0.4 percent on the forward+backward total: 652.7 us mem-efficient against 649.9 us cuDNN at 4x16x1024x64 causal bf16. Backend selection is NOT where the attention block 0.31-0.39 of published rate lives.

events.hypothesis: WHAT THIS REFUTATION DOES NOT CLOSE. (1) The attention efficiency gap itself is unexplained and still open: the block runs at 0.31-0.39 of published dense bf16 while the s1688 dense kernels run near 0.92, and this removes only ONE candidate explanation. Two backends built by different vendors landing within 0.4 percent is positive evidence that the limit is STRUCTURAL to the computation at this shape -- a 64-wide head dimension, a causal mask discarding about half the score matrix, and softmax and masking traffic between two contractions -- rather than a defect in either implementation. Which of those carries the gap is unmeasured. (2) The FLASH_ATTENTION backend is unmeasured; only cuDNN against mem-efficient was compared. Notably BOTH kernels are sm80 builds on an sm89 card -- the cuDNN symbol reads cudnn_generated_fort_native_sdpa_sm80_flash -- so the sm80-on-Ada observation that motivated this hypothesis is TRUE OF BOTH ARMS and was never the discriminator it appeared to be. A genuinely sm89-tuned or FA2 kernel is a different question. (3) Head dimension 64 at sequence 1024 is a shape choice, not a law; whether the gap narrows at a larger head dimension is a MODEL ARCHITECTURE question, changes the parameter count and the learning contract, and is outside any scheduling treatment. (4) SUB-1.5x REGARDLESS: even a perfect attention treatment is at most 1.100x on the captured step by the ceiling stated before authoring, so nothing in this direction is dispatchable as a lone arm under 1945-multiplicative-movement-only clause 1 -- true before the measurement and unchanged by it. (5) No governed number: gate A remains UNMET at p10 24,190.653 and the composite stays 10 percent.

events.hypothesis: AN INVOCATION COUNT IS A PROXY FOR THE PRECISION OF A FITTED SLOPE, AND IT IS A BAD ONE. The standard error of an OLS slope is the residual standard deviation divided by the square root of the predictor's total sum of squares, so it falls with BOTH the number of points and the spread of the predictor. A group with 122 invocations spanning 0.24 of busy fraction can resolve a slope better than one with 200 invocations spanning 0.10, and a count floor scores them the opposite way. Replacing the proxy with the quantity it stands in for should admit the heavy, high-spread groups the count floor excludes, without admitting groups whose predictor does not move -- the IQR clause still handles those. THE TRAP THIS DESIGN MUST AVOID, named before it is built: a precision floor stated as 'the slope must be several standard errors from zero' would select groups BY THE SIZE OF THEIR SLOPE and bias the pooled score upward, which is the same defect as choosing a criterion to fit an answer. So scoreability is defined as a RESOLUTION floor that depends only on the predictor spread and the residual noise and NOT on the fitted slope's value: can this group's design resolve a stated fractional change in duration across its own observed predictor span. A group with a slope of exactly zero and a group with a large one are scoreable or unscoreable on identical grounds.

hypotheses.explanation: AN INVOCATION COUNT IS A PROXY FOR THE PRECISION OF A FITTED SLOPE, AND IT IS A BAD ONE. The standard error of an OLS slope is the residual standard deviation divided by the square root of the predictor's total sum of squares, so it falls with BOTH the number of points and the spread of the predictor. A group with 122 invocations spanning 0.24 of busy fraction can resolve a slope better than one with 200 invocations spanning 0.10, and a count floor scores them the opposite way. Replacing the proxy with the quantity it stands in for should admit the heavy, high-spread groups the count floor excludes, without admitting groups whose predictor does not move -- the IQR clause still handles those. THE TRAP THIS DESIGN MUST AVOID, named before it is built: a precision floor stated as 'the slope must be several standard errors from zero' would select groups BY THE SIZE OF THEIR SLOPE and bias the pooled score upward, which is the same defect as choosing a criterion to fit an answer. So scoreability is defined as a RESOLUTION floor that depends only on the predictor spread and the residual noise and NOT on the fitted slope's value: can this group's design resolve a stated fractional change in duration across its own observed predictor span. A group with a slope of exactly zero and a group with a large one are scoreable or unscoreable on identical grounds.
hypotheses.criterion: FROZEN BEFORE ANY TRACE IS READ FOR THIS CYCLE. IDENTICAL TO THE PREDECESSOR IN EVERYTHING BUT THE SCOREABILITY FLOOR, so the two are directly comparable: same unit (group keyed by trace, symbol, grid, block), same predictor (device busy fraction over the 5,000 us immediately preceding each invocation's start, union of kernel/gpu_memcpy/gpu_memset clipped to that window over 5,000), same score (OLS of duration on busy fraction, read as predicted duration at the group's OWN p90 busy over predicted at its OWN p10), same pooling (group scores weighted by group device time), same effect line (REFUTED below 1.05, SUPPORTED at or above), same sign clause (at least two thirds of scoreable groups share the pooled sign, else INCONCLUSIVE), same coverage floor (fewer than 3 scoreable groups OR scoreable share below 0.30 of that arm's pooled device time -> INCONCLUSIVE), same per-arm scoring and the same agreement clause across arms. THE ONE CHANGE: the 200-invocation floor is REPLACED by a RESOLUTION floor. A group is scoreable if its busy-fraction IQR is at least 0.10 AND its design can resolve a 5 percent change in duration across its own observed predictor span -- formally, the standard error of the fitted slope multiplied by the group's p90-minus-p10 busy span, divided by the predicted duration at its p10, is at most 0.05. THE FLOOR DEPENDS ONLY ON PREDICTOR SPREAD AND RESIDUAL NOISE AND NEVER ON THE FITTED SLOPE'S VALUE: a group whose slope is exactly zero and one whose slope is large are scoreable or unscoreable on identical grounds, so the floor cannot select groups by the size of the effect it is measuring. No invocation count appears in any clause. Counts are still REPORTED per group so the change in the admitted population is readable. THE PREDECESSOR'S INCONCLUSIVE STANDS AS ISSUED; this is a named successor, not a repair applied in place, and if this design also fails its coverage floor that is an INCONCLUSIVE too and not a third attempt at the same answer.

hypotheses.not_closed:
WHAT THIS REFUTATION DOES NOT CLOSE.

1. IT DOES NOT CLOSE THE DENSITY MECHANISM. The effect is REAL IN SIGN and small in size: 49 of 58 scoreable groups above 1.00, pooled 1.0354 across each group's own p10-to-p90 busy span. REFUTED here means it is below the 1.05 line this cycle froze as meaningful, NOT that density has no effect on kernel duration. A future cycle that wants a smaller effect line must say so before it reads anything, and must explain why 1.05 was the wrong line on grounds other than the answer it produced.

2. IT IS A STATEMENT ABOUT SPAN, NOT ABOUT THE ARMS' DENSITY DIFFERENCE. Each group is scored across ITS OWN observed p10-to-p90 busy span inside ONE trace. The eager arm's whole-trace coverage is 0.2343 and the captured arm's is 0.8025, a difference of 0.5682 -- far wider than any within-trace group span. events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. An ADD/ADD conflict is reported whenever a path is absent at the merge base and present on both sides, REGARDLESS of whether the two sides' blobs agree. Git reports it as a conflict because there is no base to three-way merge against, not because the content differs. Both branches descend from the same seat's work in the same duo period and four of the five add/add paths are TEST files binding the same plan and checkpoint schemas, which is exactly the population most likely to have been added identically or near-identically on both sides. So the eight-path count is an upper bound on the real integration and the load-bearing number is how many paths have DIFFERENT blobs on the two sides. THE TRAP THIS MUST NOT FALL INTO, named before the measurement: a lower conflict count is the flattering answer, and my own record says both of my errors on an unwanted result ran favourable, so the count must be produced by comparing blob object ids rather than by reading diffs and judging them small. Two paths whose blobs differ by one line are still a content conflict and are counted as one; 'nearly identical' is not a category this instrument may have. THE SECOND TRAP: this is a claim about the SIZE of an integration, not about whether the merged tree is CORRECT. A clean textual merge of three runner modules can still be semantically wrong, and nothing measured here licenses running anything against the result. THE THIRD: the measurement must not mutate either worktree. <host-local path> is never changed, and the merge itself is computed with git merge-tree, which writes objects and no refs and touches no working tree.
