events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. Triton compiles each @triton.jit kernel to a cubin and exposes num_regs, n_spills and shared bytes on the compiled object, so registers per thread and static shared memory are readable WITHOUT launching anything. On compute capability 8.9 an SM carries 65,536 32-bit registers, 102,400 bytes of usable shared memory, 1,536 resident threads and 48 resident warps, with registers allocated per warp in granules. Occupancy therefore has four independent ceilings -- registers, shared memory, the thread cap and the warp cap -- and the kernel is REGISTER-LIMITED only if the register ceiling is strictly the binding one. If shared memory or a hardware cap binds first, then halving register pressure buys nothing and the lever's name describes a mechanism the kernels do not have. THE TRAP, named before the measurement: this is my own above-bar arm and a SUPPORTED answer flatters it, so every ceiling must be computed for ALL FOUR limiters and the binding one reported, never just the register one. Reporting the register ceiling alone would make registers look binding by construction -- the same defect as a filter reporting only the class it can express. THE SECOND TRAP: a compiled register count is a static property of one compilation, not an achieved occupancy on a running kernel; it bounds occupancy from above and says nothing about what the scheduler actually resident. THE THIRD: the compilation must use the SAME constexpr tile and num_warps the production call site passes, or it measures a kernel that does not run.

events.refuted_if: FROZEN BEFORE ANY COMPILATION. Both kernels are compiled at the PRODUCTION call-site configuration read from src/ember/model/ember_v0_grouped_capture.py lines 91-118 -- BM=64, BN=128, BK=32, num_warps=4, and NC=0 for _weights -- not at the default constexpr values in their signatures. For each kernel the resident-block ceiling is computed for ALL FOUR limiters on compute capability 8.9: registers (65,536 32-bit registers per SM, allocated per warp in 256-register granules), static shared memory (102,400 bytes per SM), the resident-thread cap (1,536) and the resident-warp cap (48), plus the 24-block-per-SM cap. REFUTED if the REGISTER ceiling is not STRICTLY the smallest of those five for BOTH kernels -- that is, refuted if for either kernel some other limiter binds at or below the register ceiling, because then halving register pressure buys no occupancy and the lever's name describes a mechanism its kernels do not have. Also REFUTED if the report omits any of the five ceilings, since publishing only the register ceiling would make registers binding by construction. Also REFUTED if either kernel reports n_spills greater than zero, because a spilling kernel is bound by local-memory traffic rather than by occupancy and the lever's arithmetic would then be about a different quantity. Also REFUTED if the compiled configuration does not match the production call site exactly.

events.because: The frozen criterion reads: 'REFUTED if the REGISTER ceiling is not STRICTLY the smallest of those five for BOTH kernels -- that is, refuted if for either kernel some other limiter binds at or below the register ceiling, because then halving register pressure buys no occupancy'. It does not bind strictly, for either kernel, and the reason is a TIE. Measured at the production configuration BM=64, BN=128, BK=32, num_warps=4: _rows uses 128 registers per thread and _weights 126, both with ZERO spilled bytes, and both use 24,576 bytes of static shared memory. On compute capability 8.9 that gives, per kernel, a register ceiling of 4 resident blocks per SM and a SHARED-MEMORY ceiling of exactly 4 as well, against 12 from the resident-thread cap, 12 from the resident-warp cap and 24 from the block cap. Registers and shared memory bind TOGETHER at 4 blocks per SM, which is 16 of 48 warps, an occupancy ceiling of 0.3333. So the lever two_register_limited_kernels_halved is INERT ON ITS OWN: halving register pressure on either kernel moves nothing, because shared memory holds occupancy at exactly the same 4 blocks. The premise is half true -- registers ARE a binding limiter -- and the lever as named is not, because relieving one of two tied limiters changes no ceiling. Every other clause holds: all five ceilings are reported rather than the register one alone; neither kernel spills; the compiled configuration is the call site's at ember_v0_grouped_capture.py lines 91 and 115, not the 32/64/32 defaults in the signatures; and an absent register count is refused as UNSUPPORTED rather than reported as a zero, which fired on the first run and was cured before this verdict. THE REFUTATION RUNS AGAINST MY OWN ARM: this is the third lever of the only above-bar combination on the board.

events.hypothesis: WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, AND THE SUCCESSOR IT NAMES. (a) THE NAMED SUCCESSOR IS A JOINT LEVER, not a register one: registers and shared memory tie at 4 blocks per SM, so the only treatment that can raise occupancy at all must relieve BOTH. num_stages=3 at a 24,576-byte shared footprint is the obvious handle and it is UNMEASURED -- fewer stages lowers shared memory and may raise or lower register pressure, and which way is a compilation question answerable by the same instrument at a different configuration. That successor is named and not run here. (b) OCCUPANCY IS NOT TIME. Even a treatment that doubles resident blocks does not halve either kernel's duration; occupancy and duration are different quantities and the lever's ceiling arithmetic is separately owed. Nothing here prices anything. (c) A COMPILED CEILING IS NOT AN ACHIEVED OCCUPANCY. These are hardware maxima; what the scheduler made resident during the governed step is unmeasured and no occupancy counter is read anywhere on this campaign. (d) IT DOES NOT REFUTE THE 1.6940x COMBINATION, it refutes the NAME and the assumed mechanism of one of its three levers. The combination's factor is inherited arithmetic about device time and stands as such; what falls is the claim that the third lever's gain comes from register relief, and with it the plausibility that the lever is implementable as described. (e) A PRIOR ROW NEEDS CORRECTING AND IS CORRECTED HERE RATHER THAN EDITED: the-28361us-grouped-expert-blind-spot-resolves-from-source-honest-name-32x64x32-tiles-20260921 reports the tile geometry as BM=32, BN=64, BK=32. Those are the DEFAULT constexpr values in the kernel signatures; the production call site passes BM=64, BN=128, BK=32, num_warps=4. The row read the branch it saw rather than the one that runs, and its tile figure is superseded by this measurement. (f) ONE COMPILATION, ONE TOOLCHAIN. Triton 3.5.0 on sm89; a different version can allocate registers differently and no matched-run variation is claimed. (g) Gate A is unmoved and remains UNMET at p10 24,190.653 positions/s; composite 10 percent.

events.observation: The compiled measurement an hour ago found both grouped kernels pinned at exactly 4 resident blocks per SM by TWO limiters at once: registers (128 and 126 per thread, zero spills) and static shared memory (24,576 bytes), against 12 from the thread cap, 12 from the warp cap and 24 from the block cap. Four blocks of four warps is 16 of 48 resident warps, an occupancy ceiling of 0.3333. Because the two bind together, the lever named two_register_limited_kernels_halved is inert on its own -- relieving one tied limiter changes no ceiling. The shared footprint is a direct consequence of num_stages=3 at a 64x128x32 bf16 tile, and num_stages has never been varied or measured on this campaign; the registry carries no row for it.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. Triton's software pipeline allocates one shared-memory buffer per stage for each operand tile, so shared bytes fall roughly linearly with num_stages while register pressure moves the other way or not at all -- fewer in-flight stages means fewer live accumulator and address registers, but also less latency hiding. Raising num_warps splits the same output tile across more warps, cutting registers per thread while multiplying the per-block register and warp cost, so it can move the ceiling in either direction. Since the two limiters tie today, a configuration helps ONLY if it lifts BOTH at once, and the quantity that matters is RESIDENT WARPS PER SM -- blocks times num_warps -- not resident blocks, because halving blocks while doubling warps per block is exactly no change. THE TRAPS, named before the run. (1) MEASURING BLOCKS INSTEAD OF WARPS would report a num_warps=8 configuration as worse when it is identical; the metric is frozen as resident warps. (2) CHANGING THE TILE WOULD BE A DIFFERENT TREATMENT: BM, BN and BK stay at the production 64x128x32 so the grid, the work decomposition and the arithmetic are unchanged and only the pipeline and warp mapping vary. (3) A SPILLING CONFIGURATION IS NOT AN IMPROVEMENT however high its occupancy, because spilled registers move the bottleneck to local memory; any configuration with nonzero spills is excluded and the exclusion is REPORTED rather than silent. (4) OCCUPANCY IS NOT TIME and this cannot price anything; a raised ceiling is a candidate, not a gain.

events.refuted_if: FROZEN BEFORE ANY COMPILATION. The grid is the full cross product of num_stages in {1,2,3,4,5} and num_warps in {4,8} with BM=64, BN=128, BK=32 held at the production values, compiled for BOTH kernels (_weights at NC=0). The frozen metric is RESIDENT WARPS PER SM = (minimum resident blocks per SM over all five limiters) x num_warps, capped at 48, and every one of the five ceilings is reported for every configuration. A configuration is ADMISSIBLE only if BOTH kernels compile and BOTH report ZERO spilled bytes; an inadmissible configuration is reported with its reason and never silently dropped. REFUTED if no admissible configuration reaches resident warps STRICTLY GREATER THAN 16 for BOTH kernels, where 16 is the production configuration's measured ceiling. Also REFUTED if the report ranks configurations by resident BLOCKS rather than by resident WARPS, since that metric would score a warp-count change as an improvement or a regression when it is neither. Also REFUTED if any configuration's tile differs from 64x128x32, because that would be a different treatment and not this one. Also REFUTED if a register count or a spill count comes back UNSUPPORTED for any compiled configuration and is entered as a zero rather than excluding that configuration and saying so.

One does. num_stages=2 with num_warps=8 at the frozen 64x128x32 tile reaches 24 resident warps per SM on both kernels -- occupancy ceiling 0.5000 against the production 0.3333, a 1.5x increase in the ceiling -- with ZERO spilled bytes on either kernel. events.hypothesis: WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, AND THE SUCCESSOR IT NAMES. (a) OCCUPANCY IS NOT TIME, and this is the whole gap between a candidate and a treatment. A 1.5x ceiling says more warps MAY be resident; it does not say either kernel runs faster, and num_stages=2 gives strictly less latency hiding per warp than 3, which can run slower at higher occupancy. The named successor is a measured DURATION for both kernels at stages=2/warps=8 against stages=3/warps=4 at the production shapes, and no ceiling arithmetic is stated until that exists -- an incumbent class's time bounds the SAVINGS available and bounds a replacement's own cost from neither direction. (b) IT IS A DECLARED NUMERICAL TREATMENT AND NEEDS THE LICENCE INSTRUMENT. Changing num_warps changes how the output tile is split across warps and changing num_stages changes accumulation order; _weights carries an explicit bf16 rounding boundary per chunk in its NC branch, written to match a reference. So this cannot be run as an arm on the strength of an occupancy number -- it is a candidate for the licence pair, not a shortcut past it. (c) THE SHAPES USED TO COMPILE ARE NOT THE PRODUCTION SHAPES. Register allocation does not depend on them, which is why the sweep is valid for ceilings; a DURATION measurement is meaningless at 256x256x256 and must use the governed geometry. hypotheses.observation: The compiled measurement an hour ago found both grouped kernels pinned at exactly 4 resident blocks per SM by TWO limiters at once: registers (128 and 126 per thread, zero spills) and static shared memory (24,576 bytes), against 12 from the thread cap, 12 from the warp cap and 24 from the block cap. Four blocks of four warps is 16 of 48 resident warps, an occupancy ceiling of 0.3333. Because the two bind together, the lever named two_register_limited_kernels_halved is inert on its own -- relieving one tied limiter changes no ceiling. The shared footprint is a direct consequence of num_stages=3 at a 64x128x32 bf16 tile, and num_stages has never been varied or measured on this campaign; the registry carries no row for it.
hypotheses.explanation: MECHANISM. Triton's software pipeline allocates one shared-memory buffer per stage for each operand tile, so shared bytes fall roughly linearly with num_stages while register pressure moves the other way or not at all -- fewer in-flight stages means fewer live accumulator and address registers, but also less latency hiding. Raising num_warps splits the same output tile across more warps, cutting registers per thread while multiplying the per-block register and warp cost, so it can move the ceiling in either direction. Since the two limiters tie today, a configuration helps ONLY if it lifts BOTH at once, and the quantity that matters is RESIDENT WARPS PER SM -- blocks times num_warps -- not resident blocks, because halving blocks while doubling warps per block is exactly no change. THE TRAPS, named before the run. (1) MEASURING BLOCKS INSTEAD OF WARPS would report a num_warps=8 configuration as worse when it is identical; the metric is frozen as resident warps. (2) CHANGING THE TILE WOULD BE A DIFFERENT TREATMENT: BM, BN and BK stay at the production 64x128x32 so the grid, the work decomposition and the arithmetic are unchanged and only the pipeline and warp mapping vary. (3) A SPILLING CONFIGURATION IS NOT AN IMPROVEMENT however high its occupancy, because spilled registers move the bottleneck to local memory; any configuration with nonzero spills is excluded and the exclusion is REPORTED rather than silent. (4) OCCUPANCY IS NOT TIME and this cannot price anything; a raised ceiling is a candidate, not a gain.
hypotheses.criterion: FROZEN BEFORE ANY COMPILATION. The grid is the full cross product of num_stages in {1,2,3,4,5} and num_warps in {4,8} with BM=64, BN=128, BK=32 held at the production values, compiled for BOTH kernels (_weights at NC=0). The frozen metric is RESIDENT WARPS PER SM = (minimum resident blocks per SM over all five limiters) x num_warps, capped at 48, and every one of the five ceilings is reported for every configuration. A configuration is ADMISSIBLE only if BOTH kernels compile and BOTH report ZERO spilled bytes; an inadmissible configuration is reported with its reason and never silently dropped. REFUTED if no admissible configuration reaches resident warps STRICTLY GREATER THAN 16 for BOTH kernels, where 16 is the production configuration's measured ceiling. Also REFUTED if the report ranks configurations by resident BLOCKS rather than by resident WARPS, since that metric would score a warp-count change as an improvement or a regression when it is neither. Also REFUTED if any configuration's tile differs from 64x128x32, because that would be a different treatment and not this one. Also REFUTED if a register count or a spill count comes back UNSUPPORTED for any compiled configuration and is entered as a zero rather than excluding that configuration and saying so.

events.observation: The sweep just named stages=2/warps=8 as a candidate that lifts the grouped kernels' occupancy ceiling 16 -> 24 resident warps. The named successor was a measured DURATION. Before spending it, the registry query on the class's own nouns returned grouped-expert-path-achieved-compute-rate-20260914: the whole grouped path already runs at 154.0 TF/s, 0.932 of the published 165.2 dense bf16 reference, over 18,068.1 us per step of a 130,566.9 us whole-trace device union. events.hypothesis: If a treatment is CONFINED to one class, the most it can move the step is bounded by that class's entire share -- total elimination -- and that bound is computable from receipts already on disk with no card and no new trace. The trap named before any number is read: the tempting denominator is the GOVERNED step (175,190 us or 4096/24190.653 = 169,320 us), which composes a profiled device census with a governed receipt across exactly the boundary the evidence contract forbids. So the bound is taken INSIDE one trace, on device time alone: device union is smaller than the step, and removing a fixed X from a smaller total gives a LARGER ratio, so a device-only bound is GENEROUS to the candidate. If it refuses even there, it refuses everywhere. Second trap: the achieved-rate figure counts USEFUL FLOPs while the kernel pads each group to a 64-row block, so the true achieved fraction is at or ABOVE 0.932 -- again generous to the candidate. Third: this is a bound on the CLASS, not a claim that any particular treatment reaches it; occupancy is not time and no duration is asserted.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED if that total-elimination ceiling is at or above 1.50, computed from the SAME trace that produced both quantities. Also REFUTED if the two quantities do not come from one trace, or if the grouped class's us-per-step figure cannot be reproduced from the symbol census independently of the FLOP-model route.
events.supported_if: SUPPORTED if the total-elimination ceiling on device time -- whole_device_union / (whole_device_union - grouped_class_us) -- is strictly below 1.50, so no treatment confined to the grouped expert class can clear the operator's bar as a standalone arm and stages=2/warps=8 is a STACK MEMBER ONLY.

events.because: Quoting the frozen criterion: SUPPORTED if the total-elimination ceiling on device time -- whole_device_union / (whole_device_union - grouped_class_us) -- is strictly below 1.50. It is 1.1606x. Inside one trace (cia-captured-trace-20260914T183257Z.json, all three receipts), device union 130,566.9 us per step, grouped expert class 18,068.1 us per step, share 0.1384. The two-route clause holds EXACTLY: the shape-joined FLOP model, the partition assignment and raw kernel-symbol aggregation all return 18,068.1 (_rows 11,510.0 + _weights 6,558.1), so the class figure does not rest on one model. The bound is generous to the candidate three independent ways -- device union rather than the larger governed step, useful-FLOP accounting that understates the achieved rate, and total elimination rather than any achievable saving -- and it refuses anyway. The realistic rate-only figure is far smaller: at the published dense bf16 rate the class would give back 1,228.6 us for 1.0095x, because it already runs at 0.932 of that rate. Deliberate red tightens the bar to an unsatisfiable 1.00 and REFUSES at exit 1 into a separate file, leaving the same-trace and two-route clauses armed.

events.hypothesis: THE SUCCESSOR THIS NAMES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT CLOSE. The arithmetic here is not specific to the grouped class: for ANY class, elimination clears a bar B only if the class's share of device time is at least 1 - 1/B, which at B=1.50 is 0.3333. That threshold is computable for every class in the same table in one pass, and it decides -- before any treatment is named -- which single-class confinements are refused by arithmetic and which are not. THE NAMED SUCCESSOR IS THAT WHOLE-TABLE BOUND: every class, its share, its total-elimination ceiling, and a binary of whether any confinement to it could ever clear the bar. Widen before narrowing; running it on one class and stopping is how a vocabulary misses the answer. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. (a) IT SAYS NOTHING ABOUT A STACK. The 1.5x bar governs a STANDALONE arm. stages=2/warps=8 stays lawful and worth pricing AS A STACK MEMBER, and its duration successor is still worth running for that purpose -- what is now refused is dispatching it as a lone arm, which the operator's clause already forbids for any pre-stated ceiling below 1.5x. (b) IT IS A DEVICE-TIME BOUND. The governed step is larger than the device union, so the step-level ratio is SMALLER -- the direction that strengthens the refusal -- but no profiled/governed composition is made and no step figure is quoted. (c) ONE TRACE, ONE GEOMETRY, ONE HEAD (20338ddc). A different geometry or head can carry a different share and the bound is recomputed there, never carried across. (d) IT DOES NOT SAY THE CLASS CAN BE ELIMINATED. Elimination is the arithmetic ceiling, not a proposal, and no kernel replacement is named. (e) IT DOES NOT PRICE THE OCCUPANCY CANDIDATE. Occupancy is not time; the duration measurement is what prices it, and this only says what that price can at most be worth. (f) Gate A is unmoved and remains UNMET at p10 24,190.653 positions/s; composite 10 percent.

events.observation: The grouped-class bound just closed at 1.1606x against the 1.50x bar. The arithmetic behind it is class-agnostic: elimination of a class clears a bar B only if that class's share of device time is at least 1 - 1/B, which at B=1.50 is 0.3333. The campaign has a full per-class device-time table on the same trace -- the idle-class-adjacency receipt carries thirteen classes with  already decomposed into gemm_grouped_expert, optimizer, sort, memcpy and loss -- so the threshold is readable for EVERY class in one pass, and no class has ever been checked against it.

events.hypothesis: Mechanism: a treatment CONFINED to one class cannot move the step by more than that class's entire share, so share alone decides admissibility as a standalone arm before any mechanism is named. Traps, named before any number is read. (1) THE FINER TABLE IS THE RIGHT ONE and it must be used consistently -- the nine-class table hides gemm_grouped_expert and optimizer inside , and a bound computed on  as one class would credit a treatment nobody could author, because no single treatment spans two hand-written Triton kernels and a fused AdamW. (2) THE DENOMINATOR MUST BE THE SAME TABLE'S OWN TOTAL, cross-checked against the whole-trace union that receipt states, or the shares are ratios of numbers from two accountings. (3) A CLASS THAT CLEARS THE THRESHOLD IS NOT A ROUTE. Clearing says only that the arithmetic does not refuse it; whether any treatment reaches anywhere near elimination is a separate and much harder question, and for the dense GEMM class the campaign already has an achieved rate near the published reference. (4) THE FAVOURABLE ANSWER HERE IS , because that would mean the campaign has many live single-class routes; both of my errors on an unwanted result have run favourable, so the threshold is frozen before the table is summed and no class is excluded by judgment. (5) IT IS DEVICE TIME, not the governed step, and the device union is smaller, so every ceiling computed here is GENEROUS.

events.because: Quoting the frozen criterion: SUPPORTED if EXACTLY ONE class in the thirteen-class table has a total-elimination ceiling at or above 1.50 and that class is gemm_bf16. It does. On cia-captured-trace-20260914T183257Z.json the thirteen classes sum to 130,996.2 us per step against a stated whole-trace device union of 130,996.2, so the denominator clause holds. A class needs share 0.3333 for elimination alone to reach the bar. gemm_bf16 alone is above it at 0.4012 and 1.6699x. Every other class is refused as a standalone arm by arithmetic: elementwise 0.2095 at 1.2651x, gemm_grouped_expert 0.1379 at 1.1600x, optimizer 0.1284 at 1.1473x, triton_fused 1.0448x, softmax 1.0309x, and seven more below 1.016x. Twelve of thirteen refused. The instrument's first deliberate red was TAUTOLOGICAL -- it tightened the union tolerance to a nanosecond and did not fire, because the table reproduces the union exactly -- so it was replaced, before this verdict was ruled, with a red that tightens the clause carrying the verdict: the clearing set must be EMPTY. That refuses at exit 1 into a separate file, and the union clause stays in source labelled as a tripwire that is explicitly not the red.

events.hypothesis: THE STRUCTURAL CONSEQUENCE, AND THE SUCCESSOR IT NAMES. Twelve of thirteen classes are refused as standalone arms by arithmetic, and the one that clears is gemm_bf16 -- which this campaign has already measured running near the published dense bf16 reference, so its arithmetic admissibility and its practical reachability point in opposite directions. Read together: EVERY single-class route on this trace is either refused by share or exhausted by rate. That is not an impossibility claim about the terminal and is not stated as one; it is a statement about which routes the class partition contains. What it means for selection is that the remaining routes are of three kinds, none of them a single class: a STACK of classes (the route-set re-pricing, whose best combination stands at 1.6940x on timeline with two of its three pairs still unruled on mechanism); a PRECISION change, which raises a class's rate ceiling rather than shrinking its share and so is invisible to this table; and work that is NOT IN THIS TABLE AT ALL. THE NAMED SUCCESSOR IS THE THIRD. The device union is 130,996.2 us per step while the governed step at the current p10 is about 169,320 us, so roughly a quarter of the step is not device time and no class in this table can touch it. The identical elimination arithmetic applied to that residual is the obvious next bound -- and the honest obstacle is that the two numbers come from a profiled trace and a governed receipt respectively, which the evidence contract forbids composing. So the successor is: find or produce a source that measures device union and step wall IN ONE UNPROFILED RUN, and if none exists, that absence is itself the finding and it is what blocks bounding the largest unexamined part of the step. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLOSE. (a) CLEARING IS NOT A ROUTE and refusal is not impossibility -- a refused class stays lawful and valuable as a stack member, which is exactly what stages=2/warps=8 now is. (b) THE BOUND IS ELIMINATION, not achievable saving; no treatment is claimed to reach any ceiling here. (c) THE PARTITION IS AN INSTRUMENT CHOICE and a coarser bucket can make a class appear to clear that no single treatment could act on -- the thirteen-class table is used precisely because the nine-class one hides the grouped kernels and the optimizer inside one bucket worth 0.2754. (d) ONE TRACE, ONE GEOMETRY, ONE HEAD; recompute elsewhere rather than carrying it across. (e) A RECORD DEFECT IN THIS CYCLE, corrected here rather than edited in place: the observe and explain texts were passed as inline double-quoted shell arguments containing backtick-quoted words, so bash ran command substitution and silently deleted the word other from one sentence in the observation and two in the explanation. The criterion contained no backticks and is intact; the reasoning is unchanged and is restated in the instrument's own header comment, which is the authoritative copy. (f) Gate A is unmoved and remains UNMET at p10 24,190.653 positions/s; composite 10 percent.

events.observation: The population-overlap instrument run an hour ago on the matched captured trace returns a compute-bound versus bandwidth-bound overlap of 26.3 us per step, a fraction of 0.0004, on a timeline that carries 10,336.9 us of kernel-on-kernel overlap across three streams. That result is conditional on a partition the instrument hard-codes: its compute-bound set is exactly attention, gemm_bf16 and gemm_other. gemm_grouped_expert is therefore counted as bandwidth-bound, and it is the third largest class on that trace at 29,295.0 us per step, 18.6 percent of the device union. The campaign separately measured that class running at 0.932 of the published dense bf16 rate, which is the definition of compute-bound by measurement. So the largest single input to the bandwidth-bound union is a class that arguably belongs on the other side, and no receipt states what the overlap does when it moves. Separately, the same run found three streams -- 45,107 kernel events on stream 7, 2,520 on stream 17, 18 on stream 13 -- and nothing on this campaign says which classes ride the two minority streams.

events.hypothesis: THE MECHANISM, AND WHY THE ANSWER IS NOT OBVIOUS EITHER WAY. Moving a class from one population to the other does two things at once and they pull in opposite directions. It shrinks the bandwidth union and grows the compute union, which moves the DENOMINATOR -- the overlap fraction is taken against the smaller of the two unions, and which union is smaller can itself flip. And it moves that class interval set across the boundary, so every microsecond where a grouped-expert kernel overlapped a dense GEMM stops counting as cross-population overlap while every microsecond where it overlapped an elementwise kernel starts counting. The sign of the net change is not derivable from the aggregate and has to be measured. THE TRAP THIS CYCLE IS POINTED AT. Reporting one partition and calling the result the population overlap presents a hard-coded constant as a property of the trace. The honest output is the SENSITIVITY: both assignments, side by side, in one parse, so a reader sees how much of the answer is the data and how much is the constant. If the two agree the finding is robust to the choice; if they disagree the finding was never about the device. That is the same discipline as reporting a residual rather than only the buckets a vocabulary happened to express. THE STREAM CENSUS RIDES ALONG AT NO EXTRA COST because it is the same parse, and it answers the first half of the which-pairs-overlap successor: a per-class breakdown of the three streams says whether the minority streams carry a single class or a mixture, and a class confined to its own stream is a different structural fact from one interleaved with the main stream. NO CEILING IS COMPOSED. Nothing here says what a rescheduling would collect, and the REFUTED verdict on factor-table row 3 as a large lever is untouched whichever way the sensitivity lands.

Under the published assignment the cross-population overlap is 26.3 us per step, fraction 0.0004, with the compute union the smaller at 66,146.1 against bandwidth 89,396.0. Moving gemm_grouped_expert to the compute side -- where the campaign own rate measurement of 0.932 of published dense bf16 puts it -- gives compute 95,438.0 and bandwidth 68,671.7, FLIPS which union is smaller, and raises the cross-population overlap to 8,594.0 us per step, fraction 0.1251. A divergence of 0.1247 against a frozen limit of 0.05, and a 327-fold change in the overlap itself, from one constant. So the 0.0004 I ruled on an hour ago is an artifact of the partition: with the grouped expert path counted as bandwidth-bound, its overlap with the dense GEMM class was hidden inside a population instead of crossing between them. THE SUBSTANTIVE CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT RUNS AGAINST WHAT I REPORTED EARLIER: under the classification the measurements support, bandwidth-bound work and compute-bound work on the captured path DO overlap, by about 8.6 ms per step, and factor-table row 3 premise does not survive as stated. It is still under the 0.15 line the predecessor used, so neither assignment trips that clause, and no ceiling is composed here in either direction. A SECOND CLAUSE ALSO FIRED AND IT IS A DEFECT OF MINE, NOT A PROPERTY OF THE TRACE: the every-kernel-receives-a-class clause reports 2,484 unclassified kernels, which is exactly the other class at 414.0 kernels per step over six steps. classify returns the string other as its RESIDUAL LABEL and CLASSES does not list it, so my membership test treated a named bucket as no class at all. That clause is repaired in a named successor and not edited here. The verdict does not rest on it: the divergence clause is independent and fires on its own. THE DELIBERATE RED IS UNINFORMATIVE THIS RUN and is recorded as such rather than claimed as proof -- it tightens the divergence limit to zero, and the instrument had already refused on that clause at the frozen limit. The clause firing LIVE against real data is stronger evidence that it can fire than any synthetic tightening would be.
hypotheses.not_closed: WHAT THIS DOES TO THE ROW I CLOSED AN HOUR AGO, FIRST, BECAUSE IT IS MINE AND IT RUNS AGAINST ME. the-zero-concurrency-finding-does-not-transfer-to-the-captured-path reports that the population overlap on the captured arm holds at 0.0004 and that factor-table row 3 premise SURVIVES the transfer test, and it carries the classification caveat as a not_closed line in its own text. That caveat is now measured and it is decisive: the 0.0004 is a property of counting the grouped expert path as bandwidth-bound, and under the classification the rate measurement supports the same trace gives 8,594.0 us per step of genuine cross-population overlap. The prior verdict STANDS AS ISSUED on its two structural clauses, which are untouched -- three streams, 10,336.9 us of kernel-on-kernel overlap -- and its population sentence is superseded by this row rather than edited in place. The earlier ruling should be read with this one beside it. THE STREAM CENSUS, WHICH IS THE OTHER HALF AND IS CLEAN. Stream 7 carries 154,225.9 us per step across thirteen classes, dominant share 0.4267. Streams 17 and 13 carry ONE class each and it is the same class both times: elementwise, 11,612.0 us over 420.0 kernels per step on stream 17 and 425.6 us over 3.0 kernels on stream 13. So every microsecond of multi-stream concurrency the captured path has is elementwise work running beside stream 7, and nothing else was ever moved off the main stream. That is a sharper structural fact than the aggregate: the concurrency is not a general property of replay, it is one class on two side streams. TWO DEFECTS OF MINE, NAMED AND NOT REPAIRED IN PLACE. First, the every-kernel-receives-a-class clause is wrong: classify returns the string other as its RESIDUAL LABEL and the CLASSES table does not list it, so the membership test counted 2,484 kernels -- exactly the other bucket at 414.0 per step over six steps -- as unclassified. The clause was meant to catch a census that cannot see its own population and instead caught a named bucket. Second, the deliberate red for this instrument is uninformative: it tightens the divergence limit to zero on a clause that had already fired at the frozen limit, so it demonstrates nothing the live run did not. A clause that fires on real data is stronger evidence than a synthetic tightening, and that is recorded rather than dressed up as a red. NOT CLOSED, IN COST ORDER. First, the repaired clause in a named successor: treat other as a class and refuse only on a label the table cannot produce. Second, this tests ONE assignment and not the partition -- attention, gemm_other, triton_fused and the optimizer each carry their own argument about which side they belong on, and a partition robust to one move is not robust to all of them. Third, the 8,594.0 us is measured as an overlap and not as a pairing, and whether the elementwise work on streams 17 and 13 is the whole of it is unmeasured. Fourth, serialization is still not evidence that work COULD run concurrently: the dependency graph remains unextracted. No ceiling is composed in either direction and the REFUTED verdict on factor-table row 3 as a large lever is untouched. Gate A is unmoved and remains UNMET at p10 24,190.653 applied positions per second; composite 10 percent.
hypotheses.closing: REFUTED against the frozen criterion on its divergence clause, which fired live on real data. The receipt is landed, the consequence for the row I closed an hour ago is stated rather than absorbed, and both instrument defects are named for a successor rather than edited in place.

events.observation: The assignment-sensitivity run measured 8,594.0 us per step of cross-population overlap on the matched captured trace once the grouped expert class is counted as compute-bound, where its own achieved rate of 0.932 of published dense bf16 puts it. That figure is an EXCESS -- the sum of two population unions minus their joint union -- and it names no pair. The same parse also found that the only work off the main stream is elementwise: stream 17 carries 11,612.0 us over 420.0 kernels per step and stream 13 carries 425.6 us over 3.0 kernels, both one hundred percent elementwise, while stream 7 carries 154,225.9 us across thirteen classes. So there is a candidate account sitting in the data -- the overlap is elementwise on the side streams running beside whatever occupies stream 7 -- and nothing has tested it. The two numbers are also not obviously compatible: 12,037.6 us of elementwise lives off the main stream and the cross-population overlap is 8,594.0, which is less, so either not all of that side-stream work overlaps compute-bound kernels or some of the overlap comes from somewhere else entirely.

events.hypothesis: THE MECHANISM. Concurrency on a device requires two kernels resident at once, which on this path requires two streams, because stream 7 is a single ordered queue and work on it cannot overlap itself. Therefore ALL device concurrency on this trace must involve at least one kernel from stream 17 or stream 13, and both of those are elementwise. That is a structural argument, not a measurement, and it predicts that the cross-population overlap decomposes into elementwise-against-something pairs and nothing else. THE THING THAT COULD FALSIFY IT AND IS THE REASON TO MEASURE RATHER THAN ASSERT. A profiler can record two kernels on one stream with overlapping timestamps when its timestamps are imprecise or when the events come from different devices or contexts, and this campaign has already found a class of overlap it did not expect. If pairs appear that are both on stream 7, either the single-queue premise is wrong here or the timestamps are, and either answer changes how every union on this campaign should be read. THE SECOND THING BEING MEASURED. The 8,594.0 us must reconcile against a pairwise decomposition: pairwise overlaps can exceed the union-derived excess when three or more kernels overlap at one instant, so the pairwise total is expected to be at or above it, never below. A pairwise total BELOW the excess would mean the pair enumeration is missing pairs and the instrument is not covering its own population. THE RESIDUAL CLAUSE IS REPAIRED IN THIS SUCCESSOR rather than in the predecessor, whose REFUTED verdict stands: classify returns the string other as a RESIDUAL LABEL that the CLASSES table does not list, so the correct membership test admits it as a named bucket and refuses only on a label the classifier cannot produce.

Also REFUTED if the pairwise overlap total is BELOW the union-derived cross-population excess of 8,594.0 us, because a pair enumeration that totals less than the excess it decomposes is missing pairs. Also REFUTED if any kernel receives a label the class table cannot produce.
events.supported_if: SUPPORTED if every overlapping kernel pair on the trace has at least one member on a stream other than stream 7, AND the elementwise class is a member of at least 0.95 of the overlapping time by pair, AND the pairwise overlap total is at or above the 8,594.0 us union-derived cross-population excess.

events.observation: The pair decomposition found 82.3 us per step of device overlap whose two members are both on stream 7, which is a single ordered queue and therefore cannot overlap itself. It is 0.8 percent of the total overlap and the pairs sampled from it run 0.031, 0.033, 0.064, 0.64, 0.736 and 1.695 microseconds, with the same-stream class pairs dominated by counts rather than durations -- gemm_bf16 against itself is 3.8 us spread over 32.5 pairs, a mean of 0.12 us. Nothing on this campaign has measured whether that is real concurrency or an artifact of the profiler timestamps, and the question is not confined to one row: every device-time figure this campaign has published is an interval UNION, and a union computed over intervals that spuriously overlap at their boundaries is SMALLER than the truth. That is the direction that has flattered every share, every coverage number and every elimination ceiling I have reported.

events.hypothesis: THE MECHANISM. CUPTI timestamps a kernel start and end from device counters and the profiler writes them at finite precision. Two kernels issued back to back on one queue have a true gap of at least zero; if the recorded end of the first is rounded up or the recorded start of the second is rounded down, the recorded intervals cross by a fraction of the quantum. That produces overlap that is many small crossings rather than a few large ones, concentrated at magnitudes near the recording precision, and it appears between whichever classes happen to be adjacent rather than between a particular pair. THE ALTERNATIVE IT IS BEING TESTED AGAINST is that stream 7 is not in fact a single ordered queue for these events -- a second context, a second device, or events the trace labels with a stream they did not run on. That account predicts overlaps of ordinary kernel magnitude, not fractions of a microsecond, and it would mean the stream field cannot be trusted anywhere on this campaign. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE DISTRIBUTION, not the total. Consecutive kernels on one stream sorted by start time have a gap that is positive when they are ordered and negative when the records cross. Measuring the magnitude distribution of the negative gaps against the recording precision separates the two accounts, and the positive gaps on the same stream are the control: if crossings are a rounding artifact their magnitudes sit in the same range as the smallest positive gaps. WHY THIS IS WORTH A CYCLE RATHER THAN A FOOTNOTE. The answer is an error bar on every union on this campaign, and it points one way. The instrument therefore also reports what the stream-7 union would be with every crossing removed, so the size of the flattery is a number rather than an adjective.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED if any same-stream crossing on stream 7 exceeds 5.0 us in magnitude, because a crossing of ordinary kernel scale is not a rounding artifact and would mean the stream field cannot be trusted. Also REFUTED if the median crossing magnitude exceeds 0.5 us, because a distribution centred well above the recording precision is not rounding. Also REFUTED if the total same-stream crossing time exceeds 0.02 of the stream union, because at that size it changes published figures materially whatever its cause. Also REFUTED if the instrument cannot establish the recorded timestamp precision from the trace, since then the artifact account has no scale to be compared against.
events.supported_if: SUPPORTED if every same-stream crossing on stream 7 is smaller than 5.0 us in magnitude, AND their median magnitude is at or below 0.5 us, AND their total is at or below 0.02 of the stream union -- the signature of a rounding artifact rather than of concurrency -- AND the correction to the stream union is reported as a number.
events.instrument: seat record: same_stream_crossing_census.py

events.because:
REFUTED against the frozen criterion's FIRST clause, quoted: "REFUTED if any same-stream crossing on stream 7 exceeds 5.0 us in magnitude, because a crossing of ordinary kernel scale is not a rounding artifact and would mean the stream field cannot be trusted." The largest same-stream crossing is 6.0801 us. The other three clauses HELD: median 0.0967 us against a 0.5 us limit; total 82.28 us/step = 0.00053 of the stream union against a 0.02 limit; the recorded precision was established from the trace (3 decimal places, quantum 0.001 us). Receipt seat record: same-stream-crossing-census-20260921.json, 45,107 kernels on stream 7 across six census windows, 1,983 crossings (330.5/step).

THE MATERIAL CONCERN THAT MOTIVATED THIS CYCLE IS DISSOLVED, AND NOT BY THE VERDICT. The predecessor row warned that phantom sub-microsecond overlap at kernel boundaries would make every interval UNION on this campaign slightly SMALL, in the direction that has flattered every published share, coverage figure and elimination ceiling. The instrument recomputed the stream-7 union with every crossing clipped away: 154,143.6 us/step as recorded, 154,143.6 us/step repaired, understatement 0.00 us, share 0.00000. That is not a small number, it is an ARITHMETIC IDENTITY I had not seen: two intervals that cross are merged into one interval by a union, and clipping the later one's start to the earlier one's end leaves the merged interval identical. A same-stream crossing CANNOT understate a union. So the campaign-wide flattery worry is retired at its source, whatever the crossings turn out to be, and it was retired by an instrument built to answer a different question.

WHAT THE DISTRIBUTION ACTUALLY SAYS, INCLUDING THE PART THAT REFUSES THE ROUNDING STORY AS STATED. The POSITIVE-gap control is the discriminator I froze for this, and it is decisive about the real clock: positive gaps have p01 and p10 both at 0.0312 us, which is 1/32 us, so the device timestamps tick at about 31.25 ns and NOT at the 0.001 us the trace's decimal places advertise. Against that true granularity the median crossing of 0.0967 us is about three ticks and the p90 of 0.6084 us is about twenty -- small, but not the one-tick signature a pure rounding account predicts, and my criterion's own scale reference (the recorded decimal places) was the wrong one to compare against. The 6.0801 us maximum is roughly 195 ticks and is of ordinary kernel scale, which is exactly what the clause was written to catch.

SO THE CYCLE'S OWN HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED AS STATED AND THE THIRD ACCOUNT IS NOW THE LIVE ONE. "Rounding at the recording precision" is refused by the maximum and undercut by the tick census. "The stream field is wrong" is not established either: it would predict crossings distributed like kernels, and 1,983 crossings totalling 82.28 us/step against a 154,143.6 us/step stream union is 0.05 percent of the queue, with a median of three ticks. A third account fits both halves better and neither of my two did: CUPTI's begin and end timestamps for adjacent kernels on one queue can be recorded with small independent errors, mostly a few ticks and occasionally much larger when a sample is delayed. That is a hypothesis about the instrument and it is recorded as one, not claimed.

MOVES NO GATE. Gate A remains UNMET at p10 24,190.653 applied positions/s against the 80,000 terminal; the composite stays 10 percent. No ceiling is composed and no published number is re-issued.

THE DELIBERATE RED IS UNINFORMATIVE THIS RUN, FOR THE SECOND CONSECUTIVE CYCLE AND FOR THE SAME REASON, AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH rather than claimed as proof. It tightens the maximum-crossing limit from 5.0 us to 0.0 us -- a clause that had already fired on real data at the frozen limit. A clause firing live is stronger evidence that it can fire than any synthetic tightening, but that is a defence of the run and not of the red. That is the direction that has flattered every share, every coverage number and every elimination ceiling I have reported.
hypotheses.explanation: THE MECHANISM. CUPTI timestamps a kernel start and end from device counters and the profiler writes them at finite precision. Two kernels issued back to back on one queue have a true gap of at least zero; if the recorded end of the first is rounded up or the recorded start of the second is rounded down, the recorded intervals cross by a fraction of the quantum. That produces overlap that is many small crossings rather than a few large ones, concentrated at magnitudes near the recording precision, and it appears between whichever classes happen to be adjacent rather than between a particular pair. THE ALTERNATIVE IT IS BEING TESTED AGAINST is that stream 7 is not in fact a single ordered queue for these events -- a second context, a second device, or events the trace labels with a stream they did not run on. That account predicts overlaps of ordinary kernel magnitude, not fractions of a microsecond, and it would mean the stream field cannot be trusted anywhere on this campaign. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS THE DISTRIBUTION, not the total. Consecutive kernels on one stream sorted by start time have a gap that is positive when they are ordered and negative when the records cross. Measuring the magnitude distribution of the negative gaps against the recording precision separates the two accounts, and the positive gaps on the same stream are the control: if crossings are a rounding artifact their magnitudes sit in the same range as the smallest positive gaps. WHY THIS IS WORTH A CYCLE RATHER THAN A FOOTNOTE. The answer is an error bar on every union on this campaign, and it points one way. The instrument therefore also reports what the stream-7 union would be with every crossing removed, so the size of the flattery is a number rather than an adjective.

Also REFUTED if the total same-stream crossing time exceeds 0.02 of the stream union, because at that size it changes published figures materially whatever its cause. events.observation:
The only arm on this campaign above the operator's 1.5x bar is ADMITTED_ON_TIMELINE and not ADMITTED, and the single thing holding it out is a SOURCE READING nobody has done. the-two-measured-pairwise-rulings-restore-an-above-bar-arm-at-1694x-on-the-timeline-20260921 admits elementwise_class_as_device_time + fused_optimizer_entirely + two_register_limited_kernels_halved at 1.6940x, 0.096673 s/step, 42,369.7 positions/s at perfect effectiveness, and carries as its FIRST not_closed: "MECHANISM CONTENTION IS UNRULED FOR ALL THREE PAIRS and is now the single gating unknown on this arm ... a source reading, not a measurement and not a card run."

A first look at the source says the three levers are NOT as separable as their names suggest. The register lever is two launch-argument sites in one 96-line file: src/ember/model/ember_v0_grouped_capture.py lines 72-74 and 90-92, where _rows and _weights are launched with BM=64, BN=128, BK=32, num_warps=4. The optimizer lever is a constructor keyword and an identity declaration in cia_step_runner.py (optimizer_factory at 1199-1202, capture.capture(optimizer=optimizer) at 1258). The elementwise lever as actually authored is the residency reshape, whose frozen diff (<host-local path>, 6,504 bytes) touches exactly one file, src/ember/model/ember_v0_residency.py -- and that file, at line 420, imports grouped_mm from ember_v0_grouped_capture, the very module the register lever edits, while at 876 and 880 it switches the routing call from _local_scores to _local_scores_rows.

So two of the three pairs have a structural relationship that file-level disjointness hides: the elementwise lever is the CALLER of the kernels the register lever tunes, and the register lever's own justification row is named "stages2-warps8-at-the-frozen-tile" -- an occupancy result derived at one tile and one set of operand shapes.

events.hypothesis:
WHAT MECHANISM CONTENTION IS, STATED SO IT CAN FAIL. Two levers contend in mechanism when implementing one changes the source the other acts on, or removes a structure the other's correctness argument depends on. That is a STRICTLY WIDER test than "do their edits touch the same file", and the wider part is where the answer lives here. File disjointness is necessary and worthless on its own: the residency reshape and the kernel launch parameters live in different files and are in a direct caller/callee relationship through grouped_mm.

THE THREE CANDIDATE MECHANISMS, one per pair.

(1) elementwise x register. The reshape rewrites resident_local_routes and adds a DeviceRouteIndex built OUTSIDE the capture, so the routing path stops constructing host tensors per chunk. If that reshape also changes the OPERAND SHAPES handed to grouped_mm -- the row count m, the group count, the offsets tuple -- then the occupancy result that licenses num_stages=2, num_warps=8 was derived at shapes the composed arm does not run. The register row's own title says "at the frozen tile", and a tile result is a statement about a launch geometry and its operands together. This is the pair most likely to contend, and it contends through ARGUMENTS rather than through edits.

(2) elementwise x optimizer. The fused optimizer applies its update through register_post_accumulate_grad_hook per parameter, so its correctness depends on every trained parameter receiving a grad inside the captured backward. The runner's own source already carries a comment that the grouped resident backward materialises zeros for a parameter whose step has no gradient, and that an every-parameter-applied check "was tried first and refused on step 1". A reshape of the residency path changes which parameters are touched per chunk. If it changes whether any parameter's grad is produced inside the capture, the fused hook's precondition moves.

(3) register x optimizer. The kernels are launched inside the captured forward and backward; the optimizer runs at the end of the captured step. They share the capture and nothing else -- no symbol, no tensor, no shape. The plausible contention is RESOURCE rather than source: a launch at num_warps=8 raises per-SM register and shared-memory pressure, and a fused optimizer inside the same graph competes for nothing at the same instant because the timeline already measured them INDEPENDENT at +0.0 us/step. This pair is expected to rule NO, and saying so before the run is what makes a surprise here informative.

WHY A MECHANICAL INSTRUMENT AND NOT A READING. A reading of three pairs by one seat is an assertion, and my own record says the generative half is where I fail. The mechanical half is decidable: resolve each lever's edit sites from a NAMED artifact rather than from memory, parse the modules with ast, and compute for each lever the set of module-level symbols it DEFINES or MODIFIES and the set it READS, following imports one hop. A pair contends mechanically when one lever's modified-symbol set intersects the other's read-or-modified set. That catches (2) and (3) outright and catches the EDIT half of (1). The ARGUMENT half of (1) -- whether the reshape changes grouped_mm's operand shapes -- is decided by reading the call site's arguments before and after the diff, which is also mechanical: the instrument extracts the grouped_mm call's argument expressions from both sides of the frozen diff and reports whether they differ.

WHAT WOULD MAKE THIS UNDECIDABLE, AND IT REFUSES RATHER THAN GUESSING. If a lever has no named artifact fixing its edit sites, there is nothing to rule and the instrument says so instead of inventing a site set. The optimizer lever is the exposed one: "fused_optimizer_entirely" names a keyword, and whether the ENTIRE optimizer moves inside the capture is a larger change than fused=True. The instrument requires each lever's sites to come from a diff, a receipt, or an explicit line range in a file it reads, and refuses on any lever it cannot bind.

events.refuted_if:
The hypothesis is that the three pairs DO NOT contend in mechanism and the 1.6940x arm may move from ADMITTED_ON_TIMELINE to ADMITTED.

REFUTED if any pair's levers have intersecting EDIT SITES at the symbol level -- one lever modifying a module-level symbol the other modifies -- because two treatments rewriting the same function are one treatment and must be authored and priced as one.

Also REFUTED if any lever MODIFIES a symbol another lever READS, because the reader's correctness argument was made against the symbol as it stood.

Also REFUTED if the residency reshape changes the ARGUMENT EXPRESSIONS at the grouped_mm call site, because the occupancy result licensing num_stages=2 and num_warps=8 was derived at one tile and one set of operand shapes, and an argument change moves the shapes the tile result is about.

Also REFUTED if the reshape changes WHICH PARAMETERS receive a gradient inside the captured backward, because the fused optimizer applies through a per-parameter post-accumulate-grad hook whose precondition is exactly that.

Also REFUTED if any lever's edit sites cannot be bound to a NAMED ARTIFACT -- a diff, a receipt, or an explicit line range in a file the instrument reads -- because a pair cannot be ruled against a lever whose extent is a memory.

Also REFUTED if the instrument's own symbol resolution leaves more than 0.05 of the touched symbols unresolved, because a contention test that cannot see part of its population reports absence where it has no coverage.

SUPPORTED if, for all three pairs: edit-site symbol sets are disjoint, no lever modifies a symbol another reads, the grouped_mm call site's argument expressions are unchanged across the reshape diff, the set of parameters receiving a gradient inside the capture is unchanged, every lever is bound to a named artifact, and unresolved symbols are at or below 0.05 -- and the ruling for each of the three pairs is emitted separately with the evidence that decided it.

hypotheses.explanation:
WHAT MECHANISM CONTENTION IS, STATED SO IT CAN FAIL. Two levers contend in mechanism when implementing one changes the source the other acts on, or removes a structure the other's correctness argument depends on. That is a STRICTLY WIDER test than "do their edits touch the same file", and the wider part is where the answer lives here. File disjointness is necessary and worthless on its own: the residency reshape and the kernel launch parameters live in different files and are in a direct caller/callee relationship through grouped_mm.

THE THREE CANDIDATE MECHANISMS, one per pair.

(1) elementwise x register. The reshape rewrites resident_local_routes and adds a DeviceRouteIndex built OUTSIDE the capture, so the routing path stops constructing host tensors per chunk. If that reshape also changes the OPERAND SHAPES handed to grouped_mm -- the row count m, the group count, the offsets tuple -- then the occupancy result that licenses num_stages=2, num_warps=8 was derived at shapes the composed arm does not run. The register row's own title says "at the frozen tile", and a tile result is a statement about a launch geometry and its operands together. This is the pair most likely to contend, and it contends through ARGUMENTS rather than through edits.

(2) elementwise x optimizer. The fused optimizer applies its update through register_post_accumulate_grad_hook per parameter, so its correctness depends on every trained parameter receiving a grad inside the captured backward. The runner's own source already carries a comment that the grouped resident backward materialises zeros for a parameter whose step has no gradient, and that an every-parameter-applied check "was tried first and refused on step 1". A reshape of the residency path changes which parameters are touched per chunk. If it changes whether any parameter's grad is produced inside the capture, the fused hook's precondition moves.

(3) register x optimizer. The kernels are launched inside the captured forward and backward; the optimizer runs at the end of the captured step. They share the capture and nothing else -- no symbol, no tensor, no shape. The plausible contention is RESOURCE rather than source: a launch at num_warps=8 raises per-SM register and shared-memory pressure, and a fused optimizer inside the same graph competes for nothing at the same instant because the timeline already measured them INDEPENDENT at +0.0 us/step. A pair contends mechanically when one lever's modified-symbol set intersects the other's read-or-modified set. That catches (2) and (3) outright and catches the EDIT half of (1). The ARGUMENT half of (1) -- whether the reshape changes grouped_mm's operand shapes -- is decided by reading the call site's arguments before and after the diff, which is also mechanical: the instrument extracts the grouped_mm call's argument expressions from both sides of the frozen diff and reports whether they differ.

The optimizer lever is the exposed one: "fused_optimizer_entirely" names a keyword, and whether the ENTIRE optimizer moves inside the capture is a larger change than fused=True. The instrument requires each lever's sites to come from a diff, a receipt, or an explicit line range in a file it reads, and refuses on any lever it cannot bind.

events.hypothesis:
THE RESOLUTION RULE, STATED SO IT CANNOT COLLIDE. A read set contains only names that RESOLVE to a module-level symbol the reading module can actually reach: defined at module level in the same file, or explicitly imported by name from another module. Every other free name -- a parameter, a local binding, a comprehension target, a dataclass field, an attribute -- is dropped, because none of them can denote another module's symbol. Attribute accesses are admitted only when the receiver itself resolves to an imported module. This is the same law as a kill selector: a name is not identity, and identity here is the import edge.

THE COVERAGE RULE. Module-level statements that belong to no def or class -- imports, module constants, decorator and docstring space -- get the NAMED bucket `<module>` and enter the lever's modified set. That makes the reshape's import rewrite a first-class edit site testable against the other levers, and it removes the orphan population that tripped the ceiling. A residual with a name is a measurement; a residual with no bucket is a silence.

WHAT THE REPAIR THEN HAS TO DECIDE, AND IT IS A JUDGEMENT THAT MUST BE MADE AGAINST A RULE RATHER THAN BY TASTE. If the only surviving cross-module edge is that residency calls grouped_mm and the register lever edits the launch inside `rows`, then a naive modified-x-read test asks whether `rows` is reachable from grouped_mm and answers yes, and every caller of anything ever edited contends with it. That is a test that cannot return NO and is therefore not a test. The discriminating question is narrower: does the edit change the callee's INTERFACE -- its name, its parameters, its return shape, its dtype, its error contract -- or only its internal launch configuration? An interface change propagates to the caller's correctness argument; a launch-configuration change is a replacement whose own cost is separately owed and whose caller sees nothing. My own treatment-selection law already says an incumbent's measured cost bounds the savings and bounds a replacement's cost from neither direction, which is exactly the statement that a replacement is a different implementation behind an unchanged interface.

SO THE INSTRUMENT COMPARES THE CALLEE'S SIGNATURE AND RETURN STRUCTURE ACROSS THE LEVER, not merely whether its body was touched. For the register lever that is mechanical: the edit is confined to keyword arguments of a Triton launch subscript expression, and the enclosing def's signature, its return statements and the shapes it constructs are unchanged. A residual with a name is a measurement; a residual with no bucket is a silence.

WHAT THE REPAIR THEN HAS TO DECIDE, AND IT IS A JUDGEMENT THAT MUST BE MADE AGAINST A RULE RATHER THAN BY TASTE. If the only surviving cross-module edge is that residency calls grouped_mm and the register lever edits the launch inside `rows`, then a naive modified-x-read test asks whether `rows` is reachable from grouped_mm and answers yes, and every caller of anything ever edited contends with it. That is a test that cannot return NO and is therefore not a test. The discriminating question is narrower: does the edit change the callee's INTERFACE -- its name, its parameters, its return shape, its dtype, its error contract -- or only its internal launch configuration? An interface change propagates to the caller's correctness argument; a launch-configuration change is a replacement whose own cost is separately owed and whose caller sees nothing. My own treatment-selection law already says an incumbent's measured cost bounds the savings and bounds a replacement's cost from neither direction, which is exactly the statement that a replacement is a different implementation behind an unchanged interface.

SO THE INSTRUMENT COMPARES THE CALLEE'S SIGNATURE AND RETURN STRUCTURE ACROSS THE LEVER, not merely whether its body was touched. For the register lever that is mechanical: the edit is confined to keyword arguments of a Triton launch subscript expression, and the enclosing def's signature, its return statements and the shapes it constructs are unchanged. If any of those moved, the pair contends.

THE THIRD PAIR STAYS TRIVIAL AND SAYING SO BEFORE THE RUN IS WHAT MAKES A SURPRISE INFORMATIVE. fused_optimizer_entirely and two_register_limited_kernels_halved share no module, no import edge and no symbol; the timeline already measured them INDEPENDENT at +0.0 us/step. A CONTENDS ruling on that pair would mean the instrument is wrong again, not that the pair contends.
hypotheses.criterion:

REFUTED if any pair's levers modify the same module-level symbol, including the `<module>` bucket of the same file, because two treatments rewriting one symbol are one treatment.

Also REFUTED if any lever modifies a symbol another lever IMPORTS BY NAME, because an imported symbol is the caller's declared dependency.

Also REFUTED if any lever changes the SIGNATURE, the return structure, or the raised-error contract of a symbol another lever reaches through an import edge, because that is an interface change and the caller's correctness argument was made against the interface.

Also REFUTED if the reshape touches any line of the grouped_mm call site, or drops any parameter-bearing input, since those two clauses held in the predecessor and a disagreement means one of the two instruments is wrong.

Also REFUTED if the unresolved share of edit lines exceeds 0.01 once the `<module>` bucket exists, because with a bucket for module-level statements there is nothing left that a mapper should fail to place.

Also REFUTED if the instrument reports CONTENDS for fused_optimizer_entirely + two_register_limited_kernels_halved, which share no module, no import edge and no symbol and were measured INDEPENDENT at +0.0 us/step on the timeline -- a positive there is an instrument defect and is ruled as one.

Also REFUTED if the modified-x-read test cannot return NO for a caller of an edited callee by construction, tested by a planted probe: an edit confined to a callee's internal launch keywords must rule NO while a synthetic edit to that callee's signature must rule CONTENDS, and both must be demonstrated in the same run.

SUPPORTED if all three pairs rule NO under import resolution, the callee-interface comparison is unchanged for every import edge, the call-site and gradient clauses still hold, unresolved is at or below 0.01, and the planted probe shows the test can return both answers.

hypotheses.ruling: The frozen criterion's SUPPORTED clause reads: all three pairs rule NO under import resolution, the callee-interface comparison is unchanged for every import edge, the call-site and gradient clauses still hold, unresolved is at or below 0.01, and the planted probe shows the test can return both answers. Every term is met by the landed receipt. All three pairs rule NO. Import resolution found exactly ONE cross-module edge in the whole arm -- residency imports grouped_mm, which resolves through the module-level alias grouped_mm = DynamicGrouped.apply to DynamicGrouped, which the register lever edits at line 92 -- and the interface comparison ruled it NO because that edit is confined to launch keyword arguments, so the callee's signature and return structure are unchanged. The two false CONTENDS the predecessor produced are gone: the name rows now resolves to the module-level function only inside the grouped kernel module, and residency's dataclass field and the runner's measurement list no longer reach it. Unresolved is 0.0000 against the tightened 0.01 ceiling, because the <module> bucket absorbed the reshape's own import rewrite as a named edit site rather than an orphan. The planted probe returned BOTH answers in the same run: the real keyword-only edit at lines 74 and 92 is keyword-confined True, a synthetic edit to the same callee's signature line is keyword-confined False, so the test is demonstrated to discriminate rather than assumed to. The two clauses the predecessor established survive independent re-derivation: _grouped_swiglu has zero lines touched by the reshape, and no parameter-bearing input is dropped. The trivial pair rules NO as the timeline measured it. AND THE ARGUMENT THE PREDECESSOR ROW FLAGGED AS OWED, MADE HERE AGAINST RECEIPTS: whether a launch-parameter change to a callee counts as modifying the caller's contract. It does not. A caller's correctness argument binds an interface, not a launch configuration -- and treatment-selection law already says a replacement's own cost is a SEPARATELY OWED MEASUREMENT, never inferred from the incumbent. ALIASES ARE FOLLOWED ONE HOP, so a two-hop chain or a symbol re-exported through a package __init__ would be missed. ONE worktree, ONE frozen diff, ONE head, no matched-run variation. AND THE STANDING ONE, NOW UNDISCHARGED BY SIX CONSECUTIVE CYCLES: the dependency graph is still unextracted, so serialization observed anywhere on this path is still not evidence that the work COULD run concurrently.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. Kernel-count regime, factor-table row 1: cost proportional to kernel COUNT rather than to bytes, because the mean non-GEMM kernel is far below launch latency. The local router ran a Python loop over the chunks of every sparse layer, and each iteration issued its own gather, its own vector GEMM, its own argmax and its own gate. The reshape is a DECLARED numerical treatment by its own source comment -- fp32 accumulation order, never claimed neutral -- so gate C needs a separate 64-update licence pair against the pre-reshape parent 0a7aa352, and a faster number here does not license itself. The two must never be quoted for each other.

events.observation: The grouped kernels run at an occupancy ceiling of 0.3333 and a measured alternative reaches 0.5000, and nobody has ever timed it. At the frozen production tile 64x128x32 with num_stages=3 and num_warps=4, registers per thread are 128 on _rows and 126 on _weights and static shared memory is 24,576 bytes, and those two limiters TIE at 4 resident blocks per SM, which is 16 of the architectural 48 warps. At num_stages=2 with num_warps=8 the same compilation gives registers 78 and 80, static shared 16,384 bytes, zero spilled bytes on both, and 24 resident warps per SM. That is a 1.5x occupancy CEILING and it is the only configuration in a five-by-two sweep that relieves both tied limiters at once. No duration for either configuration exists at the governed geometry. The card went idle at 1:27 PM LA when the batched local router measurement closed, and this is the next number-producing leg.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM, AND ITS SIGN IS GENUINELY OPEN. More resident warps per SM means more independent work available to hide memory latency, so a kernel whose stalls are memory-bound should speed up. Against that, num_stages=2 gives each warp strictly LESS software pipelining than num_stages=3, so every individual warp has less latency hiding of its own. The two effects point opposite ways and no arithmetic on the compilation decides between them. That is precisely why this is a duration measurement and not a ceiling claim: occupancy is not time, and a treatment that raises resident warps by 1.5x can run slower. WHAT IS MEASURED. One governed 1,024-warmed-update measurement at the 2/8 head, resident-dynamic-capture, 4 documents of 1,024 positions per step, seed 2163, support experts 0 1 8 18, against the newest governed p10 on this source line. The edit is exactly two Triton launch keyword lines and nothing else, applied on bytes and committed before the run so the head is pinned. WHAT IT IS NOT. It is not a standalone arm. Total elimination of the whole grouped expert class bounds any class-confined treatment at 1.1606x, below the 1.5x bar, so this is priced as a STACK MEMBER. It is also a DECLARED NUMERICAL TREATMENT: num_warps changes how the output tile is split across warps, num_stages changes accumulation order, and _weights carries an explicit bf16 rounding boundary per chunk. It measures duration and licenses nothing.

THE INTERACTION IS THE RESULT AND IT REFUTES THE ARM'S PRICING, NOT JUST THIS LEVER. Four governed numbers now exist on one geometry: untreated parent 24,190.653; reshape alone 23,754.278 (0.982x); 2/8 alone 22,673.804 (0.9373x); 2/8 AND reshape together 23,936.839 (0.9895x). WHAT THIS DOES TO THE MECHANISM-CONTENTION RULING, PRECISELY. That ruling found the three levers do not contend IN SOURCE, sharing exactly one cross-module edge behind an unchanged interface, and it said in its own not_closed that a symbol-and-import test is structurally blind to two levers that both assume a scheduling property or both consume the same per-SM register budget, and that the register lever is exactly that case. This measurement is that blindness made visible: the launch configuration raises resident warps, the reshape changes what those warps are asked to do, and the two only make sense together. The source ruling is not overturned -- it ruled mechanism composability and remains correct about it -- but the ARM'S ARITHMETIC, which multiplies independently priced factors, is now refuted by measurement on its own two largest levers.

If the comparator's median is ABOVE the treated medians, the treatments are simply slower everywhere and the tail is not the story.

FOUR GOVERNED RUNS AT ONE GEOMETRY NOW SIT ON DISK, so this is a four-way per-update duration comparison against one comparator, analysis-only, no lease, no card. It decides which of the remaining arms deserves card time before the freeze, which is exactly what should govern dispatch with hours left rather than picking the next authorable lever.

WHAT IS NOT CLOSED BY THIS REFUTATION. It does not refute the launch-configuration mechanism: occupancy did rise as measured, from 16 resident warps to 24, and the arithmetic that predicted it was never about p10. NO MATCHED-RUN VARIATION EXISTS ON ANY OF THE FOUR. The governed-run evidence contract requires independent matched-run variation before an improvement or ceiling claim, and a 1.05 percent composition effect sits inside a band nobody has measured. The 6.3 percent deficit ruled here is large enough that the verdict does not turn on it; the 1.05 percent interaction finding does turn on it, and is carried as an observation rather than as a measured effect size.

Comparator p10 24190.653 p50 24925.940 p90 25329.826, spread p90/p10 1.047. Reshape 23754.278 / 25274.200 / 25731.941, spread 1.083. Launch configuration on top of the reshape 23936.839 / 25431.800 / 25941.011, spread 1.084. Launch configuration alone 22673.804 / 23841.094 / 24201.301, spread 1.067. The reshape family beats the comparator by 2.0 percent at the median and 2.4 percent at p90 while losing 1.05 percent at p10; its distribution is WIDER rather than shifted down. The launch configuration alone is slower at every quantile, so its refutation is about the treatment and not about a tail.

events.hypothesis: If the reshape removes launch-bound time on the common path, as its own source comment claims by replacing roughly 30 kernels per chunk forward and 28 backward across 16 chunks and 12 layers with one launch set per sparse layer, then the typical step gets faster, which is measured. A wider distribution on top of that means some steps pay a cost the comparator does not. Two shapes are distinguishable in the per-update series and imply opposite next actions. If the slow updates CLUSTER EARLY, they are a warm-up, autotune or allocator effect that the single warm step did not absorb, and a longer warm-up moves the reshape family from minus 1.05 percent to a p10 gain without changing one line of kernel code. If the slow updates are SPREAD THROUGHOUT, the batched path has a recurring stall the per-chunk loop did not have, and no warm-up recovers it.

events.refuted_if:
The criterion is frozen on the PER-UPDATE duration series of the launch-configuration-plus-reshape run against the comparator run, both already on disk, analysis-only, no card and no lease.
SUPPORTED if the slowest decile of updates in the treated run is concentrated in the first 10 percent of update indices, defined as strictly more than 40 percent of the slowest 102 updates falling in updates 1 through 102, which is four times the 25.5 expected under a uniform spread and cannot be produced by ordinary dispersion at this sample size.
REFUTED if 25 percent or fewer of the slowest 102 updates fall in that first tenth, which is at or below the uniform expectation and says the slow updates are not an early-run effect.
INCONCLUSIVE, explicitly and in advance, for the band between those two numbers, because a partial early concentration does not discriminate between a warm-up artifact and a recurring stall that merely happens to be denser early, and calling either one on that evidence would be choosing the answer rather than measuring it.
REFUTED, separately and on instrument grounds rather than on the hypothesis, if the per-update series cannot be read for both runs, or if either series does not carry 1,024 updates, or if the treated series does not reproduce the p10, p50 and p90 already reported in its own summary to within one part in ten thousand. That last clause is the one that matters: it is the check that the series I am reading is the series the summary was computed from, rather than some other field of the same shape, which is a defect this campaign has already paid for once.
