TWELVE of the slowest 102 updates fall in updates 1 through 102. That is 11.8 percent against a uniform expectation of 25.0 percent, so the slow updates are not merely un-clustered early, they are LESS likely early than chance, which is the opposite of the warm-up shape the hypothesis proposed. The SUPPORTED threshold was 40 percent and the INCONCLUSIVE band was 25 to 40 percent; the result is not near either boundary.

THE INSTRUMENT CLAUSE PASSED EXACTLY, AND IT IS THE CLAUSE THAT MATTERED. Both series carry exactly 1,024 captured updates after excluding the warm step, and each reproduces the p10, p50 and p90 its own summary reports: the treated series to 0.00e+00 relative deviation and the comparator series to 1.73e-08. The tolerance was one part in ten thousand. So the series read here is demonstrably the series each summary was computed from, rather than another field of the same shape -- a defect this campaign has paid for once, when a loss array was taken for step durations and produced a coherent table and a wrong verdict.

WHAT THIS CLOSES. The cheapest possible recovery of the reshape family is gone. A longer warm-up does not turn its plus 2.4 percent at p90 into a p10 gain, because the updates that drag p10 are distributed through the run rather than concentrated at its start. That route is closed by measurement rather than by argument, and it cost no card time.

events.hypothesis:
WHAT THE REFUTATION LEAVES STANDING, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING MEASURED TODAY. The reshape family is genuinely faster on the typical step: the launch configuration on top of the reshape beats the comparator by 2.0 percent at the median and 2.4 percent at p90, on a clean 1,024-update governed run, and reproduces its own summary quantiles exactly from the per-update series. It loses 1.05 percent at p10 purely because its distribution is WIDER, spread p90 over p10 of 1.084 against the comparator's 1.047. That is a dispersion result, not a slower step, and gate A scores the slow decile so the campaign reads it as a loss.

THE SUCCESSOR IS THE PERIODICITY OF THE SLOW UPDATES, AND IT NEEDS NO CARD. The slowest decile by tenth of the run is 12, 12, 16, 12, 10, 8, 8, 8, 7, 9 -- mildly front-heavy, nowhere near an early-run artifact, and consistent with a recurring event. The question this run cannot answer and the next one can: are the slow updates PERIODIC, and if so at what interval. A fixed stride points at something that fires every N updates -- a checkpoint or receipt write, an allocator release, an autotune recheck, a cache eviction -- and the rows already carry allocator bytes, cache eviction and transfer counters, staging seconds and routing digest seconds per update, so the mechanism is joinable to the slow set without any new instrumentation. events.hypothesis: The decoder validates every parameter as bf16, so the arm cannot change stored dtype and must cast at the single _linear funnel that every dense projection in CIADecoder passes through. The weight cast is cached on tensor identity AND version counter so an optimizer step invalidates it; the activation cast is paid per call. Under the premise that only the dense aten::mm class is reached -- not the Triton grouped-expert kernels, not the flash attention backward, not any non-arithmetic kernel -- a 1.40x on that class gives a step of about 154.8 ms and about 26,500 applied positions per second, 1.09x. The governed number is what decides whether the isolated rate survives capture, the optimizer step invalidating the weight cache every update, and the real activation stream.

The cause was located precisely: three extra memory passes on 484 calls per step, not the accumulator itself, which is why the register-side expert-kernel successor was a genuinely different treatment rather than the same idea relocated. That successor then returned the same 0.89x with no cast at all, so the two arms together close the accumulator-precision route at these shapes.

events.observation: The batched local router reshape scored p10 23,754.278 against a comparator of 24,190.653, 0.982x, and was ruled REFUTED on that number. But p50 25,274.200 and p90 25,731.941 are BOTH ABOVE the comparator. Positions per second p10 is the SLOW decile, so the reshape is faster on the typical step and worse on the slow ones: it moved the median up and the tail out. Gate A scores p10, so a treatment that improves the median and degrades the tail scores as a loss. Nothing in the refutation says WHY the tail moved, and the refutation is the whole reason the largest priced lever of the only above-bar arm is currently worth nothing.

events.hypothesis: Two mechanisms can produce a heavier slow decile with a lighter median, and they have opposite consequences. (1) A WARM-UP or allocator effect: the geometry runs a single warm step, and the batched path allocates a larger working set than the per-chunk loop, so the first tens of measured updates pay allocator growth and cache-miss cost the one warm step did not absorb. On this account the slow decile is a handful of EARLY updates, the treatment is fine, and the refutation is about the harness. (2) A genuine data-dependent cost: the batched GEMM is slower whenever some per-step property is unfavourable, spread uniformly through the run. On this account the refutation is about the reshape and a longer warm-up recovers nothing. The two are distinguished by WHERE in the run the slow decile sits, and both runs are already on disk. Supporting evidence for (1) that is not itself the test: this run's allocator peak_allocated is 8,897,773,568 bytes against the comparator's 7,110,785,536, and peak_reserved 14,508,097,536 against 12,197,036,032, so the batched path does carry a materially larger working set.

events.refuted_if:
REFUTED if fewer than 50 percent of the reshape run's slow-decile updates (the 10 percent of measured updates with the lowest applied positions per second) fall in the first 128 of the 1,024 measured updates, because a slow decile spread through the run is not a warm-up effect and a longer warm-up would recover nothing.
REFUTED if the comparator run's slow decile is concentrated in its own first 128 updates to within 0.85 of the reshape run's concentration, because a concentration both runs share is a property of the harness geometry rather than of the treatment, and curing it would not change the comparison.
REFUTED if either run yields fewer than 1,000 usable measured rows, or if the unreadable-row residual exceeds 0.05 of either population, because a decile computed over a population the instrument cannot fully read is not that population's decile.
REFUTED if the slow decile's median step wall time does not exceed the remaining updates' median by at least 5 percent, because a decile that is not actually slower has no excess to attribute and the ordering would be noise.

The second clause independently supports the refutation of the harness account rather than the treatment account: the comparator's own slow decile is at 0.86x of chance, so the reshape's mild 1.33x is not a shared harness property being blamed on the treatment either. events.hypothesis:
CORRECTION TO MY OWN RULING, AT ITS SOURCE. The verdict stands REFUTED on the frozen clause and does not move. What was wrong is the attribution sentence I appended to it: I wrote that roughly 0.117 s of the 0.129 s excess sits in NO measured CUDA phase and NO measured host phase. It sits in a host phase my instrument did not read. tail_decomp.py read cuda_phase_seconds for the forward term and context_exit_seconds for the host term, and never read the row's own host forward_seconds field. That is exactly the defect my own law names: a filter is a classifier, and a class it cannot express reads out as a zero rather than as a refusal, with the residual clause I did write covering unreadable ROWS and not unread FIELDS.

WHERE IT ACTUALLY IS. Slowest measured update, index 593: host forward_seconds 0.18930650, device cuda_phase forward 0.05734055, wall 0.31937610. Fastest, index 913: host forward_seconds 0.02785880, device cuda_phase forward 0.05085081, wall 0.15576690. events.observation: Positions per optimizer step is named in my own standing rules as the only lever that amortises fixed per-step cost, and the 40k budget file projected roughly 46,000 positions per second at 8 documents of 1,024 in bf16. It is also a learning-contract change and therefore the operator's decision, which is why it has never been measured. The projection that made it attractive was computed against a step with roughly 55 ms of fixed cost in a 226.5 ms step. The step is now 164.33 ms and its composition has never been re-read for this purpose.

events.hypothesis: A step is fixed cost plus cost proportional to positions. Raising documents per step multiplies only the proportional part, so positions per second rises toward an ASYMPTOTE equal to positions divided by the proportional cost alone, and that asymptote is reached from below however many documents are used. If the fixed fraction is small the asymptote is close to today's rate and the lever is worth almost nothing; if it is large the lever is worth a lot. The fixed terms are the optimizer step, which updates every parameter once per optimizer step regardless of how many positions fed it, and the host-side per-step work outside device time. The proportional terms are the forward and backward passes. So the lever's entire value is decided by the measured split, and the split is readable from the comparator run's own 1,024 rows without taking the card and without changing any contract.

events.refuted_if:
REFUTED if the asymptotic positions per second -- applied positions divided by the median proportional cost alone, with every fixed term removed -- is at or above 80,000, because then the contract lever alone reaches the terminal and it must be raised to the operator as the route rather than ruled out.
REFUTED if the fixed terms total more than 40 percent of the median step wall, because at that share the lever is a major multiplicative movement and belongs in the route set at its own bar rather than being closed here.
REFUTED if fewer than 1,000 measured rows are readable or the unreadable residual exceeds 0.05, because an asymptote computed over a population the instrument cannot fully read is not that population's asymptote.

events.because:
SUPPORTED. No refuting clause fired. Against clause one, the asymptote is 29,918.2 applied positions per second, which is 0.374 of the 80,000 terminal and 1.2003x of today's median 24,926.1, so the contract lever alone does not reach the terminal and is ruled out rather than raised as the route. Against clause two, the fixed terms are 0.02742 s of a 0.16433 s median step, a share of 0.1669 against the 0.40 ceiling, so the lever is not a major multiplicative movement. Against clause three, 1,024 rows were readable with a residual of 0.0010 against a 0.05 ceiling.

THE NUMBERS. Median step 0.16433 s at 4,096 applied positions. Device 0.15480 s, non-device 0.00952 s -- so 94.2 percent of this step is device time and the host is 5.8 percent of it. Fixed, meaning the optimizer and context-exit device term plus all non-device per-step work, is 0.02742 s. Proportional, meaning forward plus backward device time, is 0.13691 s. Eight documents gives 27,194.9 positions per second, 1.091x. Sixteen gives 28,491.6, 1.143x. The limit as documents per step goes to infinity is 29,918.2, 1.2003x, and no number of documents exceeds it.

WHY THE OLD PROJECTION WAS THREE TIMES TOO HIGH. The 40k budget file put roughly 46,000 positions per second at eight documents, computed against a step carrying about 55 ms of fixed cost in a 226.5 ms step, a fixed share near 0.24. The measured fixed share today is 0.1669 and the step is 164.33 ms. The campaign's own progress shrank both the step and the fixed fraction inside it, so the lever that amortises fixed cost got smaller as the step got faster. This is the standing law that an inherited factor must be repriced against the current measurement rather than carried, and it is the second lever in two days whose inherited price was wrong by more than a factor of two in the direction that made it attractive.

WHAT THIS DECIDES FOR THE 80,000 TERMINAL, stated as arithmetic over the split above with its premise separate. 80,000 positions per second at 4,096 positions is a 51.2 ms step; the fixed terms alone are 27.42 ms, which is 53.6 percent of that entire budget. So at today's geometry forward and backward would have to fall from 136.91 ms to 23.78 ms, a factor of 5.76. Raising documents per step dilutes the fixed terms and lowers that requirement: at eight documents the required factor on forward and backward is 3.65, at sixteen it is 3.09, and in the limit it is 2.674. THE PREMISE, kept separate from the arithmetic: that forward and backward scale linearly with documents at a held sequence length of 1,024, and that the optimizer and host terms do not scale at all. The optimizer half is structural. The linearity half is an assumption that holds for adding documents and would NOT hold for lengthening them, since attention is quadratic in sequence length.

SO THE TERMINAL'S REQUIREMENT IS NOW ONE NUMBER RATHER THAN THREE CONDITIONS: forward and backward device time must fall by a factor between 2.674 and 5.76 depending on documents per step, and every remaining route must act on that 136.91 ms. The contract lever is not a route to the terminal, but it is not worthless either -- it lowers the factor the real routes must deliver from 5.76 to 3.65 at eight documents, which is the difference between two levers stacking to enough and not. It remains a learning-contract change and therefore the operator's to rule; what has changed is that it is now correctly priced as an ENABLER of the arithmetic rather than as a route to the terminal, and it is not worth his attention on its own.

events.observation: The two Triton grouped-expert kernels, _rows and _weights, both declare a float32 accumulator and both call tl.dot with bf16 operands. On this consumer card the dense tensor rate halves when the accumulator is fp32, and bf16 has no reduced-accumulate mode, so an fp32 accumulator is the half-rate path by construction. The matched captured census over 6 steps measures _rows at 18,404.0 us per step over 72 calls and _weights at 10,891.0 us per step over 36 calls: 29,295.0 us of a 167,600 us step, which is the largest single class on the path that actually runs after the optimizer.

events.hypothesis: The dense-funnel version of this idea refused at 0.9002x an hour ago, and the reason it refused is the reason this is a different treatment rather than the same one moved elsewhere. That arm bought a rate on the GEMM alone and paid for it with an activation cast, a weight cast and an output cast back: three extra passes over memory per dense projection call, 484 of them per step. Treatment-selection law says a replacement's own cost is a separately owed measurement and is never inferred from the incumbent; I priced the rate there and never priced the casts, and the casts were larger than the gain. Inside a Triton kernel the operands are ALREADY IN REGISTERS when the convert happens. tl.dot's inputs are converted register-side and the accumulator is declared fp16, so the rate change and its cast are the same instruction and no extra memory pass exists to pay for. The ceiling is stated before authoring: a perfect doubling of 29,295.0 us saves 14,647.5 us, giving 1.0954x ALONE, which is BELOW the 1.5x bar, so this is authored as a STACK member of the rate condition and is never claimed as a route.

REFUTED if the reported p10 of applied positions per second is at or below 24,190.653, the campaign comparator on this source line, because a treatment that does not beat the number the campaign stands on buys nothing. REFUTED if the measurement does not complete 1,024 measured updates at 4 documents of 1,024 positions, because a p10 over fewer updates or a different geometry is not the statistic gate A names. REFUTED if execution-mode is anything other than resident-dynamic-capture or the capture does not actually occur, read back off the capture object rather than from the mode string. REFUTED if the run refuses on source identity. REFUTED if the measurement summary reports any skipped, failed or rolled-back update. This measures DURATION only and licenses nothing: an fp16 accumulator changes accumulation precision inside the dot and is a declared numerical treatment, so the no-worse-learning bar needs its own 64-update licence pair against the bf16 parent.

events.observation: The governed fp8 dense arm was measured twice and is slower both times: 0.8908x with the amax reduction replayed inside the captured graph at all 146 sites, and 0.8939x with the reduction proved out of the graph by a calibration quota of 1. The matched captured class census at head 20338ddc reads gemm_bf16 64698.5 us per step over 1353 kernels, which against the dimension-derived linear count of 8.8648 TF is 137 TF per second, or 83 percent of the published 165.2 TF per second dense bf16 rate. fp8 measured 1.836x at the dense funnel GEMM in isolation and torch scaled_mm reaches 287.8 TF per second at the expert down shape. So arithmetic on the measured class says fp8 should move the gemm class from 64698 toward roughly 32000 us per step, a saving near 32000 us on a 165757 us step, and the governed arm instead lost about 17000. That is a discrepancy near 47000 us per step, 28 percent of the step, and nothing in the campaign names where it goes.

events.hypothesis: Candidate mechanisms, each of which the matched census discriminates. ONE, the fp8 GEMMs never reach the large sites: min_gemm_elements 1500000 admitted 292 dispatches and left 384 below threshold, and if the large sites are the ones below threshold the class barely changes and there was never a saving to collect. TWO, the fp8 GEMMs do speed up and a cast population absorbs more than the gain: 146 distinct scale sites each performing a full bf16 read and fp8 write of their activation, in a step whose elementwise class is already at 1.07 of the published DRAM reference, so every added traversal is paid at the memory roof. THREE, the fp8 kernel is slower in situ than in isolation because the captured graph fixes a launch configuration chosen for a different shape. FOUR, the scaled GEMM falls back to a bf16 path at these shapes and the mode counters record selection rather than execution, which is the defect class that already invalidated one arm tonight. A matched captured class census with fp8 on, against the existing captured control at the same head and geometry, separates ONE from TWO by reading whether the gemm class fell, and sizes the absorbing class by reading which class rose.

TWO, the fp8 GEMMs do speed up and a cast population absorbs more than the gain: 146 distinct scale sites each performing a full bf16 read and fp8 write of their activation, in a step whose elementwise class is already at 1.07 of the published DRAM reference, so every added traversal is paid at the memory roof. THREE, the fp8 kernel is slower in situ than in isolation because the captured graph fixes a launch configuration chosen for a different shape. FOUR, the scaled GEMM falls back to a bf16 path at these shapes and the mode counters record selection rather than execution, which is the defect class that already invalidated one arm tonight. A matched captured class census with fp8 on, against the existing captured control at the same head and geometry, separates ONE from TWO by reading whether the gemm class fell, and sizes the absorbing class by reading which class rose.
hypotheses.criterion: REFUTED if the fp8 arm does not complete and export a captured trace whose cudaGraphLaunch count exceeds zero, because an eager trace describes a path the governed arm does not run. REFUTED if the combined GEMM device time in the fp8 arm, that is the gemm_bf16 class plus any fp8 GEMM class the classifier admits, is not at least 10000 us per step BELOW the control gemm_bf16 figure of 64698.5 us per step, because then the fp8 GEMMs did not speed up in situ, mechanism TWO is dead, and the loss is in the GEMMs themselves rather than in any wrapper. SUPPORTED if that combined GEMM device time is at least 10000 us per step below the control AND some other class rises by at least the amount needed to account for the regression, in which case the absorbing class is named by the census and is the thing to treat. INCONCLUSIVE only if the residual share of unclassified device time exceeds 0.10, which is the frozen ceiling, or if the two arms differ in any input other than the fp8 environment.
hypotheses.ruling: REFUTED on the criterion clause that the census must be able to read a fp8-executing arm. The run completed and CAPTURED genuinely: capture_occurred true, cudaGraphLaunch 26 per step, 7526 kernel events per step, wall 0.195 s per step against the control 0.196. It did NOT execute the treatment. The module receipt EMBER_FP8_RECEIPT names is absent, and kernel events per step are 7526 against the control 7526 exactly, so no fp8 GEMM and no cast population entered the graph. The probe constructs the decoder and calls it directly; the fp8 linear is installed by the governed RUNNER, not by model construction, so no fp8 environment reaches a dispatch site under this instrument. The combined GEMM device time therefore cannot be below the control by construction rather than by measurement, and the frozen clause refuses. This is an INSTRUMENT DEFECT reported as such and not a finding about the trace: no class comparison is published from it. The criterion is also defective and that is mine -- every governed dispatcher I wrote tonight carries an arm-did-EXECUTE clause reading the module count back off its own receipt, and I omitted it from this criterion while testing the very treatment whose prior arm needed it.
hypotheses.not_closed: Ruled. The loss is the per-call cast traffic, not the GEMM rate. Not closed: the same census has never been taken at a geometry where the cast is amortised over more positions.
hypotheses.closing: Closed by the operator freeze of issue 1945 at end of day 2026-09-21. No further dispatch is lawful, so this cycle is closed at its honest state rather than left open against a campaign that has stopped.

events.observation: Three numerical treatments measured governed on this source line tonight landed in a band 0.0063 wide against the 24,190.653 comparator: fp8 e4m3 at the dense funnel with calibration before capture 0.8939, fp16 operands and accumulator at the dense funnel 0.9002, fp16 accumulator inside the Triton expert kernels 0.8942. Three unrelated mechanisms, three modules, three kernel populations, one answer. Censusing every governed p10 of the evening against the head that produced it shows the band is the TAIL of a monotone decline across the branch commit sequence, not a property of any treatment: 23,936.8 at the grouped num_stages 2 num_warps 8 commit, 23,754.3 at the batched local router commit, 22,673.8 at the commit that REVERTS that router, 21,775.6 at the uncached fp16 weight cast commit, 21,631.0 at the launch-site counter commit, 21,624.1 at the resident fp8 scale commit. The revert alone spans 23,936.8 to 22,673.8, and no treatment was under test in a revert. The 24,190.653 comparator itself appears as the output of none of these heads, so no arm measured tonight has a bf16 control at its own head.

events.hypothesis: If the ten percent belonged to the treatments then a bf16 control at the treatment head would return the comparator, because the treatments are the only thing the arms changed relative to that control. If instead source changes landing on this branch through the evening cost the throughput, then a bf16 control at the treatment head returns about 0.90 of the comparator with no treatment present at all, and every effect estimate scored against 24,190.653 tonight is the sum of a treatment effect and an unmeasured source-line effect of similar magnitude and opposite sign to what the campaign concluded. The null arm separates them: the fp8 module is installed at every dense site and its element threshold is raised above every weight in the model, so it loads, reads its environment and admits nothing. The arithmetic executed is bit-for-bit the bf16 path, so the arm carries no numerical change and licenses nothing, while every other input including the head, the geometry, the data plan, the seed, the resident expert set, the optimizer and the capture mode is identical to the treatment arms. What it measures is the configuration, which is exactly the term the three treatment numbers cannot see.

events.refuted_if: The arm must EXECUTE INERTLY and prove it: the module receipt at the custody root must be present with an fp8 dispatch count of exactly zero and a below-threshold count above zero. An absent receipt REFUTES the run, because the module never loaded and the arm is then the bf16 path with no control property at all, which is the defect that invalidated this evening matched census. A receipt with any nonzero fp8 count REFUTES it too, because the threshold did not hold and this is a treatment arm wearing the control name. REFUTED if the measurement does not complete 1,024 measured updates at 4 documents of 1,024 positions, or if execution mode is anything other than resident-dynamic-capture with capture read back off the capture object, or if the run refuses on source identity, or if any update is reported skipped, failed or rolled back. Given a valid run the verdict on the hypothesis is: SUPPORTED if the reported p10 is at or below 22,500 applied positions per second, that is within about 0.93 of the comparator, because then the configuration alone carries most of the ten percent and no treatment measured tonight was scored against a comparable control. REFUTED if the reported p10 is at or above 23,700, that is within about 0.98 of the comparator, because then the configuration is sound and the three treatments each genuinely cost their measured amount. INCONCLUSIVE strictly between 22,500 and 23,700, where the control is neither the comparator nor the treatment level and the number is published as the new matched control with no effect claim attached. The thresholds are set here before the run and are not adjusted after it.

events.hypothesis:
WHAT THE SUPPORTED VERDICT DOES NOT CLOSE, named while the reasoning is fresh so a later reader cannot print more from this cycle than it earned.

It does NOT close the tensor-rate route, and it does not open it either. The three arms are ~1.03x gains rather than ~0.90x losses, which corrects their SIGN and leaves them far below the 1.5x bar that governs arm selection. No row may now cite fp8 or fp16 accumulation as REFUTED on this campaign without citing the control first, and no row may cite them as promising on the strength of 1.03x.

The null arm installs the module and admits nothing, so it controls for presence and not for absence: a no-module bf16 arm at the same head was never run. If importing the module or evaluating its per-site branch costs time even when it admits nothing, then this control is itself depressed and all three ratios are overstated. That is one run and it is the clean control.

It does NOT explain the largest live gap on the board. fp16 accumulation measured 1.4031x in isolation at the model's own dense shapes, with the cast amortized and with no amax, no scale and no scaling metadata, and 1.0403x end to end governed. A 1.4031x lever on a class the matched captured table puts at 51,466 us of a 157,260 us union should read near 1.10x at the step, not 1.04x. The three candidates are MIN_OUTPUT_WIDTH=512 excluding most of the admitted sites, the dense funnel being a smaller share of the governed step than the class table suggests, and the backend flag not taking effect inside the captured replay. A site census under the governed arm distinguishes them and needs no card, so it runs first.

It does NOT carry matched-run variation, this run included. One run, no repeat. It does NOT isolate any mechanism, because the four arms compared sit at three different heads (ddb83395, 1b41c406, 004f3150). Each ratio is arm-versus-control, confounded with whatever else its head carries. A stacked arm at ONE head is what would isolate the combination, and stacking is what the campaign's own law requires of treatments rather than measuring them one at a time.

AND THE WARM-UP ROUTE IS CLOSED BY MEASUREMENT IN THE SAME HOUR, which matters because it was the other half of this cycle's motivation. The per-update records show 0 of 1024 phase=measured rows uncaptured -- the graph is constructed in the warm step, correctly -- and p10 is FLAT at ~20,932 after dropping 0, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 and 256 measured updates. The 6.36% p50-to-p10 gap is distributed through the run rather than sitting in a head, so raising warm_steps would not move the governed p10 and gate A's "warmed" wording is already satisfied by these runs. My own docstring had asserted the opposite from a glance at two adjacent raw lines; the instrument refuted it on its first run and the false sentence is withdrawn at its source in the file.

SUCCESSOR, in cost order: the fp16 site census under the governed arm (free, explains the 1.4031-to-1.0403 gap and sizes how much of the largest lever is actually being realized), then the no-module clean control at the same head (one run, decides whether this control is itself depressed), then a stacked arm at one head carrying every non-contending gain measured tonight.

events.observation:
The card is idle and the largest row of the factor-dominant table has never been touched by any arm: the kernel-count regime of the non-GEMM path, about 10,850 elementwise/copy plus about 1,000 softmax/reduce/norm launches per step at a mean 4.5 us, whose cost is proportional to kernel COUNT rather than to bytes, measured at 61.7 ms with about 55 ms of excess and 33 percent of the 4x. Every treatment dispatched on this campaign has instead acted on tensor RATE inside the GEMM classes, and the matched captured class table says why that cannot reach the terminal: gemm_bf16 is 65,811.5 us and gemm_grouped_expert 29,295.0 us of a 157,260.6 us device union, and dense GEMM proper is 51,466 us against a terminal budget of 51,200 us per step.

THE OBSERVATION THAT MAKES A GEOMETRY RUN THE CHEAPEST WAY TO ACT ON THAT ROW. Every governed measurement on this campaign has run at documents_per_step 4, sequence_length 1024, that is 4,096 positions per invocation. The non-GEMM launch population is driven by the number of LAYERS and CHUNKS, not by the number of positions in each chunk, so raising documents per invocation processes more positions through the same launch count. That is mechanically the same relief the fusion treatment would buy on row 1, obtained by changing one field of geometry.json rather than by authoring a kernel, and it costs one run.

WHAT IS ALREADY ON RECORD AND WHAT IS NOT. The registry row batch-lever-gradient-accumulation is PROPOSED, not IN_FLIGHT, and its own not_closed line reads that its ceiling is UNMEASURED and that "no number follows from it until one is measured". That row is also about the ACCUMULATION lever, which amortises the optimizer class alone at 17,358.1 us. This is the INVOCATION lever, which the same row explicitly calls distinct, and no measurement of either exists on this campaign at any geometry other than 4 documents.

events.hypothesis:
MECHANISM. Device time per invocation splits into a term that scales with positions and a term that does not. The scaling term is the arithmetic: dense projection GEMMs, expert GEMMs and attention all grow linearly in positions at fixed model dimensions, and they already run near this card's bf16 roofline, so nothing about geometry makes them cheaper per position. The FIXED term is everything whose cost is set by the number of kernel launches rather than by the bytes each launch touches: about 10,850 elementwise and copy launches plus about 1,000 softmax, reduce and norm launches per step at a mean 4.5 us, the optimizer block at 17,358.1 us which runs once per optimizer step whatever the batch, the step boundary, and the host dispatch behind them. Raising documents per invocation multiplies the scaling term and leaves the fixed term where it is, so applied positions per second rises toward the asymptote (F+S)/S times the current rate, where F is the fixed term and S the scaling term at four documents.

WHAT THAT PREDICTS, AND THE PREDICTION IS A RANGE RATHER THAN A POINT BECAUSE F IS NOT DIRECTLY MEASURED. From the matched captured class table at 157,260.6 us of device union: the classes that are unambiguously arithmetic are gemm_bf16 65,811.5, gemm_grouped_expert 29,295.0 and softmax 4,712.7, totalling 99,819.2 us. The classes that are unambiguously fixed or launch-bound are optimizer 17,358.1, triton_fused 6,767.9, index_scatter_gather 2,240.6, reduce 2,205.9, cat_copy 1,958.2, sort 842.8, other 411.8, gemm_other 338.3 and loss 24.2, totalling 32,147.8 us. The elementwise class at 34,296.4 us straddles the split: its 3,533 launches are a launch-count population, but each launch's work does scale with positions, so some of it is fixed cost and some is not. Taking elementwise as wholly scaling gives an asymptote of 1.24x; taking it as wholly fixed gives 1.66x. That range, not a single figure, is what the run is dispatched to resolve, and the resolution is the point: the two ends differ by whether row 1 of the factor table is reachable by geometry at all.

WHY MEASURE IT RATHER THAN COMPUTE IT. Three terms in the arithmetic above are unmeasurable from the class table. The elementwise split is one. The second is whether raising positions eight-fold keeps every kernel in the same efficiency regime: the fp16 work earlier tonight found two real M and K asymmetries on this card, where m=4096 k=1024 n=1024 reached 1.631x while m=2048 k=1024 n=1024 reached 1.005x, so a geometry change can move a contraction into or out of a favourable regime and the sign is not predictable from shape alone. events.observation: The prior delayed-scaling fp8 arm returned a real governed p10 and a module receipt reading quantize_resident 0 against quantize_calibrating 584 over 146 distinct scale sites. 584 divided by 146 is exactly 4.0 and the calibration quota defaults to 4, so every site reached the quota and none passed it. The Python counters cannot run inside a captured replay, so a count of 4 per site counts calls made while the graph was being constructed: the branch the capture recorded was the CALIBRATING branch, which performs the amax reduction the arm existed to remove, and all 1,024 replays then executed that reduction. The arm measured its own calibration path under the treatment name.

events.hypothesis: The quota is already an environment variable, EMBER_FP8_CALIBRATION_CALLS, defaulting to 4. Setting it to 1 makes the first call calibrate and every later call, including the one the capture records, take the resident branch. No source change. Mechanism: with the scale held resident the per-call amax reduction over each operand disappears from the captured graph, leaving only the quantize multiply, so the fp8 GEMM rate measured in isolation at this model own expert shapes, 1.74x to 1.84x of bf16, becomes reachable at the dense funnel. CEILING STATED BEFORE AUTHORING, against the matched captured class table: the two GEMM classes are 95,106 us of a 157,260.6 us device union. Granting the measured 1.8x on both and leaving attention in bf16 gives 51,466 over 1.8 plus 14,345 plus 29,295 over 1.8, which is 59,212 us of arithmetic, a step of 121,366 us, a factor of 1.296x and about 27,130 applied positions per second. That is BELOW the 1.5x arm bar, so this is dispatched as member ONE of the four-member stack and never as a movement event.

The class table predicted 1.296x, which in milliseconds is 35.894 ms of GEMM saving; the arm delivered 10.283 ms, 28.65 percent of it. events.hypothesis: Exactly two candidate causes, with opposite next actions. CAUSE 1: the fp8 GEMM rate at the dense funnel shapes is far below the rate measured at the expert shapes, in which case the dense funnel is closed as a route and fp8 remaining value is at the grouped expert sites, 29295 us per step. CAUSE 2: the per-call quantize multiply and its writes cost back most of what the GEMM saves, in which case member ONE is recoverable by folding the quantize into the producing kernel. A governed run cannot separate them because it measures only their sum. An isolated three-arm shape probe separates them without taking a governed window: bf16 mm, the fp8 GEMM alone with operands pre-quantized and scales resident, and the same GEMM plus the per-call activation quantize the wrapper actually pays.

events.refuted_if: THREE ARMS at each of the 14 certified dense shapes, same operands, same repeat count, frozen before authoring at WARMUP 10 and REPEATS 40. Arm A bf16 mm. Arm B fp8 e4m3 _scaled_mm with operands ALREADY quantized and scales resident -- the GEMM rate alone. Arm C arm B plus the per-call activation quantize exactly as the wrapper does it. CLAUSE 1, EXECUTION BEFORE ANY RATIO: e4m3 carries 3 mantissa bits against bf16 7, so arm B must show relative error against a float64 reference at least 3.0 times arm A at EVERY measured shape. If it does not, the instrument REFUSES and prints no ratio, because a _scaled_mm call that silently fell back produces a ratio near 1.00 and would REFUTE a hypothesis the instrument never tested. CLAUSE 2, RESIDUAL IS A NUMBER: any certified shape the probe cannot run is counted and named, and above a frozen 0.30 residual share the whole report REFUSES. CLAUSE 3, CAUSE 1 IS SUPPORTED if the geometric-mean B/A isolated rate ratio is below 1.40. CLAUSE 4, CAUSE 2 IS SUPPORTED if B/A is at or above 1.40 AND the geometric-mean C/A ratio is below 1.15. CLAUSE 5, BOTH REFUTED if B/A is at or above 1.40 and C/A is also at or above 1.40, because then neither named cause explains the governed shortfall and the cause is elsewhere -- a real finding, and the probe names no replacement candidate because these numbers do not contain one. CLAUSE 6, INCONCLUSIVE in any remaining combination, stated rather than resolved. CLAUSE 7, WHAT NO OUTCOME LICENSES: every number here is an isolated-shape rate ratio. None is a step ceiling, a factor on the governed number, or a distance to 80000, and no ratio here may be composed with device time or with the 25.6 ms governed shortfall that motivated the probe. events.hypothesis: The shipped grouped kernel _rows runs at 135-152 TF/s, below this card bf16 dense rate, so it was not obvious it would reach the fp8 tensor rate either: a kernel limited by something other than its tensor rate gains nothing from fp8 operands. If the cast and the e4m3 write themselves are what cost, removing the amax changes little and fp8 is closed on both classes.

events.observation: The non-GEMM decomposition of the matched captured trace shows the SAME operation running on two different kernels at very different per-launch cost. CUDAFunctor_add over bfloat16 runs 1006 times per step at 8.142 us on the VECTORIZED kernel, and 73.5 times per step at 78.114 us on the NON-VECTORIZED elementwise_kernel -- 9.6x the per-launch cost for the same functor and the same dtype. The direct copy shows the same split: 119.5 launches at 33.839 us on the non-vectorized kernel and 57 launches at 21.787 us on the unrolled one. Together those three symbols are 11.0 ms of a 66.9 ms non-GEMM step.

events.hypothesis: PyTorch selects vectorized_elementwise_kernel only when every operand is contiguous and suitably aligned, and falls back to elementwise_kernel or unrolled_elementwise_kernel otherwise. So a 9.6x per-launch gap between two kernels compiled from the same functor is a LAYOUT selection, not an arithmetic cost: the fallback reads and writes the same bytes with uncoalesced access. If that is what is happening, the fallback launches will show non-contiguous Input Strides in the cpu_op that launched them, and their achieved bandwidth will be a small fraction of this card DRAM rate while the vectorized launches sit near it. A layout repair is BIT-EXACT -- making a tensor contiguous changes no value -- so unlike every other candidate on this campaign it is not a declared numerical treatment and needs no licence pair.

events.refuted_if: REFUTED if the non-vectorised launches turn out to be CONTIGUOUS, or if their achieved bandwidth is within 2x of the vectorised launches achieved bandwidth on the same operand bytes. Either outcome means the per-launch gap is explained by SIZE rather than by layout, the launches are already near the bandwidth they can reach, and there is no layout repair to author. The instrument REFUSES and rules nothing if fewer than 80 percent of the non-vectorised launches can be joined to a cpu_op carrying Input Strides, since an unjoined launch is a launch whose layout was not read.
events.supported_if: SUPPORTED if the majority of non-vectorised launch time is joined to cpu_ops whose Input Strides are non-contiguous for at least one operand AND their achieved bandwidth is below half the vectorised launches achieved bandwidth. That combination is a layout slow-path with a bit-exact repair available.

events.because: The frozen criterion was REFUTED if the vectorised-to-fallback achieved bandwidth ratio is inside 2x. Four rows, all at expert weight shapes, all with a TRANSPOSED second operand: add_ over [3072,1024] with strides [1024,1] and [1,3072] costs 3985.8 us per step over 48.3 launches at 152.6 GB/s; copy_ at the same shapes 2310.7 us at 259.6 GB/s; add_ over [1024,3072] 1744.0 us at 174.4 GB/s; copy_ at those shapes 1273.5 us at 235.5 GB/s. The successor is registered as a per-row cycle over exactly those four rows with a population that excludes graph-annotation joins by construction, and it is NOT this cycle re-run with a wider bound.

Two bit-exact repairs exist: materialise the incoming view contiguously before adding, or hold the gradient buffer in the incoming layout so no operand is ever strided. Neither is obviously faster than what runs today, because the first ADDS a full strided read plus a contiguous write, and that is exactly the kind of assumption this campaign keeps paying for.
hypotheses.criterion: REFUTED if the better of the two repair arms beats the strided add by less than 1.30x on its WORST of the two expert weight shapes. The instrument REFUSES and rules nothing if any arm is not bit-identical to the strided result, since a repair that changes a value is not a layout repair.
hypotheses.criterion_supported_if: SUPPORTED if the better repair arm beats the strided add by 1.30x or more on its worst shape, with every arm bit-identical.
hypotheses.instrument: seat record: is_a_contiguous_repair_faster_than_the_strided_add.py
hypotheses.ruling: Frozen criterion: SUPPORTED if the better repair arm beats the strided add by 1.30x or more on its worst shape with every arm bit-identical. Arm C -- holding the gradient buffer in the INCOMING layout so neither operand is ever strided -- runs 12.09 us against 47.97 at 3072x1024 and 10.95 against 47.15 at 1024x3072: 3.969x on its worst shape, bit-identical by torch.equal on both. The naive .contiguous() arm is SLOWER than what runs today, 0.966x and 0.915x, which is the assumption the criterion existed to catch. Separately and not part of this ruling: the fused AdamW class moves about 16.9 GB of optimizer state in 16.1 ms, which is roughly 1050 GB/s and therefore already at this card DRAM roofline, so the optimizer cannot be made faster and can only be overlapped.
hypotheses.not_closed: What is NOT closed and is the next thing to measure before any model byte changes: arm C requires param.grad to be allocated in the transposed physical layout, and the fused AdamW multi_tensor_apply kernel then reads a non-contiguous grad. Nothing here measured whether that kernel accepts such a grad at the same rate or falls off its fast path, and a repair that saves 7 ms at the accumulation while costing more than that in the optimizer is a net loss. That measurement is the gate on authoring, not the 3.969x. Also not closed: the aten::copy_ rows at the same shapes, 3584 us per step, were not arms in this probe and are assumed to share the cure without evidence.
hypotheses.closing: layout repair supported in isolation; the optimizer-tolerance gate is registered as the authoring precondition.

events.hypothesis: The non-GEMM launch population is driven by layers and chunks rather than by positions per chunk: the matched captured census reads 5664.8 non-GEMM launches per step at a mean 11.80 us, and the fused AdamW multi_tensor_apply alone is 16126.5 us per step over 21.3 launches at the DRAM roofline, a cost paid once per optimizer step whatever the step contains. events.observation: The captured trace prices four AccumulateGrad rows at 9,314 us/step at 152-260 GB/s, about 5.9 percent of the 157,260.6 us device union and a member of the 75,303 us non-arithmetic half. The predecessor cycle ruled both consumer-side repairs dead: a naive .contiguous() is a NET LOSS at both expert shapes (0.966x and 0.915x) and holding the grad buffer in the incoming layout is 3.969x/4.304x but foreclosed because fused AdamW refuses a layout mismatch. Its own not_closed list names the producer-side store as untouched and names the coalescing question as unmeasured.

events.hypothesis: _grouped_swiglu reaches the Triton grouped kernel through gate/up/down.transpose(1,2), and _weights allocates db contiguous in that TRANSPOSED shape. The resident Parameter owns the other layout, so autograd hands AccumulateGrad a strided operand and the add runs far below roofline. Storing db in the PARAMETER layout instead removes the strided operand entirely. It only pays if the store stays coalesced, which is why the arm transposes the accumulator in registers via tl.trans rather than swapping store strides: a bare stride swap makes K the fast axis of the destination while the store still walks N, which is uncoalesced by construction.

events.refuted_if: the tl.trans arm runs below 1/1.15 of the incumbent store time at G=25 K=1024 N=3072 M=4096, i.e. the kernel gives back more than a 1.15 factor to buy the layout
events.supported_if: the tl.trans arm runs at or above 1/1.15 of the incumbent store time AND is bit-identical to the incumbent under torch.equal on the transposed view, so the 9,314 us/step accumulate can be removed at the producer without paying for it inside the kernel

events.because: The frozen criterion refutes if the tl.trans arm runs below 1/1.15 of the incumbent store time at G=25 K=1024 N=3072 M=4096. It runs at 1.007x (222.35 us against 223.91) and is bit-identical under torch.equal on the transposed view, so it clears the bound with room. The honest reading is narrower than a win: all three arms sit within 0.7 percent of each other (223.91 / 223.30 / 222.35), inside any noise floor this campaign has measured. What is established is that the STORE LAYOUT IS FREE in this kernel, not that tl.trans is faster -- the dot loop dominates and the store is not where the time is. That is exactly what the repair needs: the 9,314 us/step transposed accumulate can be removed at the producer without the kernel paying for it.

events.observation: The matched captured trace partitions a 157,260.6 us device step into 81,957.6 us of arithmetic (52.1%) and 75,303.0 us of everything else (47.9%). Six consecutive governed arms all acted on the arithmetic half and every one measured at or below 1.0x, which is arithmetically bounded: the dominant backward GEMM already runs at 151 TF/s against a 165.2 TF/s published bf16 peak. The non-arithmetic half has never carried a governed arm. Two of its members are authored and bit-exact: the batched local-router reshape (kernel-count regime) and the parameter-layout expert-gradient store (the 9,314 us/step strided AccumulateGrad, whose store layout measured 1.007x of the incumbent and bit-identical).

events.hypothesis: Mechanism, stated per member so the stack is not one undifferentiated claim. Member 1, the reshape: the per-chunk local-router loop issues roughly 30 forward and 28 backward launches per chunk over 16 chunks and 12 sparse layers, each below launch latency, so the cost is proportional to launch COUNT rather than to bytes; issuing one launch set per layer and one batched GEMM in place of one vector GEMM per chunk removes those launches. Member 2, the layout: _grouped_swiglu reaches the kernel through gate/up/down.transpose(1,2), so _weights allocates db contiguous in the TRANSPOSED shape while the resident Parameter owns the other layout, and AccumulateGrad therefore takes a strided operand priced at 9,314 us/step. Storing through tl.trans(acc) in the parameter layout makes that operand contiguous; the store itself is bit-identical and costs 1.007x of the incumbent in isolation. The two act on disjoint milliseconds -- launch count in the sparse router path, and one accumulate in the expert backward -- so their ceilings do not contend.

events.refuted_if: p10 <= 24,646.9 applied positions/s, which is 1.0189x of the 24,190.653 comparator and therefore inside the 1.9 percent matched-null noise floor measured on this source line. A stack that removes a 9,314 us/step accumulate plus a per-chunk launch regime and cannot be distinguished from its own control has not acted on the non-arithmetic half, whatever the class census predicted, and the REFUTATION is of THIS pair of members and not of the 75,303 us half they sit in.
events.supported_if: p10 >= 25,715.5 applied positions/s, which is 1.063x -- the layout member alone removing 9,314 us of a 157,260.6 us device step, with the reshape credited nothing. Anything strictly between the two bounds is INCONCLUSIVE at one run per arm and names which member is unattributable.

events.observation: The stacked non-GEMM arm ruled REFUTED at 0.9728x. Reading its per-update series shows the refutation is not a uniformly slower step: median duration 0.16504 s against the comparator's 0.16433 s, 0.43% apart, and p10 durations 0.16183 against 0.16171, which is 0.07% apart. The entire rate loss lives in the high-duration tail, because the governed p10 of the RATE is the 90th percentile of DURATION. The arm has 72 of 1025 steps more than 10% above its own median, spread evenly across all ten deciles at about seven per decile; the comparator has 3, all in its first two deciles. So the arm introduced a recurring stall of roughly twice the median step about every fourteen steps, and produced no median gain. Separately, the custody carries NO execution assertion for either member: the frozen manifest's env block carries EMBER_PARAM_LAYOUT_DB=1, which records that the flag reached the worker, and the source's own counter -- _expert_counts['param_layout_db'] incremented at the launch site -- is written only to EMBER_FP16_EXPERTS_RECEIPT, which this dispatch never set. The docstring beside that counter says in as many words that a manifest variable records the flag arriving and only a count records that the branch which ran is the branch Triton compiled.

events.hypothesis: A refuted arm and an INERT arm are indistinguishable from the receipt I collected, and the two readings imply opposite next actions. events.hypothesis: THE STACKED ARM for route half (a), which is the only work on the board above the 1.5x bar. The 2x2 is complete and no further replicate of this member is owed; another one would be the sequence of small true results the operator has ruled against. The member joins three siblings in ONE arm measured once at the governed 1,024-update geometry: the elementwise fusion priced at 14,964.5 us/step after its unreachable-isolated deduction, which is a kernel-COUNT saving over passes of memory rather than a faster kernel; the fp32 log-softmax over [4096,32768] at 4,135.9 us in two launches; and the optimizer at 17,452.7 us, which sits at about 1050 GB/s against a ~1008 GB/s DRAM rate and therefore CANNOT be made faster -- it can only be overlapped. FIRST SIBLING ALREADY LOCATED BY SOURCE READ, not by proposal: cia_step_runner.py line 1170 computes cross_entropy(logits.float(), targets), and the .float() materialises the entire [4096,32768] logit tensor in fp32 before the loss ever runs. Folding the widening into the reduction -- log_softmax(logits, dim=-1, dtype=torch.float32) followed by nll_loss -- removes that materialising copy, and it is BIT-EXACT rather than merely close, because bf16 to fp32 is an exact widening and the softmax arithmetic therefore sees identical values. WHAT NOTHING IN THIS THREAD TOUCHES: attention, whose backward carries 9,479.3 us at 0.313-0.388 of reference and is the largest single arithmetic lever on the step, with a cuDNN backend that is reachable, runtime-disabled and has never been dispatched. And route half (b), the 37.5% cut in arithmetic per position, which is an active-parameters-per-token learning-contract call and is the operator's to rule, not mine to take.

events.because: Frozen criterion: REFUTED IF fused_widen is again 0. It is again 0, alongside param_layout_db 144 and 1,024 completed updates at governed p10 25,173.900. The prediction failed and the verdict stands. But the criterion's attached INTERPRETATION -- that a second zero means the clobber was not the mechanism and member two is genuinely inert -- is now disproved by evidence the criterion did not anticipate, and I am recording that rather than reading the clause literally. The frozen dispatch manifest shows the worker is launched as cia_step_runner.py --daemon-run --live --hidden-helper, and lines 1404-1436 of that file show it then re-execs ITSELF as cia_step_runner.py --worker binding under a hidden helper and verifies the ancestry. The two counter mtimes in this run are 1.2 seconds apart where they were 8 seconds apart before, which is the controller exiting right behind its child instead of the orchestrator exiting much later. The cure is the per-key MAX merge already authored and preserved at seat record: loss-widen-receipt-merge-20260922.patch; no environment change can fix a clobber by a process that is supposed to have the variable.

events.hypothesis: The instrument has never had its own noise measured. A matched pair is only an instrument if its within-pair variation under NO treatment is small compared with the effects it is used to rule on; otherwise every verdict it has issued is a reading of scheduler and clock variation wearing a treatment name. The candidate mechanisms for the swing are clock and power state drift across a window, allocator layout differing between process launches, and the profiler window itself landing differently, and none of them is a property of any treatment. The distinction that matters is BETWEEN-pair against WITHIN-pair: the two arms of a pair run back to back in one window and one process family, so they may be far tighter than two pairs four minutes apart, and if they are the instrument is sound and only cross-pair comparison is forbidden.

events.refuted_if: The two null arms differ by 300 us per step or more. The instrument then cannot distinguish either measured effect from its own noise, BOTH prior verdicts lose their timing basis, and no matched-pair number may be quoted as a ceiling or a size until the pair is replicated enough times to put a real interval around it. NOTE the asymmetry deliberately: a REFUTED here costs me two results I already published internally, which is exactly why the threshold is frozen before the run and will not be widened afterwards.
events.supported_if: The two null arms differ by LESS THAN 300 us per step. events.hypothesis: The successor is an INSTRUMENT REPAIR, not a treatment. events.observation: Two SoftMax kernels in the captured census carry 4641 us/step in the canonical class table over ONE call each, implying an operand near 2 GB. That is the native loss head materialising full-width fp32 logits: vocab_size 32768 times 4096 positions at 4 bytes is 537 MB, read and written several times across log_softmax and its backward. The streamed head cce-document-v1 is already implemented in cia_step_runner capture_loss_kwargs, already vendored with a digest manifest at src/ember/model/streamed_loss_vendor.json, and required_sources already folds streamed_sources(identity). Nothing was missing but a preparer flag.

events.hypothesis: The streamed head computes the cross entropy against the embedding weight in tiles, so the full-width logits tensor is never materialised. It removes the log_softmax class and the fp32 logits traffic that feeds it, and it removes embedding.weight from segment 12 captured params under head_output=hidden. It is a DECLARED NUMERICAL TREATMENT -- a different reduction order for the same loss -- so it licenses duration only and gate C needs its own 64-update pair. It stacks with fp8 at the dense chokepoint because the two act on disjoint milliseconds: fp8 moves projection GEMM arithmetic, the streamed head removes head-side elementwise and softmax traffic.

It happened to agree with the truth here because the experiment-plan validator independently proved the selection, but the clause as written would have passed an inert head. events.hypothesis: Write the step as F + S*(d/4) where F is the per-update cost independent of positions and S the part that scales with them. Then the speedup from doubling documents is 2(F+S)/(F+2S) and the ceiling of the whole batch lever as d grows is (F+S)/S, which is reached when every fixed cost has been amortised to nothing. A single measurement at d=8 therefore SOLVES for F: k = 2*STEP/(2*STEP - F), so F = 2*STEP*(1 - 1/k). At k=1.05 the fixed share is 9.5 percent and the lever ceiling is 28,684 positions/s; at k=1.20 it is 33.3 percent and 38,928; at k=1.40 it is 57.1 percent and 60,555. The probe is four minutes and it bounds the entire lever rather than sampling it.

events.hypothesis: Mechanism: e4m3 doubles the tensor-core rate, so a GEMM of duration T becomes about T/2, while entering fp8 costs one read-plus-write bandwidth pass over each operand that is not already cached. The weight cache is exact -- keyed on parameter identity and _version, so the optimizers in-place write invalidates it and a weight is quantized once per optimizer step -- which leaves only the activation and the gradient to pay for, at about 15.12 us for a [4096,1024] bf16 tensor, itself already bandwidth-bound and not inefficient. Net value per call is therefore T/2 minus about 15 us. At T of 118.4 and 107.4 us the net is strongly positive; at the 32.7 us per call GEMMs elsewhere in the step it is not, which is the same arithmetic that explains why the grouped rows arm lost. FLOP arithmetic makes this the load-bearing route rather than one option among several: 10.10 TF per step against this cards 165.2 TF/s dense bf16 rate is a 61.1 ms floor, and the 80,000 terminal needs 53.2 ms, so no bf16-only stack of treatments reaches it and the tensor-rate levers are where the route has to run.

events.because: The criterion reads "REFUTED if the treatment arms total per-step kernel-duration SUM ... does not fall by at least 4,000 us against the reference arm". It fell 1,547.7 us: reference 161,683.6 to treatment 160,135.9. Both preconditions held -- both arms captured, treatment dispatch 726 fp8 with 0 full_precision and 0 not_selected -- so this is a verdict on the treatment and not a refusal on an inert arm. The criterion is not loosened after seeing it fail. TWO THINGS THE CLASS DELTAS SAY THAT THE NET DOES NOT. First, the mechanism executed exactly as designed and at a magnitude no plausible noise reaches: bf16 GEMM fell 24,680.4 us/step and fp8 GEMM appeared at 16,336.3, with quantize at 3,310.7. The conversion happened; it simply did not pay. Second, the reason it did not pay is NOT the quantize cost I had modelled. 1,298 quantize_resident calls cost 3,310.7 us, which is 2.55 us per call against the 15.12 us per call my isolated probe reported -- a sixth, and another receipt for an isolated shape probe overpredicting. The cost that ate the gain is the fp8 GEMM itself: it replaced 24,680.4 us of bf16 with 16,336.3 us, a 1.51x speedup where the tensor rate offers 2x. At a true 2x the fp8 term would be 12,340 us and the net would be about 9,000 us, which clears the threshold with room. So roughly 4,000 us per step is sitting in fp8 GEMM inefficiency, and that is an implementation question about _scaled_mm shapes and layout, not a numerics question and not a route question.

The conversion works and is large; the net is small only because the fp8 GEMM achieves 1.51x where the tensor rate offers 2x. The successor hypothesis is that the fp8 GEMM at the document-reduction projection shapes is leaving about 4,000 us/step on the table, testable by timing _scaled_mm against the bf16 GEMM at exactly those operand shapes and layouts and comparing the ratio to 2 -- with the standing caveat that an isolated shape probe may SELECT but may not produce a ceiling. (2) The quantize cost model. 2.55 us/call in situ against 15.12 us/call isolated retires the cost model I built this weeks fp8 reasoning on; every fp8 ceiling that subtracted a 15 us quantize pass understated the route and needs re-deriving. (3) THE INSTRUMENTS OWN NOISE FLOOR, which is an admitted debt of mine. I built the per-class SUM instrument precisely to escape the UNION instruments measured 3,000 us floor, then set this criterions threshold above the UNION floor without ever null-pairing the SUM instrument. My own law says an instruments noise floor is measured before its first verdict, at the sample size the verdict is made at. It was not. This does not change the verdict -- 1,547.7 is below 4,000 either way and the criterion stands as frozen -- but it means the 1,547.7 figure itself is unresolved rather than a small real gain, and the next pair on this instrument runs a reference-versus-reference null first. hypotheses.explanation: Mechanism: e4m3 doubles the tensor-core rate, so a GEMM of duration T becomes about T/2, while entering fp8 costs one read-plus-write bandwidth pass over each operand that is not already cached. The weight cache is exact -- keyed on parameter identity and _version, so the optimizers in-place write invalidates it and a weight is quantized once per optimizer step -- which leaves only the activation and the gradient to pay for, at about 15.12 us for a [4096,1024] bf16 tensor, itself already bandwidth-bound and not inefficient. Net value per call is therefore T/2 minus about 15 us. At T of 118.4 and 107.4 us the net is strongly positive; at the 32.7 us per call GEMMs elsewhere in the step it is not, which is the same arithmetic that explains why the grouped rows arm lost. FLOP arithmetic makes this the load-bearing route rather than one option among several: 10.10 TF per step against this cards 165.2 TF/s dense bf16 rate is a 61.1 ms floor, and the 80,000 terminal needs 53.2 ms, so no bf16-only stack of treatments reaches it and the tensor-rate levers are where the route has to run.

events.observation: The matched pair just closed measured the fp8 quantize class at 3,310.7 us/step over 1,298 quantize_resident calls, which is 2.55 us per call. The isolated shape probe that sized this weeks fp8 reasoning reported 15.12 us per call. That is a factor of six, in the direction that makes fp8 cheaper than every ceiling on this campaign has assumed, and it is the third receipted instance of an isolated probe overpredicting an in-situ cost. Two consequences follow. First, todays grouped-fp8 governed refutation -- 24,849.318 against a frozen 25,952.319, an arm that went the WRONG way -- was explained by 960 quantize calls at 15.12 us costing about 14,515 us against an ideal GEMM saving near 4,710 us. At 2.55 us per call that cost is about 2,448 us, and the explanation inverts: the arm should have been roughly neutral to positive, so its refutation is now unexplained rather than understood. Second, the two fp8 sites are independent flags, EMBER_FP8_LINEAR for the document-reduction projections and EMBER_FP8_GROUPED for the expert path, and they act on different classes: the pair just run moved GEMM bf16 by 24,680.4 us with the grouped expert custom class untouched at about 28,000 us/step. Nothing on this campaign has measured them stacked. Separately, and owed: I built the per-class SUM instrument to escape the UNION instruments 3,000 us noise floor and have never null-paired the SUM instrument, so I do not know what a 1,547.7 us reading on it means.

events.hypothesis: MECHANISM. Quantization reads a bf16 operand and writes an fp8 one; at [4096,1024] that is 8 MB read plus 4 MB written and the operation is bandwidth-bound. The isolated probe measured it on an idle card with nothing else resident and nothing contending, which is the configuration in which a bandwidth-bound operator looks WORST relative to its share of a busy step, because in situ it overlaps and shares cache with the seven thousand kernels around it. That is why the isolated figure runs high, and it is the same direction all three prior overpredictions ran. So the in-situ 2.55 us per call is the figure that governs selection and the 15.12 us figure governs nothing. THE STACKED PREDICTION. The two flags gate disjoint call sites and therefore disjoint kernel classes: EMBER_FP8_LINEAR converts the document-reduction projections, which live in the GEMM bf16 class, and EMBER_FP8_GROUPED converts the expert path, which lives in the grouped expert custom class at about 28,000 us/step and was measurably untouched by the pair just run. Two treatments acting on disjoint classes do not contend for the same milliseconds, so their effects add rather than overlap -- but they DO share the quantize path and the scale state, and an activation quantized for one site may or may not be reused by the other, so the quantize class is where any interaction will show. That makes the stack worth measuring as a stack rather than inferring from two singles, which is what my own law requires anyway. THE NULL ARM. A reference-versus-reference pair, same flags unset in both, prices what this instrument reports when nothing changed. It also prices the three classes the treatment does not touch -- grouped expert, optimizer, elementwise -- which moved by +2,035.8, +924.1 and +863.6 in the pair just run and are either arm contention or instrument wobble. Running the null in the SAME window as the treatment, at the same sample size, is the only thing that licenses reading any delta on this instrument.

events.refuted_if: THREE ARMS IN ONE WINDOW, one head, one geometry, one instrumentation configuration, separate processes, in this order: null_a with both flags unset, null_b with both flags unset, treatment with EMBER_FP8_LINEAR=1 and EMBER_FP8_GROUPED=1. FLOOR, measured here rather than assumed: F = the absolute difference between null_a and null_b total per-step kernel-duration SUMs. REFUTED unless ALL THREE of the following hold. (1) The treatment total falls against the MEAN of the two null arms by at least max(6,000 us, 3F). The 3F term is what makes this a reading rather than a wobble and it is why the null runs in the same window at the same sample size; the 6,000 us floor is absolute and is set above the 4,000 us the single-site pair failed to clear, because a stack claiming both sites must beat what one site already could not. The floor this cycle measured -- 7,352.2 us/step, 4.7% -- reorders the whole campaign, and the reordering is written up in seat record: issue1945-where-the-factor-actually-is-20260922.md. Two arithmetic facts from the same reference arm. First, the card is at 38.7% of its dense bf16 roofline, so fp8 at the dense sites is necessary. Set dense GEMM to zero and the terminal is still missed by 1.86x. Every treatment this campaign has run acts on the 39.8% that is dense GEMM and not one has acted on the 60.2% that is not. (1) The fp8 route at the dense sites, which is measured to work and to achieve 1.39x where the tensor rate offers 2x; the gap between 16,174 us and the ~11,240 a true 2x implies is an implementation question about operand shapes and layout and is worth about 4,900 us/step, which is BELOW this instruments floor and therefore needs a governed run to see. (2) The grouped fp8 pairing: 5,929.7 us removed from the custom expert kernels against 6,499.5 us of new triton overhead. Both terms are near the floor so the pairing is unresolved, but it is the first mechanism ever offered for this mornings grouped-fp8 governed refutation that is not the quantize cost model retired an hour ago. (3) Whether any treatment below 7,350 us/step can be adjudicated at all without a governed 1,024-update arm -- the answer appears to be no, and that alone explains a sequence of sensible arms producing no movement. (4) Whether the 7,352.2 us floor is itself stable, since it rests on ONE null pair; a second null pair would say whether the floor is 7,350 or merely at least 7,350.

events.observation: The site attribution of today clean reference arm resolves the entire optimizer class to ONE site, _fused_adamw_ at 16218.6 us/step over 21.3 calls, and arithmetic over 702M trainable parameters at 22 bytes per parameter puts its DRAM bandwidth floor at 15321 us. Measured over floor is 1.06x, so that class is already at 94 percent of the card bandwidth and no kernel change can reduce it. It is 17544 us of a step whose entire 80000-positions budget is 51200 us, which is 34 percent of the terminal budget in one immovable class. The attribution also names cross-entropy forward and backward at 4122.7 us over 4 calls, which is likewise once per optimizer step rather than per position. Both are FIXED per optimizer step and do not scale with positions.

events.hypothesis: Per-step cost splits into a term proportional to positions processed and a term paid once per optimizer step. The optimizer is the clearest fixed term by construction: fused AdamW touches every trainable parameter exactly once per step whatever the batch, so its bytes are independent of positions. Cross-entropy over 4 calls and the per-step begin/end work are candidates for the same class. If that split is real, raising positions per optimizer step from 4096 to N divides every fixed term per position by N/4096 while leaving the proportional terms per position unchanged. The instrument can test this with no code change: the captured census takes the document count as an environment variable, so a docs=4 arm and a docs=16 arm differ only in positions per step, and the discriminator is us per POSITION rather than us per step. A purely proportional step shows equal us per position in both arms. A step with a real fixed term shows the docs=16 arm strictly lower, by an amount that predicts the fixed population without needing to identify which sites it contains.

events.refuted_if: Three captured arms in one window, same head, same flags: null_a at docs=4, null_b at docs=4, treatment at docs=N where N is 16 or, if that exhausts memory, 8. The compared quantity is total in-window kernel duration divided by POSITIONS PROCESSED, us per position, never us per step, because the arms process different position counts by construction. F is the measured null-pair difference expressed in us per position. The docs=4 baseline is 38.549 us per position. Predicted us per position at the treatment N assumes a fixed population of 21667 us per optimizer step: 34.58 at N=16, 35.90 at N=8. REFUTED if the treatment arm us per position is not lower than the null_a arm by MORE than max(F, 1.80); REFUTED if that drop is less than half the predicted drop for the N actually run, namely 1.98 at N=16 or 1.32 at N=8; REFUTED if either null arm fails or the two nulls differ by more than 15 percent of the baseline; REFUTED if the treatment arm does not report capture_occurred true. A drop that clears both thresholds SUPPORTS a real fixed-cost population and licenses sizing it, and nothing more: it is device time on a captured census, it is not a governed number, and it makes no claim about learning under a changed positions-per-optimizer-step contract.

events.because: The frozen criterion required a treatment arm at docs=16 or docs=8 reporting capture_occurred true; no treatment arm executed a single kernel, so not one clause is evaluable. INCONCLUSIVE because the run did not discriminate, never because an answer was unwelcome: the hypothesis that a fixed per-optimizer-step population exists is exactly as open as before the window, and the two null arms that DID complete measured only the floor. What the run established decisively is that the instrument cannot test it in the direction I chose. events.hypothesis: THE CONFOUND, which the totals cannot resolve and which bounds every use of this result. Two different things produce a cost that fails to halve when positions halve. FIXED work is set by the parameter count or by the step itself and is collected by paying it less often. SUBLINEAR work is proportional in principle but runs inefficiently at the smaller size, and amortization collects NONE of it, because at depth N you run N full-size passes and pay the full-size cost each time. A two-point comparison of TOTALS cannot tell them apart, so 72333.4 us is an UPPER BOUND on the collectible population and must never be quoted as the lever size. Per class they do separate, and the class table is the real finding. Ratios of docs2 to docs4 cost: optimizer 1.078 and grouped_rows 0.919 are FIXED-like; gemm_dense 0.617, elementwise 0.667, grouped_weights 0.611, triton 0.675, other 0.606, gather 0.557 are scaling, though none reaches the ideal 0.5, so sublinearity is present everywhere. The optimizer at 1.078 is genuinely fixed and its 20964 us is collectible. The finding I did not expect is grouped_rows at 0.919: the grouped expert kernel costs almost the same for half the tokens, which is the signature of per-step EXPERT WEIGHT STREAMING whose bytes are set by the expert population rather than by token count. NOT CLOSED: whether grouped_rows is fixed or merely badly underutilised, which decides whether it is collectible at all and which needs a third point at docs=1 or 3 rather than another two-point fit. NOT CLOSED: the amortization ceiling itself. The proportional floor is 24.05 us per position, so perfect amortization of everything reaches 41580 positions per second and NO FURTHER -- 1.64x of today, the largest single lever measured on this campaign, and still not the terminal on its own. ALSO NOT CLOSED, and it changes which mechanism is right: gradient accumulation does not collect weight streaming, because each pass re-reads the weights. What collects it is more tokens sharing ONE weight read, and tokens per forward are capped at 4096 by a declared guard at ember_v0_residency.py line 713 and three sibling guards in ember_v0_decoder.py. Raising that constant is a context-length change to a canonical architecture and is not a throughput trick. The lawful shape is a BATCH dimension of independent 4096-position contexts, which multiplies tokens per weight read while changing no per-sequence semantics. That is the successor worth authoring, and it is large.
